title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄序
嘉靖甲子例大比天下士先
是禮官徵各省應試生數太
濫主司斂才類忽二三塲不
得績實學爲
國家用上其議
制曰可須布天下廵按山東監察
===
御史楊〔標〕祗承
新命東公肅度視昔加慎〔伯涵〕學
識寡陋濫典試事亦惴惴焉
以不稱
聖天子求賢德意是懼竊聞之曆
元相循而一周甲子爲世首
而萬物之炳著于離明也必
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄序

嘉靖甲子，例大比天下士。先是，禮官徵各省應試生數太濫，主司斂才類忽二三塲，不得績實學爲國家用，上其議。制曰：「可。」須布天下。廵按山東監察御史楊〔標〕祗承新命，東公肅度，視昔加慎。〔伯涵〕學識寡陋，濫典試事，亦惴惴焉，以不稱聖天子求賢德意是懼。竊聞之，曆元相循，而一周甲子爲世首，而萬物之炳著于離明也，必
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

In the jiazi year of Jiajing (1564), the scholars of the realm underwent the regular triennial examination. Previously, the ritual officials had ascertained that the numbers of students sitting the examinations in the provinces were excessive. Those presiding over the selection of talent commonly neglected the second and third sessions, making it impossible to assess genuine learning for the service of the state [?]. They submitted their deliberations. The Emperor's decree reads: “Approved.” This was to be promulgated throughout the realm. Yang Biao 楊標, Investigating Censor on巡按 duty in Shandong, reverently received the new command. He conducted affairs in the east with solemn restraint [?], exercising greater care than before. I, Bohan 伯涵, possess scant learning and limited understanding, yet have undeservedly been entrusted with directing the examination. I too am apprehensive, fearing that I may fail to fulfill the sage Son of Heaven's virtuous intention of seeking worthy men.

I have heard that calendrical epochs succeed one another, and that a complete sixty-year cycle marks the beginning of an age. For all things to become brilliantly manifest in the brightness of Li, they must …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
自震出靑兗之疆列震位爲
東藩自黃帝生于壽丘以土
德王天下於八年甲子創曆
紀正朔首開文運啓虞舜繼
堯立極以肇道統至春秋秀
鍾孔子講道洙泗述六經爲
萬世道德師說者謂
岱海實嶽瀆所宗故應運洩靈
爲天下倡自古然矣我
太祖高皇帝汛掃胡氛復三五綱
常於洪武甲子定科舉期式
是爲開泰之基今
聖天子
中興弘化闡
punctuated: 自震出。靑兗之疆，列震位，爲東藩。自黃帝生于壽丘，以土德王天下，於八年甲子創曆紀正朔，首開文運，啓虞舜繼堯立極，以肇道統。至春秋，秀鍾孔子，講道洙泗，述六經，爲萬世道德師。說者謂岱海實嶽瀆所宗，故應運洩靈，爲天下倡，自古然矣。我太祖高皇帝汛掃胡氛，復三五綱常，於洪武甲子定科舉期式，是爲開泰之基。今聖天子中興弘化，闡
translation_en: …emerge from Zhen. The lands of Qing and Yan occupy the position of Zhen, the eastern trigram, and form the eastern bulwark. The Yellow Emperor was born at Shouqiu and ruled All under Heaven through the virtue of Earth. In the eighth year of his reign, a jiazi year, he established the calendar and fixed the beginning of the year, first inaugurating the flourishing of culture. This paved the way for Shun of Yu to succeed Yao and establish the supreme standard, initiating the transmission of the Way. By the Spring and Autumn period, the region’s finest qualities were concentrated in Confucius, who taught the Way beside the Zhu and Si rivers and transmitted the Six Classics, becoming the teacher of the Way and virtue for all generations. Commentators say that Mount Dai and the sea are indeed revered as foremost among the sacred mountains and waterways. Thus, responding to the cycles of destiny, they manifest their spiritual potency and take the lead for All under Heaven; this has been so since antiquity. Our Emperor Taizu Gao swept away the baleful influence of the northern peoples and restored the cardinal relationships and constant virtues of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors. In the jiazi year of the Hongwu reign, he fixed the schedule and regulations of the civil-service examinations, laying the foundation for an era of peace and prosperity. Now our sagely Son of Heaven, reviving the dynasty and extending its transforming influence, elucidates…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
敬一微旨揭示膠庠使天下咸
知崇信孔子以隆黃帝堯舜
盛治已非一日之積矣迺甲
子首元恭遇
萬壽誕辰特
命撫臣肅祀
岱海與論秀期值御史於巳卯
日試士畢率諸執事北向稽
===
首祝曰願
聖天子萬壽無疆永立民極又祝
曰願得名世者出是科佐
聖天子永保民致治時祥光纏
北極而旁燭乎鎖闈莫不忭躍倍
恒品合詞頌曰異哉此
punctuated: 敬一微旨，揭示膠庠，使天下咸知崇信孔子，以隆黃帝堯舜盛治，已非一日之積矣。迺甲子首元，恭遇萬壽誕辰，特命撫臣肅祀岱海。與論秀期值，御史於巳卯日試士畢，率諸執事北向稽首祝曰：「願聖天子萬壽無疆，永立民極！」又祝曰：「願得名世者出是科，佐聖天子永保民致治！」時祥光纏北極，而旁燭乎鎖闈，莫不忭躍倍恒品，合詞頌曰：「異哉，此
translation_en:
…the subtle meaning of reverent single-mindedness (jingyi), displaying it in the schools so that all under Heaven would know to revere and trust Confucius, thereby bringing to greater fullness the flourishing governance of the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun. This achievement had already accumulated over far more than a single day.

Then, in the jiazi year that begins the cycle, we reverently encountered His Majesty’s birthday celebration. He specially commanded the Grand Coordinator to perform solemn sacrifices to Mount Tai and the sea. This coincided with the season for selecting outstanding scholars. On the simao day [?], after examining the candidates, the Censor led the officials serving at the examination in facing north and bowing their heads to the ground. He prayed: “May the Sagely Son of Heaven enjoy boundless longevity and forever establish the highest standard for the people!” He further prayed: “May men renowned in their age emerge from this examination to assist the Sagely Son of Heaven in forever protecting the people and achieving good governance!”

At that moment, auspicious radiance encircled the northern celestial pole and shone outward upon the sealed examination compound. Everyone leaped for joy with far more than ordinary fervor, joining their voices in praise: “Wondrous is this…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
岱海昭格明徵
聖壽同天則登崇才賢茂翊
曆運不在茲乎於是〔伯涵〕謹率
諸同事披所試士千九百卷
卽其言以究其心必三塲稱
詔格乃入選遴
制取七十有五人雖言人人殊各
===
抒所自得而稱文舉類動準
六經至於析忠邪之分審王
霸之歸盡人情物理之變貫
仁義而賤詐力慨然見於自
靖者甚正蓋一變至道之幾
於是乎在而所以講隆其會
者不徒爲一方文物之盛而
punctuated: 岱海昭格明徵，聖壽同天，則登崇才賢，茂翊曆運，不在茲乎？」於是〔伯涵〕謹率諸同事，披所試士千九百卷，卽其言以究其心，必三塲稱詔格，乃入選遴。制取七十有五人。雖言人人殊，各抒所自得，而稱文舉類，動準六經。至於析忠邪之分，審王霸之歸，盡人情物理之變，貫仁義而賤詐力，慨然見於自靖者甚正。蓋一變至道之幾，於是乎在。而所以講隆其會者，不徒爲一方文物之盛而
translation_en:
…the manifest proof of the numinous response of Mount Tai and the sea! May His Majesty’s longevity equal Heaven’s! Is it not here that worthy and talented men will be raised to distinction, abundantly assisting the fortunes of the dynasty?” Thereupon, [Bohan] respectfully led his colleagues in examining the 1,900 sets of papers submitted by the candidates. We investigated their minds through their words, admitting them to selection only if their work in all three sessions met the standards prescribed by imperial edict. The prescribed quota was seventy-five men.

Although their words differed from person to person, each expressing what he had grasped for himself, their citations of texts and adducing of analogous cases consistently took the Six Classics as their standard. In distinguishing loyalty from wickedness, discerning the ultimate tendencies of true kingship and hegemonic rule, and fully exploring the variations of human feelings and the principles of things, they held fast to benevolence and righteousness and disdained deceit and force. The convictions ardently expressed in determining their own moral stance were thoroughly upright. Here, indeed, lay the possibility of reaching the Way through a single transformation. And the purpose of fostering and bringing distinction to this gathering was not merely to enhance the cultural flourishing of one region…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
已昔人論星野山東當山河
兩界之會爲陽氣所始升而
天下亦往往於大䄅長紳之
見占世太平我
明再闢洪濛貞元旺氣泓蓄二
百餘年而昌發於
今日重新甲子猶之氣轉洪鈞
===
肇化機於東方也凡士之得
於甄陶者卽遐壤下邑莫不
乘時思奮如蟄斯震而况於
景軒庭步堯墟履舜井洋洋
於洙泗間獨無眞才以應其
求耶雖然産才者地也惟才
也斯成地之能顯才者時也
punctuated:
已。昔人論星野，山東當山河兩界之會，爲陽氣所始升，而天下亦往往於大䄅長紳之見，占世太平。我明再闢洪濛，貞元旺氣泓蓄二百餘年，而昌發於今日，重新甲子，猶之氣轉洪鈞，肇化機於東方也。
凡士之得於甄陶者，卽遐壤下邑，莫不乘時思奮，如蟄斯震。而况於景軒庭、步堯墟、履舜井，洋洋於洙泗間，獨無眞才以應其求耶？雖然，産才者地也，惟才也斯成地之能；顯才者時也。
translation_en:
…alone. When men of former times discussed the celestial divisions corresponding to terrestrial regions, they placed Shandong at the meeting of the two domains of mountains and rivers, where yang energy first rises. People throughout the realm also often divined an age of great peace from the appearance of men in grand ceremonial robes and long sashes [?]. Our Ming dynasty opened the primordial cosmos anew. The flourishing energy of cyclical renewal accumulated in deep abundance for more than two hundred years and now issues forth in splendor. With the commencement of a new jiazi cycle, it is as though vital energy were turning the great potter’s wheel of creation, setting the workings of transformation in motion in the east.
All scholars who have benefited from cultivation and training, even in remote regions and humble towns, seek to seize the moment and exert themselves, stirring like hibernating creatures at the thunder. How much more so those who revere the court of Xuanyuan, walk among the remains of Yao’s dwelling, tread the ground around Shun’s well, and move at ease between the Zhu and Si rivers! Could they alone lack true talent to answer the demand? Nevertheless, it is the land that produces talent, and only through talent is the land’s capacity fulfilled; it is the age that brings talent to prominence…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
惟才也斯翊時之運
國家以文斂才求其措之躬行
騰茂實而策殊勳微獨以文
而已夫
泰山滄海之高深夫人類能言
之至於歷談不謬無逾東人
士者以嘗登涉焉而窮其勝
===
也茲七十有五人者去聖人
之居甚近以所誦法者先資
其言旣見錄於有司使行不
足以成信是徒談
岱海而未得其高深何貴於東
人士乎矧遭逢
聖神在上是復睹黃帝堯舜而親
punctuated:
惟才也斯翊時之運。國家以文斂才，求其措之躬行，騰茂實而策殊勳，微獨以文而已。夫泰山滄海之高深，夫人類能言之；至於歷談不謬，無逾東人士者，以嘗登涉焉而窮其勝也。
茲七十有五人者，去聖人之居甚近，以所誦法者先資其言，旣見錄於有司，使行不足以成信，是徒談岱海而未得其高深，何貴於東人士乎？矧遭逢聖神在上，是復睹黃帝堯舜而親
translation_en:
…Only through talent can the course of the age be furthered. The state gathers talent through literary composition, seeking men who will put their learning into personal practice, produce abundant substantive achievements, and establish exceptional merit—not merely excel in writing. As for the height of Mount Tai and the depth of the vast sea, almost anyone can speak of them. Yet in recounting their particulars without error, none surpass the men of Shandong, for they have climbed the mountain and traversed the sea, fully exploring their wonders.
These seventy-five men live very near the dwelling place of the Sage. What they recite and take as their model has already furnished the substance of their words, and they have now been selected by the responsible officials. If their conduct does not suffice to substantiate those words, they merely speak of Mount Tai and the sea without grasping their height and depth. What, then, would make the men of Shandong worthy of esteem? Moreover, they have encountered an age when a sagely and divinely wise sovereign reigns above: this is to behold the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun once again, and personally…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
爲之臣不特如孔子之嘉
其道已也而忍於負之乎諸
士誠知所際之不偶也由此
服官政隨其職之所在以先
聖所垂訓者竭忠事
聖天子務期利
社稷福生民明徵於事功如
泰山之爲高滄海之爲深以成
能而翊運俾天下稱才焉則
有以仰副乎
===
聖神壽考作人之化而衍泰道於
無疆者自齊魯是科始矣其
於甲子重新之會不永有
厤光也哉錄成以
punctuated:
爲之臣，不特如孔子之嘉其道已也，而忍於負之乎？諸士誠知所際之不偶也，由此服官政，隨其職之所在，以先聖所垂訓者竭忠事聖天子，務期利社稷、福生民，明徵於事功，如泰山之爲高、滄海之爲深，以成能而翊運，俾天下稱才焉，則有以仰副乎聖神壽考作人之化，而衍泰道於無疆者，自齊魯是科始矣。其於甲子重新之會，不永有厤光也哉？
錄成，以
translation_en:
…to serve as his subjects, rather than merely, like Confucius, admiring his Way: could they bear to fail him? If these gentlemen truly understand that the opportunity they have encountered is no ordinary one, then, upon entering official service, each should, wherever his duties lie, follow the teachings handed down by the former sages and serve the sage Son of Heaven with utmost loyalty. They must strive to benefit the altars of soil and grain and bring blessings to the people, demonstrating this plainly through their achievements—as lofty as Mount Tai and as deep as the vast sea. By perfecting their abilities and assisting the fortunes of the dynasty, they will cause all under Heaven to acclaim their talent. Thus they will be able to fulfill the expectations of the sage and divine sovereign’s enduring work of nurturing worthy men. The boundless extension of the Way of harmonious prosperity will then begin with this examination cohort from Qi and Lu. At this moment when the sixty-year cycle begins anew with the jiazi year, will this not bring lasting glory to the calendar [?]?
Upon completion of the record, …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
廥〔伯涵〕循職事敬次具論之盛
爲
明時頌而因以朂諸士云是舉
也先巡按御史高〔應芳〕夙奉
令典禮聘儒臣校文則〔伯涵〕
暨教諭劉〔田〕吳〔世忠〕施〔陽得〕
學正皇甫〔鍾岳〕教諭錢〔用商〕
===
楊〔邦憲〕區〔次顏〕陳〔思育〕提調
則左布政使李〔多〕右布政使
李〔磐〕監試則副使胡〔湧〕秦〔鈁〕
遴士則提學副使曹〔三暘〕是
時巡撫戶部右侍郎兼右僉
都御史鮑〔象賢〕綏懷保釐適
弘文敎總理河道工部右侍
punctuated: 廥〔伯涵〕循職事，敬次具論之盛，爲明時頌，而因以朂諸士云。是舉也，先巡按御史高〔應芳〕夙奉令典，禮聘儒臣；校文則〔伯涵〕暨教諭劉〔田〕、吳〔世忠〕、施〔陽得〕、學正皇甫〔鍾岳〕、教諭錢〔用商〕、楊〔邦憲〕、區〔次顏〕、陳〔思育〕。提調則左布政使李〔多〕、右布政使李〔磐〕；監試則副使胡〔湧〕、秦〔鈁〕；遴士則提學副使曹〔三暘〕。是時，巡撫戶部右侍郎兼右僉都御史鮑〔象賢〕綏懷保釐，適弘文敎；總理河道工部右侍
translation_en:
…Gui Bohan 廥伯涵 [?], in discharge of his official duties, respectfully set forth the splendor of the collected discussions [?], composing a tribute to this enlightened age and thereby exhorting the scholars.
For this examination, the former Regional Inspector, Censor Gao Yingfang, had early acted upon the prescribed regulations and courteously invited scholarly officials. Those who evaluated the compositions were Bohan, together with County School Instructors Liu Tian, Wu Shizhong, and Shi Yangde; Department School Director Huangfu Zhongyue; and County School Instructors Qian Yongshang, Yang Bangxian, Ou Ciyan, and Chen Siyu. The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Duo and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Pan. The officials supervising the examination were Surveillance Vice Commissioners Hu Yong and Qin Fang. The official responsible for selecting scholars was Education Intendant Cao Sanyang, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner.
At this time, Grand Coordinator Bao Xiangxian, Right Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, fostered peace and good government, further extending literary education. The Director-General of River Conservancy, Right Vice Minister of Works…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
郎兼右僉都御史陳〔堯 宣〕猷
樹軌表正士習巡鹽監察御
史馮〔善 印〕馬監察御史吳〔守〕
振揚風教士知所奮戶部主
事張〔喬 檜〕張〔允 濟〕王〔同 贊〕工
部署郎中事員外郎姜〔國 華〕
員外郎皮〔豹〕主事游〔季 勳〕葉
===
〔以 蕃〕行人司行人蒙〔詔〕孫〔振〕
〔宗〕有事茲土樂觀盛典左參
政李〔瑜〕左參議徐〔岱〕副使劉
〔衍 祚〕鄧〔棟〕張〔任〕僉事薛〔一 鶚〕
黃〔正 色〕申〔佐〕署都指揮僉事
曹〔勳〕陸〔淇〕防範于外均與有
勞右參政史〔直 臣〕僉事張〔問〕
punctuated: 郎兼右僉都御史陳〔堯 宣〕猷樹軌表，正士習；巡鹽監察御史馮〔善 印〕、馬監察御史吳〔守〕振揚風教，士知所奮。戶部主事張〔喬 檜〕、張〔允 濟〕、王〔同 贊〕，工部署郎中事員外郎姜〔國 華〕、員外郎皮〔豹〕、主事游〔季 勳〕、葉〔以 蕃〕，行人司行人蒙〔詔〕、孫〔振〕〔宗〕，有事茲土，樂觀盛典。左參政李〔瑜〕、左參議徐〔岱〕、副使劉〔衍 祚〕、鄧〔棟〕、張〔任〕、僉事薛〔一 鶚〕、黃〔正 色〕、申〔佐〕、署都指揮僉事曹〔勳〕、陸〔淇〕，防範于外，均與有勞。右參政史〔直 臣〕、僉事張〔問〕
translation_en:
…Vice Minister and Concurrent Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Chen Yaoxuan established exemplary standards through his measures and rectified the habits of the scholars. Feng Shanyin [?], Investigating Censor inspecting the salt administration, and Wu Shou, Investigating Censor overseeing horses [?], promoted moral instruction, and the scholars knew to exert themselves.

Zhang Qiaogui, Zhang Yunji, and Wang Tongzan were Bureau Secretaries in the Ministry of Revenue. Jiang Guohua was a Vice Director acting as Director in the Ministry of Works; Pi Bao was a Vice Director, and You Jixun and Ye Yifan were Bureau Secretaries in that ministry. Meng Zhao and Sun Zhenzong were Messengers in the Office of Transmission. They had official business in this region and gladly witnessed the grand ceremony.

Li Yu was Left Administration Vice Commissioner, and Xu Dai was Left Administration Assistant Commissioner. Liu Yanzuo, Deng Dong, and Zhang Ren were Surveillance Vice Commissioners. Xue Yi’e, Huang Zhengse, and Shen Zuo were Surveillance Assistant Commissioners. Cao Xun and Lu Qi were Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners. They maintained security outside the examination precincts, and all contributed their efforts.

Right Administration Vice Commissioner Shi Zhichen and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Zhang Wen…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
〔仁〕署都指揮僉事王〔倫〕以入
賀行右叅議秦〔宗道〕以部稅行
右叅議張〔邦土〕副使陳〔絳羅〕
〔塤〕王〔惟寧〕黃〔中〕余〔朝卿〕僉事
黃〔九成〕董〔世彥〕張〔守中〕以列
銜名事一方例得備書云
河南開封府扶溝縣儒學教
諭胡〔伯涵〕謹序
punctuated:
〔仁〕、署都指揮僉事王〔倫〕以入賀行，右叅議秦〔宗道〕以部稅行。右叅議張〔邦土〕、副使陳〔絳羅〕〔塤〕、王〔惟寧〕、黃〔中〕、余〔朝卿〕、僉事黃〔九成〕、董〔世彥〕、張〔守中〕，以列銜名，事一方，例得備書云。
河南開封府扶溝縣儒學教諭胡〔伯涵〕謹序。
translation_en:
…[Ren, completing the preceding name, Zhang Wenren], and Wang Lun, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, had departed to offer congratulations at court. Qin Zongdao, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner, had departed to supervise tax collection. Zhang Bangtu, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner; Chen Jiang and Luo Xun [?], Surveillance Vice Commissioners, together with Wang Weining, Huang Zhong, and Yu Chaoqing; and Huang Jiucheng, Dong Shiyan, and Zhang Shouzhong, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners—all held the listed offices and served in this region, and thus, according to established practice, their names could be recorded in full here.
Preface respectfully written by Hu Bohan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Fugou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:

監臨官

浙江金華府蘭谿縣儒學教諭施陽得〔復徵，直隸無錫縣人，己酉貢士〕。
直隸鳳陽府壽州儒學學正皇甫鍾嶽〔汝鎮，河南睢州人，己酉貢士〕。

translation_en:
Shandong Provincial Examination, Forty-third Year of Jiajing (1564)

Supervising Official
Yang Biao, Investigating Censor assigned to patrol Shandong, had the courtesy name Tingzhan and was from Qingjiang County, Jiangxi. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingchen year.

Proctors
Li Duo, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong, had the courtesy name Zhiqing and was from Yangcheng County, Shanxi. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinchou year.
Li Pan, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shandong, had the courtesy name Bogu and was from Gushi County, Henan. He was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Examination Monitors
Hu Yong, Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Ruyuan and was from Xingzi County, Jiangxi. He was a metropolitan graduate of the guichou year.
Qin Fang, Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Minghe and was from Cixi County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the gengxu year.

Examiners
Hu Bohan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Fugou County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Yisha [?] and was from Guangji County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the bingwu year.
Liu Tian, Instructor at the Confucian School of Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Chaofu and was from Changzhou County, Zhili. He was a tribute scholar of the renzi year.

Associate Examiners
Wu Shizhong, Instructor at the Confucian School of Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Yijie and was from She County, Zhili. He was a tribute scholar of the renzi year.
Shi Yangde, Instructor at the Confucian School of Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Fuzheng and was from Wuxi County, Zhili. He was a tribute scholar of the jiyou year.
Huangfu Zhongyue, Instructor at the Confucian School of Shou Subprefecture, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Ruzhen and was from Sui Subprefecture, Henan. He was a tribute scholar of the jiyou year.
Qian Kaishang, Instructor at the Confucian School of Xinchang County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Ruoyin and was from Wujiang County, Zhili. He was a tribute scholar of the guimao year.
Yang Bangxian, Instructor at the Confucian School of Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Zizhen and was from Baling County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar of the renzi year.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:

山東等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷崔佐〔廷相江西清江縣人監生〕
山東等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷火錢〔濟卿直隸揚州衛人監生〕
收掌試卷官
山東都轉運鹽使司運使彭寀〔廷湖湖廣茶陵州人甲午貢士〕
濟南府知府魏棠〔順甫湖廣蒲圻縣人庚戌進士〕
兗州府知府李守仁〔興安陝西鳳翔縣人丁未進士〕
===
東昌府知府馮霦〔澤甫山西蒲州人癸丑進士〕
濟南府同知陳墀〔子獻湖廣江夏縣人庚午貢士〕
受卷官
青州府同知王簡〔子敬直隸趙州人丙午貢士〕
登州府通判錢有威〔惟重直隸常熟縣人庚戌進士〕

東昌府臨清州知州蹇來譽〔子脩四川巴縣人庚戌進士〕
濟南府歷城縣知縣賈仁元〔子善山西萬泉縣人壬戌進士〕
punctuated:
河南汝寧府新蔡縣儒學教諭吳顏〔德愚，廣東南海縣人，己酉貢士〕。浙江金華府浦江縣儒學教諭陳忠育〔惟錫，湖廣武陵縣人，戊午貢士〕。

印卷官：山東等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷崔佐〔廷相，江西清江縣人，監生〕。山東等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷火錢〔濟卿，直隸揚州衛人，監生〕。

收掌試卷官：山東都轉運鹽使司運使彭寀〔廷湖，湖廣茶陵州人，甲午貢士〕。濟南府知府魏棠〔順甫，湖廣蒲圻縣人，庚戌進士〕。兗州府知府李守仁〔興安，陝西鳳翔縣人，丁未進士〕。東昌府知府馮霦〔澤甫，山西蒲州人，癸丑進士〕。濟南府同知陳墀〔子獻，湖廣江夏縣人，庚午貢士〕。

受卷官：青州府同知王簡〔子敬，直隸趙州人，丙午貢士〕。登州府通判錢有威〔惟重，直隸常熟縣人，庚戌進士〕。濟南府推官劉之蒙〔淑正，直隸霸州人，壬戌進士〕。濟南府濱州知州袁孟龍〔子雲，直隸興化縣人，庚子貢士〕。東昌府臨清州知州蹇來譽〔子脩，四川巴縣人，庚戌進士〕。濟南府歷城縣知縣賈仁元〔子善，山西萬泉縣人，壬戌進士〕。
translation_en:
Wu Yan, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xincai County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Deyu and was from Nanhai County, Guangdong. He was a tribute student of the jiyou year.

Chen Zhongyu, Instructor in the Confucian School of Pujiang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Weixi and was from Wuling County, Huguang. He was a tribute student of the wuwu year.

Huo Qian [?], Registrar in the Registry of the Shandong Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Jiqing and was from Yangzhou Guard, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). He was a student of the Imperial University.

Officials Responsible for Collecting and Safekeeping Examination Scripts:

Peng Cai, Salt Distribution Commissioner of Shandong, had the courtesy name Tinghu and was from Chaling Subprefecture, Huguang. He was a tribute student of the jiawu year.

Wei Tang, Prefect of Jinan, had the courtesy name Shunfu and was from Puqi County, Huguang. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the gengxu year.

Li Shouren, Prefect of Yanzhou, had the courtesy name Xing’an and was from Fengxiang County, Shaanxi. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the dingwei year.

Feng Bin, Prefect of Dongchang, had the courtesy name Zefu and was from Puzhou, Shanxi. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the guichou year.

Chen Chi, Vice Prefect of Jinan, had the courtesy name Zixian and was from Jiangxia County, Huguang. He was a tribute student of the gengwu year.

Officials Responsible for Receiving Examination Scripts:

Wang Jian, Vice Prefect of Qingzhou, had the courtesy name Zijing and was from Zhaozhou, Zhili. He was a tribute student of the bingwu year.

Qian Youwei, Assistant Prefect of Dengzhou, had the courtesy name Weizhong and was from Changshu County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the gengxu year.

Liu Zhimeng, Prefectural Judge of Jinan, had the courtesy name Shuzheng and was from Bazhou, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the renxu year.

Yuan Menglong, Subprefect of Binzhou in Jinan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ziyun and was from Xinghua County, Zhili. He was a tribute student of the gengzi year.

Jian Laiyu, Subprefect of Linqing in Dongchang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zixiu and was from Ba County, Sichuan. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the gengxu year.

Jia Renyuan, Magistrate of Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zishan and was from Wanquan County, Shanxi. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the renxu year.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
巍巍乎唯天爲大唯堯則之
唯天下至誠爲能盡其性
近聖人之居若此其甚也
易
九五孚于嘉吉象曰孚于嘉吉位正中也
豐大也明以動故豐
二篇之策萬有一千五百二十當萬物之
===
數也
夫乾確然示人易矣夫坤隤然示人簡矣
爻也者效此者也象也者像此者也
書
帝光天之下至于海隅蒼生
任官惟賢才左右惟其人臣爲上爲德爲
下爲民其難其愼惟和惟一德無常師
主善爲師善無常主協于克一
皇建其有極歛時五福
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
巍巍乎！唯天爲大，唯堯則之。
唯天下至誠，爲能盡其性。
近聖人之居，若此其甚也！

易
九五：孚于嘉，吉。象曰：「孚于嘉，吉」，位正中也。
豐，大也。明以動，故豐。
二篇之策，萬有一千五百二十，當萬物之數也。
夫乾，確然示人易矣；夫坤，隤然示人簡矣。
爻也者，效此者也；象也者，像此者也。

書
帝光天之下，至于海隅蒼生。
任官惟賢才，左右惟其人。臣爲上爲德，爲下爲民。其難其愼，惟和惟一。德無常師，主善爲師；善無常主，協于克一。
皇建其有極，歛時五福。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
How majestic! Heaven alone is great, and Yao alone took it as his model.
Only one possessed of the utmost sincerity under Heaven can fully realize his nature.
So very close was his dwelling to that of the sage!

Book of Changes
Nine in the fifth place: Sincerity toward what is good brings good fortune. The Commentary on the Images says: “Sincerity toward what is good brings good fortune” because the position is correct and central.
Feng means greatness. Clarity joined with movement produces abundance.
The yarrow stalks reckoned for the two parts total eleven thousand five hundred and twenty, corresponding to the number of the myriad things.
Qian, firm and strong, shows people ease; Kun, yielding, shows people simplicity.
The lines imitate this; the images represent this.

Book of Documents
The emperor’s radiance extends throughout all under Heaven, reaching the common people even in the remotest coastal regions.
Appoint to office only the worthy and talented; place at your side only suitable people. Ministers serve their sovereign by fostering virtue and those below by serving the people. How difficult this is, and how carefully it must be done! Be harmonious and single-minded. In cultivating virtue, there is no fixed teacher: take goodness as your teacher. Goodness has no fixed exemplar: unite in attaining singleness of purpose.
The sovereign establishes the supreme standard and gathers these five blessings.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
小大之臣咸懷忠良
詩
彼茁者葭壹發五豝于嗟乎騶虞
雨我公田遂及我私
王奮厥武如震如怒進厥虎臣闞如虓虎
鋪敦淮濆仍執醜虜截彼淮浦王師之
所
赫赫厥聲濯濯厥靈壽考且寧
春秋
===
夏公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男
曹伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕
齊師宋師曹師城邢〔僖公元年〕春王正月
城楚丘〔僖公二年〕春諸侯城緣陵〔僖公
十有四年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕公會晉侯齊
侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子杞伯救鄭
〔成公七年〕
齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田〔定公十年〕
punctuated:
小大之臣，咸懷忠良。

詩
彼茁者葭，壹發五豝，于嗟乎騶虞！
雨我公田，遂及我私。
王奮厥武，如震如怒。進厥虎臣，闞如虓虎。鋪敦淮濆，仍執醜虜。截彼淮浦，王師之所。
赫赫厥聲，濯濯厥靈，壽考且寧。

春秋
夏，公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕
齊師、宋師、曹師城邢。〔僖公元年〕春，王正月，城楚丘。〔僖公二年〕春，諸侯城緣陵。〔僖公十有四年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭。〔成公六年〕公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、杞伯救鄭。〔成公七年〕
齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。〔定公十年〕
translation_en:
The ministers, great and small, all cherish loyalty and goodness.

Book of Odes
Luxuriant are those reeds! One arrow is loosed at five sows. Ah, the zouyu, the righteous beast!
Let rain fall on our public fields, and then reach our private fields.
The king roused his martial might, like thunder, like wrath. He advanced his tiger-like ministers, roaring like fierce tigers. They deployed in strength along the banks of the Huai and repeatedly seized the enemy captives. Order prevailed along those shores of the Huai, where the king’s army was stationed.
Illustrious is your renown; splendid is your spiritual power. May you enjoy long life and peace.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In summer, the duke met at Kuiqiu with the chief minister, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi〕
The armies of Qi, Song, and Cao fortified Xing. 〔First year of Duke Xi〕 In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, Chu Qiu was fortified. 〔Second year of Duke Xi〕 In spring, the feudal lords fortified Yuanling. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Xi〕
Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔Sixth year of Duke Cheng〕 The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and the Earl of Qi to relieve Zheng. 〔Seventh year of Duke Cheng〕
Men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. 〔Tenth year of Duke Ding〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
禮記
故天降膏露地出醴泉山出器車河出馬
圖鳳皇麒麟皆在郊棷龜龍在宮沼
樂文同則上下和矣
唯聖人爲能饗帝
天地四方者男子之所有事也故必先有
志於其所有事然後敢用穀也
第貳場
論
===
聖人之心純亦不已
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜潁川太守黃霸爵關內侯詔〔元康四年〕
擬唐以李靖爲右僕射誥〔貞觀四年〕
擬宋以張載爲崇文院校書謝表〔熙寧二年〕
判語〔五條〕
官文書稽程
punctuated:
禮記
故天降膏露，地出醴泉，山出器車，河出馬圖，鳳皇麒麟皆在郊棷，龜龍在宮沼。
樂文同，則上下和矣。
唯聖人爲能饗帝。
天地四方者，男子之所有事也。故必先有志於其所有事，然後敢用穀也。
第貳場
論
聖人之心，純亦不已。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜潁川太守黃霸爵關內侯詔〔元康四年〕。
擬唐以李靖爲右僕射誥〔貞觀四年〕。
擬宋以張載爲崇文院校書謝表〔熙寧二年〕。
判語〔五條〕
官文書稽程。
translation_en:
Record of Rites
Thus Heaven sends down sweet dew, the earth brings forth springs of sweet water, the mountains yield vessels and chariots, and the river produces the horse chart. Phoenixes and qilin are all found in the groves beyond the city, and turtles and dragons in the palace ponds.
When the patterns of music are shared, those above and below are in harmony.
Only a sage can offer sacrifice to the Lord on High.
Heaven, Earth, and the four quarters are where a man has duties to perform. Therefore, he must first set his mind upon those duties; only then does he dare to partake of grain.

Second Session
Discourse
The sage’s heart is pure and unceasing.

Imperial Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One question from these categories [?]〕
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty granting Huang Ba, Grand Administrator of Yingchuan, the noble rank of Marquis within the Passes. 〔Fourth year of Yuankang〕
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Li Jing Vice Director of the Right of the Department of State Affairs. 〔Fourth year of Zhenguan〕
Compose a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song dynasty for Zhang Zai’s appointment as Proofreader in the Institute for the Veneration of Literature. 〔Second year of Xining〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items〕
Delaying official documents beyond the prescribed time limit.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
私借官車船
詐冒給路引
老幼不拷訊
造作不如法
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問至治之世醇和之氣溢爲靈液而甘露
零焉所謂瑞出於天上瑞也我
太祖高皇帝
===
昌期應運
革祉凝祥
至德格于
穹昊和氣溢于寰宇
登極之初甘露零于
乾清宮再零于鍾山矣至洪武乙卯至日行
太報于
圜丘而甘露零于
齋宮因
punctuated:
私借官車船。
詐冒給路引。
老幼不拷訊。
造作不如法。

第叁場
策〔五道〕

問：至治之世，醇和之氣溢爲靈液，而甘露零焉，所謂瑞出於天，上瑞也。我太祖高皇帝，昌期應運，革祉凝祥，至德格于穹昊，和氣溢于寰宇。登極之初，甘露零于乾清宮，再零于鍾山矣。至洪武乙卯，至日行太報于圜丘，而甘露零于齋宮，因
translation_en:
Privately borrowing government carts and boats.
Fraudulently obtaining travel permits.
Exemption of the elderly and young from interrogation under torture.
Manufacture or construction that does not conform to regulations.

Third Session
Policy Questions 〔Five questions〕

Question: In an age of perfect government, the vital energy of pure harmony overflows as numinous liquid, and sweet dew descends. This is what is meant by an auspicious sign issuing from Heaven—the highest kind of auspicious sign. Our Emperor Taizu Gao responded to Heaven’s appointed destiny at a flourishing juncture, renewed blessings [?], and gathered auspicious influences. His consummate virtue reached the lofty heavens, and harmonious vital energy filled the universe. At the beginning of his reign, sweet dew descended upon the Palace of Heavenly Purity (Qianqing Gong), and it descended again upon Zhongshan. In the yimao year of the Hongwu reign [1375], on the winter solstice, he performed the great thanksgiving sacrifice [?] at the Circular Mound, and sweet dew descended upon the Palace of Abstinence. Thereupon …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
特著爲甘露論以示羣工天下臣民傳播久矣
可得而莊誦之與我
皇上
道邁黃虞
心涵太始中和贊化信順通
玄一德格
天仰符
聖祖
神貺洊臻于宇内者種種疊見矣如嘉靖辛卯
===
至日行
大報于
圜丘而甘露零于
皇考之玄宮因
特製爲
欽天記頌以
賜勳輔其與
聖祖甘露論先後一揆也亦可得而闡揚之與
夫
punctuated: 特著爲《甘露論》，以示羣工，天下臣民傳播久矣，可得而莊誦之與？我皇上道邁黃虞，心涵太始，中和贊化，信順通玄，一德格天，仰符聖祖，神貺洊臻于宇内者，種種疊見矣。如嘉靖辛卯至日，行大報于圜丘，而甘露零于皇考之玄宮，因特製爲《欽天記頌》，以賜勳輔。其與聖祖《甘露論》，先後一揆也，亦可得而闡揚之與？夫
translation_en:
…specially composed the Discourse on Sweet Dew to show to the assembled officials. It has long circulated among the officials and people throughout the realm. Might it be solemnly recited?

Our Emperor’s Way surpasses that of the Yellow Emperor and Shun; his mind embraces the primordial beginning. Through equilibrium and harmony he assists the transforming processes of nature; through sincerity and accord he communes with the mysterious. His undivided virtue reaches Heaven, matching above the example of the sagely ancestor. Divine blessings have repeatedly descended throughout the realm, appearing in many forms, one after another. For example, on the winter solstice of the xinmao year of Jiajing [1531], he performed the great sacrifice of thanksgiving at the Circular Mound, and sweet dew fell upon the sepulchral palace of his deceased imperial father. He therefore specially composed the Record and Eulogy of Revering Heaven and bestowed it upon the meritorious nobles and chief ministers. This work and the sagely ancestor’s Discourse on Sweet Dew, though composed at different times, follow the same principle. Might its meaning likewise be expounded and proclaimed?

Now, …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
郊報之日甘露輙零
聖祖
神孫同符不爽允見
玄元篤祜之奇應也不知我
聖祖我
皇上所以孚格之者果何所本與顓鋪張而推
原之以見
聖人得天之實
問學古有獲傅說之言也儒者守焉子路
===
曰何必讀書然後爲學則夫子疾之學
之不可已也如是然唐虞之世墳典未
備士生斯時何所誦習而稷契臯夔道
德勳業若此其卓卓也伊尹樂堯舜之
道於畎畝說者謂其誦詩讀書然與厥
後左右商王功成允殖果自誦讀中來
與尚父磻溪之釣叟耳後車一載爲王
者師其果何所本與抑誦讀之外固自
有其學與其見諸問答者亦可指而言
punctuated:
郊報之日，甘露輙零。聖祖神孫，同符不爽，允見玄元篤祜之奇應也。不知我聖祖、我皇上所以孚格之者，果何所本與？顓鋪張而推原之，以見聖人得天之實。
問：「學古有獲」，傅說之言也，儒者守焉。子路曰：「何必讀書，然後爲學？」則夫子疾之。學之不可已也如是。然唐虞之世，墳典未備，士生斯時，何所誦習，而稷、契、臯、夔道德勳業，若此其卓卓也？伊尹樂堯舜之道於畎畝，說者謂其誦詩讀書，然與？厥後左右商王，功成允殖，果自誦讀中來與？尚父，磻溪之釣叟耳，後車一載，爲王者師，其果何所本與？抑誦讀之外，固自有其學與？其見諸問答者，亦可指而言
translation_en:
…On the day of the suburban sacrifice of thanksgiving, sweet dew invariably descended. The sagely ancestor and his divine descendant received identical auspicious signs, without discrepancy: truly this reveals the wondrous response of the abundant blessings bestowed by the Primal Mystery (Xuanyuan). Yet upon what, ultimately, did our sagely ancestor and our present emperor base the sincerity through which they elicited this response? Expound this fully and trace its source, thereby revealing the reality of the sage’s winning Heaven’s favor.
Question: “Study antiquity and you will gain something”: these are the words of Fu Yue, which Confucian scholars uphold. When Zilu said, “Why must one read books before it can count as learning?” the Master disapproved. Such is the necessity of never abandoning learning. Yet in the age of Tang and Yu, the ancient writings and canons were not yet complete. What did scholars born in that age recite and study, that Ji, Xie, Gao, and Kui should have been so outstanding in virtue and achievement? Yi Yin delighted in the Way of Yao and Shun while working in the fields. Commentators say that he recited the Odes and read the Documents. Was this so? Later, he assisted the king of Shang, accomplishing great deeds and bringing lasting growth. Did these achievements truly arise from recitation and reading? Shangfu, the Venerated Father, was merely an old fisherman at Panxi; yet once taken aboard the accompanying carriage, he became the king’s teacher. Upon what, ultimately, was this founded? Or is there indeed a learning beyond recitation and reading? Can what appears in their questions and answers likewise be identified and explained…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
之與後世典籍大備燦若日星宜其德
業炳耀先民矣顧舉賢良者見斥於轅
生號通經者失身於王氏稽古自負者
至誇車馬之榮施帳授徒者不免聲伎
之溺讀書以明理也乃有不識字之譏
經術以經世也乃有三不足之說不學
無術者忠宜於漢室不由師傳者默契
大道然則問學其可廢與諸生皆誦
法孔子者也其明辯之以著於篇不然
則說之見固矣
===
===
問姓氏之立先王所以維繫人心辯別人
道其義大矣然何以為姓何以為氏姓
氏抑起於何時與且古有因國而氏因
謚而氏因官因爵因居因事而氏而今
不然豈古姓氏可改而今不可改與抑
別有其故與三代而上無容議矣乃漢
司馬遷脩史記傳世本以明姓氏之所
由果何所據而考與晉宋而降譜牒紛
punctuated:
之與？後世典籍大備，燦若日星，宜其德業炳耀先民矣。顧舉賢良者見斥於轅生，號通經者失身於王氏，稽古自負者至誇車馬之榮，施帳授徒者不免聲伎之溺。讀書以明理也，乃有不識字之譏；經術以經世也，乃有三不足之說。不學無術者忠宜於漢室，不由師傳者默契大道，然則問學其可廢與？諸生皆誦法孔子者也，其明辯之，以著於篇。不然，則說之見固矣。

問：姓氏之立，先王所以維繫人心、辯別人道，其義大矣。然何以為姓？何以為氏？姓氏抑起於何時與？且古有因國而氏、因謚而氏、因官、因爵、因居、因事而氏，而今不然，豈古姓氏可改，而今不可改與？抑別有其故與？三代而上，無容議矣。乃漢司馬遷脩《史記》，傳《世本》，以明姓氏之所由，果何所據而考與？晉宋而降，譜牒紛
translation_en:
…can these also be identified and discussed? In later ages, the canonical writings became fully available, brilliant as the sun and stars. Surely people’s virtue and achievements ought to have shone more brightly than those of their predecessors. Yet one recommended as worthy and good was rebuked by Master Yuan; one reputed to understand the classics compromised himself by serving the Wang house; one who prided himself on investigating antiquity went so far as to boast of the distinction of his carriages and horses; and one who set up a teaching curtain to instruct disciples could not avoid being engrossed in music and entertainers. Books are read to illuminate principle, yet there was the taunt that someone did not recognize written characters. Classical learning is intended to order the world, yet there was the doctrine of the “three things not worth heeding.” One without learning or scholarly skill proved loyal and serviceable to the Han ruling house [?], while one who received no instruction from a teacher attained an unspoken accord with the Great Way. Can inquiry and learning, then, be dispensed with? You candidates all study and take Confucius as your model. Distinguish these matters clearly and set out your conclusions in writing. Otherwise, the view expressed here will stand confirmed.

Question: The establishment of surnames and lineage names was a means by which the former kings bound people’s hearts together and distinguished human relationships. Its significance was great indeed. But what constitutes a surname, and what constitutes a lineage name? When did surnames and lineage names first arise? In antiquity, lineage names were derived from states, posthumous titles, offices, noble ranks, places of residence, and events. Today this is no longer so. Could surnames and lineage names be changed in antiquity but not today? Or is there some other reason? We may leave aside the Three Dynasties and earlier times. But when Sima Qian of the Han compiled the Records of the Grand Historian and transmitted the Origins of Lineages (Shiben) [?] to explain the origins of surnames and lineage names, on what evidence did he actually base his investigations? From the Jin and Song onward, genealogical records proliferated…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
然若百家譜百官譜官族志氏族志姓
系錄衣冠譜元和姓纂諸譜不知於史記
世本亦可參考而並論歟古者自羲寧
祖自仁率親士庶人得世其家卿大夫
得世其族諸侯得世其國教化行而風
俗美矣而今則不然以根本之道不明
而支派之分未辨也茲欲重本敦化使
綱維振於上而不渙分義昭於下而有
紀必何如而後可
===
問文武並用長久之術雖甚盛德不能去
兵也凡志在康時者固不可以弗之講
矣不知博覽載籍宜何所準焉孔子云
不教而戰是謂棄之而乃或不然有試
以婦人而爭取信於闔閭有驅市人以
戰而卒收功於泜水至今談兵者偉之
如是則戰可不教矣其運用之妙可得
而測之否與減竈可以制勝也而或以
□□□□□衆可以制勝也而或以用寡
punctuated:
然，若《百家譜》《百官譜》《官族志》《氏族志》《姓系錄》《衣冠譜》《元和姓纂》諸譜，不知於《史記》《世本》亦可參考而並論歟？古者自羲寧祖，自仁率親，士庶人得世其家，卿大夫得世其族，諸侯得世其國，教化行而風俗美矣。而今則不然，以根本之道不明，而支派之分未辨也。茲欲重本敦化，使綱維振於上而不渙，分義昭於下而有紀，必何如而後可？

問：文武並用，長久之術，雖甚盛德，不能去兵也。凡志在康時者，固不可以弗之講矣。不知博覽載籍，宜何所準焉？孔子云：「不教而戰，是謂棄之。」而乃或不然：有試以婦人而爭取信於闔閭，有驅市人以戰而卒收功於泜水，至今談兵者偉之。如是，則戰可不教矣。其運用之妙，可得而測之否與？減竈可以制勝也，而或以□□□□□衆可以制勝也，而或以用寡
translation_en:
…in profusion, including such genealogical works as Genealogies of the Hundred Families, Genealogies of the Hundred Officials, Account of Official Lineages, Account of Clans, Record of Surname Descent, Genealogies of the Gentry, and the Yuanhe Compilation of Surnames. Can these also be consulted alongside the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji) and the Origins of Hereditary Houses (Shiben), and discussed together with them? In antiquity, people honored their ancestors through righteousness [?] and drew their kin together through benevolence. Men of service and commoners could perpetuate their households through the generations, ministers and grandees their lineages, and feudal lords their states. Moral instruction prevailed, and customs were fine. Today, however, this is not so, because the principles governing the roots are unclear and the distinctions among the branches have not been discerned. If we now wish to give weight to the roots and strengthen moral transformation, so that the bonds of order are upheld above without disintegrating, and the duties proper to each station are manifest below in an orderly fashion, what must be done to achieve this?

Question: Employing both civil and military means is the art of securing enduring rule. Even those of the most exalted virtue cannot dispense with arms. Anyone intent on bringing peace to the age must certainly study this matter. Yet, in reading widely through the written records, what should one take as a standard? Confucius said: “To send them into battle without instruction is to abandon them.” Yet some cases seem otherwise: one man conducted a trial with women and thereby strove to win the confidence of Helü; another drove townspeople into battle and ultimately won victory at the Zhi River. To this day, those who discuss warfare admire these achievements. If so, it seems that one can wage war without training. Can the subtle mastery with which they employed their forces be fathomed? Reducing cooking fires can secure victory, yet some have used [five illegible characters; connection uncertain]. A large force can secure victory, yet some have used a small force…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
勝以至行軍有簡者有煩者有寛者有
嚴者迹其所行若矛盾而其成功則同
他如先據北山而勝秦者智矣或隳之
而潰焉一卒爲神而復齊者奇矣或效
之而殲焉讀父書者不免自殞孰古法
者乃反喪師稽其所用若合而其勝敗
顧殊此其故何也可歷指而言之與夫
棄繻請纓固濟南之少年也諸士子必
有慕其風而興起者矣願盡言之以觀
===
所蓄
問山東古齊魯宋衛之墟平原沃壤世守
禮義天下稱名邦焉
明興以來加惠元元休養訓習宜其惇龐蕃息
益倍曩時顧惟近事則有可議者閭閻
凋敝逋負未輸何以督之徭役不均貧
弱坐困何以平之流移未復田野多蕪
何以辟之饑饉間臻賑救無策何以備
之軍伍歲勾冊籍仍缺何以清之驛傳
punctuated:
勝。以至行軍，有簡者，有煩者，有寛者，有嚴者，迹其所行若矛盾，而其成功則同。他如先據北山而勝秦者智矣，或隳之而潰焉；一卒爲神而復齊者奇矣，或效之而殲焉。讀父書者不免自殞，孰古法者乃反喪師。稽其所用若合，而其勝敗顧殊，此其故何也？可歷指而言之與？夫棄繻請纓，固濟南之少年也。諸士子必有慕其風而興起者矣，願盡言之，以觀所蓄。

問：山東，古齊魯宋衛之墟，平原沃壤，世守禮義，天下稱名邦焉。明興以來，加惠元元，休養訓習，宜其惇龐蕃息，益倍曩時。顧惟近事，則有可議者：閭閻凋敝，逋負未輸，何以督之？徭役不均，貧弱坐困，何以平之？流移未復，田野多蕪，何以辟之？饑饉間臻，賑救無策，何以備之？軍伍歲勾，冊籍仍缺，何以清之？驛傳
translation_en:
…win. Even in conducting campaigns, some employ simple measures and others elaborate ones; some are lenient and others strict. Their actions appear contradictory, yet they achieve the same success. For other examples, the man who first occupied Beishan and defeated Qin was wise, yet another abandoned it [?] and suffered a rout. The man who made a single soldier into a divine figure [?] and recovered Qi was ingenious, yet another imitated him and was annihilated. One who read his father’s military writings could not escape his own destruction; another, versed in ancient methods, instead lost his army. On examination, the methods they employed seem alike, yet their victories and defeats differed. Why was this? Can you identify the cases individually and explain them? The man who discarded his silk travel credential and requested a cord with which to bind the enemy was, after all, a youth from Jinan. Among you candidates there must be those who admire his example and are inspired to action. Set forth your views fully, so that we may see the learning you have accumulated.

Question: Shandong occupies the former territories of the ancient states of Qi, Lu, Song, and Wei. With its level plains and fertile soil, it has upheld ritual propriety and righteousness for generations and is renowned throughout the realm as a distinguished region. Since the rise of the Ming, benevolence has been extended to the common people, allowing them to recuperate and receive instruction. They ought therefore to have become more upright and substantial in their customs, and to have multiplied and flourished far beyond former times. Yet recent circumstances present matters calling for discussion. Communities are impoverished, and tax arrears remain unpaid: how should payment be enforced? Labor obligations are unevenly distributed, leaving the poor and weak trapped in hardship: how should these be equalized? Those who fled or migrated have not returned, and much farmland lies waste: how should it be brought into cultivation? Famine strikes from time to time, but there is no plan for relief: how should preparations be made? Men are called up each year to fill military vacancies, yet the registers still show deficiencies: how should these be put in order? The postal relay service…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
衝疲供億靡繼何以應之寇盜竊發緝
捕滋擾何以靖之訟獄繁興朋儕相構
何以息之夫宇宙內事皆吾分內事也
古人自秀才時卽以天下爲己任况此
乃諸生目擊者乎其必有槩于中久矣
願條陳之司
國計者將有採焉
punctuated: 衝疲，供億靡繼，何以應之？寇盜竊發，緝捕滋擾，何以靖之？訟獄繁興，朋儕相構，何以息之？夫宇宙內事，皆吾分內事也。古人自秀才時，卽以天下爲己任，况此乃諸生目擊者乎？其必有槩于中久矣。願條陳之，司國計者將有採焉。
translation_en: …overburdened and exhausted by traffic, with provisions no longer forthcoming: how can these demands be met? Bandits and robbers spring up, and efforts to apprehend them cause further disturbance: how can peace be restored? Lawsuits proliferate, and associates bring accusations against one another: how can this be stopped? Indeed, all affairs within the universe fall within our own responsibilities. The ancients took responsibility for all under Heaven upon themselves even while still students; how much more should you students do so when these are matters you have witnessed yourselves? Surely you have long felt deeply concerned about them. Please set out your proposals point by point; those responsible for the state's finances may find something to adopt in them.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人七十五名
第一名王象坤　新城縣學增廣生　詩
第二名錢楷　東昌府學生　易
第三名吳道傳　朝城縣學生　書
第四名韓必光　安丘縣學生　禮記
第五名苗應元　武定州學生　春秋
第六名張燭　壽光縣學增廣生　詩
第七名馬三樂　陽信縣學生　易
===
第八名杜時　泗水縣學生　詩
第九名臧惟一　諸城縣學增廣生　書
第十名孟春　淄川縣學生　詩
第十一名米成道　館陶縣學生　易
第十二名韓荅善　淄川縣學增廣生　書

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
巍巍乎唯天爲大唯堯則之
王象坤
同考試官教諭區　批〔精確整嚴宜錄以式〕
同考試官教諭楊　批〔語意渾融不落色相〕
同考試官教諭施　批〔民不能名堯孔子以則天名之〕
〔此作發揮明盡亦善言聖人者〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔講則天處語有斟酌〕
===
考試官教諭胡　批〔典雅可誦〕
聖人擬帝德之同乎天所以見其大也蓋至大
莫如天也而帝堯之德獨能同之其大爲何如
哉夫子上嘉而言之也意謂帝王之治本于德
帝王之德備于堯吾觀諸天而徵堯之爲大矣
蓋物之以大稱者或可得而踰焉可踰非大也
或可得而限焉可限非大也若夫輕清上浮而
測之莫窮其端凡天下之有形者不出其所覆
之下穹窿廣運而廓之莫究其極凡天下之有
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
巍巍乎！唯天爲大，唯堯則之。
王象坤
同考試官教諭區批〔精確整嚴，宜錄以式。〕
同考試官教諭楊批〔語意渾融，不落色相。〕
同考試官教諭施批〔民不能名堯，孔子以則天名之。〕〔此作發揮明盡，亦善言聖人者。〕
考試官教諭劉批〔講則天處，語有斟酌。〕
考試官教諭胡批〔典雅可誦。〕
聖人擬帝德之同乎天，所以見其大也。蓋至大莫如天也，而帝堯之德獨能同之，其大爲何如哉！夫子上嘉而言之也，意謂帝王之治本于德，帝王之德備于堯，吾觀諸天而徵堯之爲大矣。蓋物之以大稱者，或可得而踰焉，可踰非大也；或可得而限焉，可限非大也。若夫輕清上浮，而測之莫窮其端，凡天下之有形者，不出其所覆之下；穹窿廣運，而廓之莫究其極，凡天下之有
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

“How lofty! Heaven alone is great, and Yao alone took it as his model.”
Wang Xiangkun

Associate Examiner Ou, Instructor, comments: “Precise, exact, orderly, and rigorous; it should be included as a model.”
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “The language and meaning blend seamlessly, without becoming bound to outward forms.”
Associate Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: “The people could find no name for Yao’s greatness; Confucius characterized him as taking Heaven as his model.” “This composition develops the meaning clearly and fully; its author, too, speaks well of the sage.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The wording in the discussion of taking Heaven as one’s model is carefully weighed.”
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “Classical and elegant, worthy of recitation.”

The sage compares the emperor’s virtue to Heaven, showing thereby his greatness. Nothing is greater than Heaven, yet Emperor Yao’s virtue alone could equal it. How great, then, must he have been! The Master spoke these words in lofty praise [?], meaning that the government of emperors and kings is rooted in virtue, and that their virtue was fully realized in Yao. By observing Heaven, I can attest to Yao’s greatness.

Things called great may sometimes be surpassed; what can be surpassed is not truly great. They may sometimes be bounded; what can be bounded is not truly great. But consider Heaven: light and pure, it floats above, and no measurement can exhaust its extent. All things under Heaven that have form lie beneath its covering. title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
象者悉囿于所包之中天之巍巍固莫有竝其
大者矣唯堯之爲君也中天應運而峻德之昭
格者有以脗合其貞觀之體繼天出治而至德
之充周者有以克配其丕冒之神物無不覆嘗
見天之大不可踰也而堯之首出庶物亦孰得
而踰之峻極于天誠有唐之一人而前乎此者
未之或先矣物無不包嘗見天之大不可限也
而堯之光被四表亦孰得而限之溥博如天誠
放勳之獨優而後乎此者殆難其繼矣謂之曰
===
唯天爲大唯堯則之信乎天以巍巍而位乎上
所以爲萬物之天者此也堯以巍巍而位乎下
所以爲萬民之天者此也非堯莫能配天非天
莫能盡堯吁此其所以爲大也抑史臣贊堯曰
欽明曰恭讓曰文武聖神不一而足至吾夫子
則天之外無餘說焉蓋史臣所陳散殊之迹而
夫子獨探其統體之全譬之風雨露雷莫非至
教而一言蔽之則天而已後世徒襲其迹至有
如雲如日稱之者秪見乎其小之也於此知萬
punctuated: 象者悉囿于所包之中。天之巍巍，固莫有竝其大者矣。唯堯之爲君也，中天應運，而峻德之昭格者，有以脗合其貞觀之體；繼天出治，而至德之充周者，有以克配其丕冒之神。物無不覆，嘗見天之大不可踰也，而堯之首出庶物，亦孰得而踰之？峻極于天，誠有唐之一人，而前乎此者未之或先矣。物無不包，嘗見天之大不可限也，而堯之光被四表，亦孰得而限之？溥博如天，誠放勳之獨優，而後乎此者殆難其繼矣。謂之曰：「唯天爲大，唯堯則之。」信乎！天以巍巍而位乎上，所以爲萬物之天者此也；堯以巍巍而位乎下，所以爲萬民之天者此也。非堯莫能配天，非天莫能盡堯。吁！此其所以爲大也。抑史臣贊堯，曰欽明，曰恭讓，曰文武聖神，不一而足。至吾夫子，則天之外無餘說焉。蓋史臣所陳，散殊之迹，而夫子獨探其統體之全。譬之風雨露雷，莫非至教，而一言蔽之，則天而已。後世徒襲其迹，至有如雲如日稱之者，秪見乎其小之也。於此知萬
translation_en:
…all that has perceptible form lies within its embrace. Such is Heaven’s loftiness: nothing can equal its greatness. Only Yao, as ruler, responded to the destined course of his age in accord with Heaven; the shining reach of his lofty virtue accorded with Heaven’s enduring manifestation. Following Heaven in bringing forth good government, the fullness and pervasiveness of his consummate virtue matched Heaven’s spirit of all-encompassing protection. Nothing is outside Heaven’s shelter: we see that its greatness cannot be surpassed. Who, then, could surpass Yao, who stood foremost among all things? His loftiness reached Heaven itself. Truly, he was the unique sovereign of Tang, and none before him had exceeded him. Nothing is outside Heaven’s embrace: we see that its greatness cannot be bounded. Who, then, could bound Yao’s radiance, which extended to the four outermost regions? Vast and expansive as Heaven, such was the singular excellence of Fangxun [Yao]; those who came afterward could scarcely carry it on. Thus it is said: “Heaven alone is great; Yao alone modeled himself upon it.” How true! Heaven, lofty and majestic, occupies its place above; this is what makes it Heaven to all things. Yao, lofty and majestic, occupies his place below; this is what makes him Heaven to all the people. None but Yao could match Heaven; nothing but Heaven could fully express Yao. Ah! This is what constituted his greatness.

Moreover, the court historians praised Yao as reverent and discerning, respectful and yielding, accomplished in civil and martial virtues, sagely and spiritual—their descriptions were manifold. Yet our Master [Confucius] offered no further explanation beyond his modeling himself upon Heaven. What the historians set forth were separate manifestations; the Master alone fathomed the unified whole. To draw an analogy, wind, rain, dew, and thunder are all forms of supreme instruction [?]; yet to sum them up in a single word, they are simply Heaven. Later generations merely repeated these outward manifestations, even praising him as like clouds or like the sun; this only shows how they diminished him. From this we know that throughout the myriad…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
世爲君者莫如堯而萬世之稱堯者莫如夫子
之一言
唯天下至誠爲能盡其性
錢楷
同考試官教諭吳　批〔性卽理也天以是理賦之於人本無不實故德無不實則性無不盡而天地人物自相通矣作〕
發明無餘蓋深於性理之說者
考試官教諭劉　批〔詞意周匝體製閑雅宜〕
多士
===
考試官教諭胡　批〔明遂整潔〕
論誠之至者能全其天之所命焉蓋天之所命
者性也至誠純乎天矣此性之所以全與中庸
二十二章言天道也謂夫自性之眞實而言謂
之誠自誠之賦予而言謂之性其實一也故誠
有未至者性不可得而盡矣惟夫湛一中涵而
太極之懿獨隆於天縱之初精純內蘊而无妄
之眞不汨於形生之後斯則德無不實而誠極
其至矣有不足以盡性乎蓋一疵不存則萬理
punctuated:
世爲君者莫如堯，而萬世之稱堯者莫如夫子之一言。
唯天下至誠爲能盡其性。
錢楷
同考試官教諭吳　批〔性卽理也，天以是理賦之於人，本無不實，故德無不實則性無不盡，而天地人物自相通矣。作〕發明無餘，蓋深於性理之說者。
考試官教諭劉　批〔詞意周匝，體製閑雅，宜〕多士。
考試官教諭胡　批〔明遂整潔。〕
論誠之至者能全其天之所命焉。蓋天之所命者性也，至誠純乎天矣，此性之所以全與！中庸二十二章言天道也，謂夫自性之眞實而言謂之誠，自誠之賦予而言謂之性，其實一也。故誠有未至者，性不可得而盡矣。惟夫湛一中涵，而太極之懿獨隆於天縱之初；精純內蘊，而无妄之眞不汨於形生之後，斯則德無不實而誠極其至矣。有不足以盡性乎？蓋一疵不存，則萬理
translation_en:
…among rulers throughout the ages, none equals Yao; and among those who have praised Yao throughout the ages, none equals the Master in this single statement.

“Only one possessed of the utmost sincerity under Heaven can fully realize his nature.”

Qian Kai

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “Nature is principle. Heaven endows human beings with this principle, which is originally entirely real. Thus, when virtue is entirely real, nature is fully realized, and Heaven, Earth, human beings, and things are naturally interconnected. This composition elucidates the matter exhaustively; its author surely has a profound understanding of the teachings on nature and principle.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “The wording and ideas are comprehensive, and the form is poised and elegant, befitting the many scholars [?].”

Comment by Examiner Hu, Instructor: “Clear and penetrating [?], orderly and polished.”

I maintain that one whose sincerity reaches its utmost can fully realize what Heaven has ordained for him. For what Heaven ordains is nature; utmost sincerity is wholly in accord with Heaven. Is this not how nature is fully realized? Chapter twenty-two of the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of the Way of Heaven. Considered in terms of the reality of nature, it is called sincerity; considered in terms of the endowment of sincerity, it is called nature. In substance, they are one. Thus, where sincerity has not reached its utmost, nature cannot be fully realized. Only when limpid unity is held within, and the excellence of the Supreme Ultimate flourishes uniquely at the very inception of Heaven’s endowment; when refined purity is stored within, and the truth of freedom from falsity remains unclouded after bodily life begins—only then is virtue entirely real and sincerity brought to its utmost. Could there be anything insufficient for fully realizing nature? For when not a single flaw remains, the myriad principles…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
自爲之明盡不必擇善以爲知而誠之所通精
而明焉于凡所性之體爲能周知之而不蔽一
眞自知則衆善自爲之悉有不必固執以爲仁
而誠之所立妙而應焉于凡所性之藴足以兼
體之而不遺是雖散於庶物統於人倫天之賦
於我者何悉也然莫非性也則亦莫非誠之所
盡也以實心而會實理固將合巨細於畢舉矣
而何有於滲漏乎微而天載顯而民彝我之受
於天者至足也然有是誠也卽有是性之能盡
===
也以至德而凝至道固將貫精粗於一致矣而
何有於虧欠耶至是則人物之所以立命者先
得其同然天地之所以立心者獨完其大本而
位育參賛亦吾性分之能事矣非天道而何哉
雖然誠者盡性者也誠之者復性者也安勉不
同成功一也是以子思不徒曰盡性而卽以致
曲爲言蓋欲學者以至誠爲的趨而赴之耳固
非徒以絶德示天下也孟子言稱堯舜而察識
擴充開示眞切其亦有所受也夫
punctuated: 自爲之明盡，不必擇善以爲知，而誠之所通，精而明焉，于凡所性之體，爲能周知之而不蔽。一眞自知，則衆善自爲之悉有，不必固執以爲仁，而誠之所立，妙而應焉，于凡所性之藴，足以兼體之而不遺。是雖散於庶物，統於人倫，天之賦於我者何悉也！然莫非性也，則亦莫非誠之所盡也。以實心而會實理，固將合巨細於畢舉矣，而何有於滲漏乎？微而天載，顯而民彝，我之受於天者至足也。然有是誠也，卽有是性之能盡也。以至德而凝至道，固將貫精粗於一致矣，而何有於虧欠耶？至是，則人物之所以立命者，先得其同然；天地之所以立心者，獨完其大本，而位育參賛，亦吾性分之能事矣。非天道而何哉？雖然，誠者盡性者也，誠之者復性者也。安勉不同，成功一也。是以子思不徒曰盡性，而卽以致曲爲言，蓋欲學者以至誠爲的，趨而赴之耳，固非徒以絶德示天下也。孟子言稱堯舜，而察識擴充，開示眞切，其亦有所受也夫！
translation_en:
…all principles naturally become fully clear. There is no need to select the good in order to attain understanding: what sincerity penetrates is refined and luminous, enabling one to know comprehensively, without obscurity, the entire constitution of one’s nature. When the single truth knows itself [?], all goodness naturally becomes fully possessed. There is no need to hold fast to it in order to attain benevolence: what sincerity establishes is subtle and responsive, enabling one to embody together, without omission, everything contained in one’s nature. Though dispersed among the myriad things and brought together in human relationships, how comprehensive is what Heaven has endowed in me! Yet none of this lies outside nature, and therefore none lies beyond what sincerity fully realizes. By bringing a true heart into accord with true principles, one will surely embrace great and small alike, leaving nothing unfulfilled. How could anything slip through?

From Heaven’s workings in their subtlety to the constant norms of human life in their manifest form, what I have received from Heaven is utterly complete. With this sincerity, there is the capacity to realize this nature fully. By concentrating the utmost Way through the utmost virtue, one will surely unite the refined and the coarse in a single coherence. How could there be any deficiency? At this point, one first apprehends the common ground by which people and things establish their allotted existence, and uniquely preserves intact the great foundation by which Heaven and Earth establish their heart. Ensuring that all things take their proper places and flourish, and participating in and assisting the transforming work of Heaven and Earth, are also achievements within the capacities of my own nature. What could this be but the Way of Heaven?

Nevertheless, those who are sincere fully realize their nature; those who strive to become sincere restore their nature. Being at ease in this and exerting oneself toward it differ, but the achievement is one. Thus Zisi does not speak only of fully realizing one’s nature; he also speaks of developing particular incipient goodness to its utmost. His intention is simply that learners take utmost sincerity as their target and press toward it. He certainly does not merely display surpassing virtue to the world. Mencius invokes Yao and Shun in his teaching, yet gives lucid and concrete instruction in discerning and recognizing goodness, and extending and enlarging it. Surely he too had received this teaching through transmission!

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
近聖人之居若此其甚也
吳道傳
同考試官教諭陳　批〔是題作者非窘則俗此作會意〕
〔成文且思逸辭清〕
同考試官學正皇甫　批〔塲中士子率多於居之甚近處〕
〔纏擾便自庸腐此作獨能擺脫道意錄之〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔思致微婉〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔孟子自任意宛然言外〕
大賢於聖道之傳而有感於生同其地焉夫孟
===
子願學孔子者也況於生同其地則見而知之
者將不在是乎孟子叙道統而終之以此蓋謂
聖人之道欲其遠有所寄必先近有所承自禹
皐伊呂以来固皆見而知也至于今何獨不然
那彼斯道之傳雖幸乎世之未遠而授受之機
或限于地之相隔亦未敢謂必得其傳也乃今
之於孔子何幸其地之相近乎蓋魯與鄒其爲
封不同也由鄒之魯其相去則無幾也仰哲人
之未遠而私竊以善其身可以遡其淵源之自
punctuated:
近聖人之居，若此其甚也。
吳道傳
同考試官教諭陳，批〔是題作者非窘則俗，此作會意〕〔成文，且思逸辭清。〕
同考試官學正皇甫，批〔塲中士子率多於居之甚近處〕〔纏擾，便自庸腐，此作獨能擺脫道意，錄之。〕
考試官教諭劉，批〔思致微婉。〕
考試官教諭胡，批〔孟子自任意宛然言外。〕
大賢於聖道之傳，而有感於生同其地焉。夫孟子願學孔子者也，況於生同其地，則見而知之者將不在是乎？孟子叙道統而終之以此，蓋謂聖人之道，欲其遠有所寄，必先近有所承。自禹皐伊呂以来，固皆見而知也，至于今何獨不然那？彼斯道之傳，雖幸乎世之未遠，而授受之機或限于地之相隔，亦未敢謂必得其傳也。乃今之於孔子，何幸其地之相近乎！蓋魯與鄒，其爲封不同也；由鄒之魯，其相去則無幾也。仰哲人之未遠，而私竊以善其身，可以遡其淵源之自
translation_en:
“So very near to the place where the sage lived.”
Wu Daochuan
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Those who write on this topic are either constrained or trite. This composition grasps its meaning and develops it into an essay; its thought is also untrammeled and its language clear.”
Associate Examiner Huangfu, School Director, comments: “Candidates in the examination compound mostly become entangled in the extreme proximity of the residences, and so lapse into the pedestrian and stale. This composition alone breaks free and expresses the meaning [?]; I select it.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The conception is subtle and the expression gentle.”
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “Mencius’s sense of his own responsibility is vividly present beyond the words.”
The great worthy, reflecting on the transmission of the sage’s Way, was moved by having been born in the same locality. Now Mencius aspired to learn from Confucius. Since he was, moreover, born in the same locality, might not one who knows through seeing be found here? Mencius concluded his account of the succession of the Way with these words. His meaning was that, if the sage’s Way is to have someone to whom it may be entrusted in the distant future, it must first have someone nearby to receive it. From Yu, Gao, Yi, and Lü onward, they were indeed all men who knew through seeing. Why should this alone not be so today?
As for the transmission of this Way, although one may be fortunate that the intervening generations are not distant, the opportunity to impart and receive it may be restricted by geographical separation; one would not yet dare claim that one was certain to receive its transmission. How fortunate, then, is the geographical proximity to Confucius now! Lu and Zou were different domains, but the distance from Zou to Lu was slight. Looking up to the wise man, who is not yet far removed, and privately drawing upon him to perfect oneself, one can trace his teaching to its very source …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
幸流風之未泯而近取以宗其道可以探其統
緒之歸聖人之至教固未得躬逢其盛也壤地
之相接則教思之猶存自此而求之不有餘師
乎聖人之精藴固不可悉得而聞也宮墻之在
望則微言之可稽由是而之焉文不在玆乎是
雖以道覺天下者地不足以限之而心法淵微
之奧於至近者爲尤觀其深焉其必有見知者
以紹其傳若禹皐之生於唐虞之際者矣是雖
以心求聖人者居不足以囿之而聖德漸被之
===
深於至近者爲獨得其宗焉殆將使聞知者賴
有所啓若伊呂之出於夏商之世者矣觀此而
孟子自任之意不居然可見乎韓子曰孔子傳
之孟軻夫孔門稱心傳者惟顏之卓爾曾之一
貫孟子乃私淑子思者而特以道統歸之何哉
蓋戰國之世邪說横行仁義充塞非孟子廓清
之功孔子之道亦幾于晦矣然則稱其功不在
禹下者此也其叙道統而勇于自任殆有所感
也夫
punctuated: 幸流風之未泯，而近取以宗其道，可以探其統緒之歸。聖人之至教，固未得躬逢其盛也；壤地之相接，則教思之猶存，自此而求之，不有餘師乎？聖人之精藴，固不可悉得而聞也；宮墻之在望，則微言之可稽，由是而之焉，文不在玆乎？是雖以道覺天下者，地不足以限之，而心法淵微之奧，於至近者爲尤。觀其深焉，其必有見知者以紹其傳，若禹皐之生於唐虞之際者矣。是雖以心求聖人者，居不足以囿之，而聖德漸被之深，於至近者爲獨。得其宗焉，殆將使聞知者賴有所啓，若伊呂之出於夏商之世者矣。觀此，而孟子自任之意，不居然可見乎？韓子曰：「孔子傳之孟軻。」夫孔門稱心傳者，惟顏之卓爾、曾之一貫。孟子乃私淑子思者，而特以道統歸之，何哉？蓋戰國之世，邪說横行，仁義充塞，非孟子廓清之功，孔子之道亦幾于晦矣。然則稱其功不在禹下者，此也。其叙道統而勇于自任，殆有所感也夫！
translation_en:
…Fortunate that the surviving influence has not yet faded, one may draw upon what lies nearby and take his Way as one's guiding principle, thereby tracing where the succession of his teaching leads. Although one could not personally encounter the sage's supreme teaching in its flourishing days, in these adjoining lands the spirit of that teaching still survives. Seeking it here, would one not find more than enough instruction? Although one cannot hear all the sage's profound teachings, the walls of his residence remain in sight, and his subtle words can still be investigated. Proceeding along this path, could one not say, “Does not this cultural tradition reside here in me?” Thus, although geography cannot confine one who awakens the world through the Way, the profound subtleties of the teaching of the mind are especially accessible to those nearest at hand. Considering its depth, there must surely be someone who knows through seeing and continues its transmission, like Yu and Gao Yao, who lived in the time of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. Likewise, although one's place of residence cannot restrict one who seeks the sage through the mind, the deeply permeating influence of the sage's virtue is uniquely available to those nearest at hand. By grasping its essential principle, such a person might provide enlightenment for those who know through hearing, like Yi Yin and Lü Shang, who emerged in the ages of Xia and Shang. From this, is not Mengzi's intention to assume this responsibility himself plainly evident?

Master Han said, “Kongzi transmitted it to Meng Ke.” Among Kongzi's disciples, those celebrated for receiving the transmission of the mind were only Yan Hui, with his perception of what “stands towering before me,” and Zeng Shen, with his understanding of the “single thread running through it all.” Mengzi, however, learned indirectly from Zisi. Why, then, is the succession of the Way specifically assigned to him? In the Warring States period, heterodox teachings ran rampant, obstructing benevolence and righteousness. Without Mengzi's achievement in clearing them away, Kongzi's Way would nearly have fallen into obscurity. This, then, is why his achievement is said to be no less than Yu's. In recounting the succession of the Way and boldly taking its responsibility upon himself, he must surely have been moved by this concern!

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
易
九五孚于嘉吉象曰孚于嘉吉位正中也
錢楷
同考試官教諭吳　批〔詮理精到脩詞縝密〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔上下串講甚得經旨〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔通篇無一閒字〕
隨文任賢以成治象復推本於德焉蓋同德相
信致治之本也今九五以德而信賢焉其成功
而獲吉也宜哉此二聖文象交明其義也蓋謂
===
人君欲致天下之治固必先於用賢然賢者可
以虛拘乎哉今隨之九五以陽剛中正之君下
應六二中正之賢則是知二爲可嘉之君子也
推誠以相待而情意與之交孚寄之以股肱心
膂而不秉之以疑貳焉虛已以相從而心神與
之契合置之於左右先後而不間之以形迹焉
如此則信之也篤旣結其篤棐之忱而任之也
專則得其翊翼之助德業成於上下之交而九
功九敘自臻夫豫大之休庶事康於明良之會
punctuated:
易

九五，孚于嘉，吉。象曰：「孚于嘉，吉，位正中也。」

錢楷

同考試官教諭吳批〔詮理精到，脩詞縝密〕
考試官教諭劉批〔上下串講，甚得經旨〕
考試官教諭胡批〔通篇無一閒字〕

隨文任賢以成治，象復推本於德焉。蓋同德相信，致治之本也。今九五以德而信賢焉，其成功而獲吉也宜哉！此二聖文象交明其義也。蓋謂人君欲致天下之治，固必先於用賢，然賢者可以虛拘乎哉？今隨之九五，以陽剛中正之君，下應六二中正之賢，則是知二爲可嘉之君子也。推誠以相待，而情意與之交孚，寄之以股肱心膂，而不秉之以疑貳焉；虛已以相從，而心神與之契合，置之於左右先後，而不間之以形迹焉。如此，則信之也篤，旣結其篤棐之忱；而任之也專，則得其翊翼之助。德業成於上下之交，而九功九敘自臻夫豫大之休；庶事康於明良之會，
translation_en:
Book of Changes

“Nine in the fifth place: Sincerity toward the worthy brings good fortune. The Image says: ‘Sincerity toward the worthy brings good fortune because the position is correct and central.’”

Qian Kai

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “The elucidation of principle is precise and penetrating; the wording is carefully wrought and closely knit.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The connected exposition of the preceding and following passages captures the meaning of the classic very well.”
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “There is not a single superfluous word in the entire piece.”

The line text of Following (Sui) speaks of entrusting the worthy with office to achieve good government; the Image further traces this back to virtue. For shared virtue and mutual trust are the foundation of good government. Now nine in the fifth place trusts the worthy on the strength of virtue. How fitting that it should accomplish its work and obtain good fortune! Thus the two sages, through the line text and the Image, illuminate this meaning together.

The meaning is that a ruler who wishes to bring order to all under Heaven must first employ the worthy. Yet can worthy men be held by empty gestures? Now nine in the fifth place in Following represents a ruler of firm yang character, central and correct, who responds below to the worthy man represented by six in the second place, likewise central and correct. He thus recognizes the second line as a gentleman worthy of esteem. He treats him with utter sincerity, and their feelings and intentions meet in mutual trust. He entrusts him with serving as his arms and legs, heart and backbone, without treating him with suspicion or wavering trust. He humbles himself to follow him, and their minds and spirits accord. He places him beside him and before and behind him, allowing no concern with outward formalities to come between them. In this way, his trust is profound, securing the worthy man’s heartfelt commitment to faithful assistance; and his delegation of responsibility is undivided, gaining his sustaining support. Virtuous achievements are accomplished through the intercourse of ruler and minister, and the nine accomplishments and their orderly arrangement naturally attain the blessings of abundant ease and greatness. All affairs prosper through the meeting of an enlightened ruler and a worthy minister …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
而惟脩惟和永底於豐亨之盛其占之吉也不
亦宜乎此固九五任賢之效也然豈無所本哉
夫子小象申之以爲治之未臻凡以賢之未用
也賢之未信凡以德之未協也今九五得陽剛
之正居上卦之中則無爲以守至正而無反無
側有以全天德之純精一以執厥中而不偏不
倚有以建維皇之極是德立于己而取人之則
以端以我之正取彼之正好爵之縻一出于中
心之願矣君心既純而顯俊之善已備以我之
===
中用彼之中一德之美自協于同心之孚矣五
所以能任其賢者以此否則心有未同德有未
合賢者未必知知而未必信也其能孚于嘉也
知是乎吁觀吉之由於孚嘉則知親賢之爲急
觀孚之由於正中則知脩德之爲本聖人繫隨
九五之義深矣抑考周公作立政稱用人之盛
不曰九德咸事而惓惓于迪知忱恂蓋欲其迪
德翕受以盡取人立政之道也夫子之意卽周
公之意與噫謨明弼諧唐虞所以爲帝交脩爽
punctuated:
而惟脩惟和，永底於豐亨之盛，其占之吉也，不亦宜乎？此固九五任賢之效也，然豈無所本哉？夫子小象申之，以爲治之未臻，凡以賢之未用也；賢之未信，凡以德之未協也。今九五得陽剛之正，居上卦之中，則無爲以守至正，而無反無側，有以全天德之純；精一以執厥中，而不偏不倚，有以建維皇之極。是德立于己，而取人之則以端。以我之正取彼之正，好爵之縻，一出于中心之願矣。君心既純，而顯俊之善已備；以我之中用彼之中，一德之美，自協于同心之孚矣。五所以能任其賢者以此。否則，心有未同，德有未合，賢者未必知，知而未必信也，其能孚于嘉也知是乎？
吁！觀吉之由於孚嘉，則知親賢之爲急；觀孚之由於正中，則知脩德之爲本。聖人繫隨九五之義深矣！抑考周公作《立政》，稱用人之盛，不曰九德咸事，而惓惓于迪知忱恂，蓋欲其迪德翕受，以盡取人立政之道也。夫子之意，卽周公之意與！噫！謨明弼諧，唐虞所以爲帝；交脩爽
translation_en:
…and all is cultivated and brought into harmony, enduringly attaining abundant prosperity. Is it not fitting that its prognostication should be auspicious? This is indeed the effect of employing worthy men at the nine in the fifth place. Yet surely it has a foundation? In the Commentary on the Lesser Images, Confucius elaborates: government has not reached perfection simply because worthy men have not been employed; worthy men have not been trusted simply because virtue has not accorded with theirs. Now the nine in the fifth place possesses the rectitude of firm yang and occupies the center of the upper trigram. Through nonaction it maintains utmost rectitude, without deviation or partiality, thereby preserving the purity of heavenly virtue. Through refinement and singleness of purpose it holds fast to the mean, without bias or inclination, thereby establishing the sovereign’s supreme standard. Thus virtue is established within oneself, and the standard for selecting men is set right. With my own rectitude I select those who are upright: binding them to me with honorable rank proceeds entirely from my heart’s desire. Once the ruler’s heart is pure, the excellence of bringing outstanding men to prominence is fully realized. With my own centrality I employ their centrality: the beauty of shared virtue naturally accords with the mutual trust of united hearts. This is how the fifth line can entrust responsibility to worthy men. Otherwise, if their hearts are not united and their virtues do not accord, worthy men may not even be recognized; even if recognized, they may not be trusted. Could its sincerity toward the good be like this [?]?
Ah! Observing that auspiciousness arises from sincerity toward the good, we understand the urgency of drawing close to worthy men. Observing that sincerity arises from rectitude and centrality, we understand that cultivating virtue is the foundation. Profound indeed is the meaning that the sage attached to the nine in the fifth place of Following! Moreover, consider how the Duke of Zhou, in composing Establishing Government, praised excellence in employing men. Rather than speaking of “all nine virtues being put into service,” he dwelt earnestly on guiding, understanding, sincerity, and trustworthiness. His intention was surely that the ruler should advance virtue and receive worthy men inclusively, thereby fully realizing the Way of selecting men and establishing government. Confucius’s intention was surely the same as the Duke of Zhou’s! Ah! Enlightened counsels and harmonious assistance were what made the rulers of Tang and Yu true emperors; mutual cultivation and enlightened…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
輔商周所以爲王君臣相得相濟之功盛矣哉
夫乾確然示人易矣夫坤隤然示人簡矣
文也者效此者也象也者像此者也
馬三樂

造化顯貞觀之理而聖人因之以作易焉蓋易
知簡能理之顯於貞觀者也聖人作易以立卦
===
爻有不則而像之也哉大傳論卦爻吉凶至此
蓋謂天地者陰陽之實體易書者卦爻之法象
欲知作易之原盍於天地貞觀者觀之乎彼乾
以至健而運乎上固難窮其於穆之微矣然所
以確然示人者惟易焉爾化鼓於無心遂立夫
萬象之有機運於莫測卽開夫羣物之先始而
亨者不可遏也動而直者莫之禦也仰觀于上
而示人以可見者有弗易耶坤以至順而位于
下固難測其含弘之秘矣然其所以隤然示人
punctuated:
輔，商周所以爲王。君臣相得相濟之功盛矣哉！

夫乾確然示人易矣，夫坤隤然示人簡矣。文也者，效此者也；象也者，像此者也。

馬三樂

造化顯貞觀之理，而聖人因之以作《易》焉。蓋易知簡能，理之顯於貞觀者也。聖人作《易》以立卦爻，有不則而像之也哉？《大傳》論卦爻吉凶，至此蓋謂天地者，陰陽之實體；《易》書者，卦爻之法象。欲知作《易》之原，盍於天地貞觀者觀之乎？彼乾以至健而運乎上，固難窮其於穆之微矣。然所以確然示人者，惟易焉爾。化鼓於無心，遂立夫萬象之有；機運於莫測，卽開夫羣物之先。始而亨者，不可遏也；動而直者，莫之禦也。仰觀于上，而示人以可見者，有弗易耶？坤以至順而位于下，固難測其含弘之秘矣。然其所以隤然示人
translation_en:
…assistance: this was how the Shang and Zhou attained kingship. How splendid were the achievements of ruler and ministers in finding accord and aiding one another!

“Qian, firm and steadfast, shows people ease; Kun, yielding and gentle, shows people simplicity. Patterns emulate these; images represent these.”

Ma Sanle

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of Qian and Kun, patterns and images, is exceptionally penetrating and thorough.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔It grasps the purport of purity and stillness, subtlety and precision.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Lucid, polished, classical, and elegant.〕

The workings of creation reveal the principle of constancy made manifest, and the sages followed this in composing the Book of Changes. For knowing through ease and accomplishing through simplicity are this principle revealed in its constant manifestation. When the sages composed the Changes and established its hexagrams and lines, could they have failed to take this as their model and represent it? At this point in its discussion of the hexagrams and lines and their auspicious and inauspicious outcomes, the Great Commentary means that heaven and earth are the actual embodiments of yin and yang, while the book of the Changes presents their models and images in hexagrams and lines. If we wish to understand the origins of the Changes, should we not look to the constant manifestations of heaven and earth?

Qian moves above with utmost vigor. Certainly, it is difficult to fathom the subtleties of its profound, unceasing activity. Yet what it steadfastly shows people is simply ease. Transformation proceeds without conscious intent, and thus brings the myriad forms into existence; its workings move unfathomably, and thereby initiate the multitude of things. What originates and flourishes cannot be checked; what moves straight ahead cannot be resisted. Looking upward, is anything that it visibly shows people other than ease?

Kun occupies its place below with utmost compliance. Certainly, it is difficult to fathom the mysteries of its all-embracing vastness. Yet the way it shows itself to people, yielding and gentle…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
者以簡焉爾承天以行無煩於創始之力隨帝
以入惟安夫後得之常廣生焉而無所勞也效
法焉而不自作也俯察于下而示人以可見者
有弗簡耶此固造化貞常之理而實已具乎畫
前之易矣聖人作易有弗本於是哉彼發揮於
剛柔文固生矣而奇偶之畫實所以藏造化之
秘一而實者效夫乾之易也二而虛者效夫坤
之簡也是雖剛柔止於對待之體而究其精蘊
則健順之至理已默寓于時成之中矣爻非所
===
以效此者耶觀變於陰陽卦固立矣而消長之
妙實所以通神明之德陽之自消而息者像夫
乾之易也陰之自消而息者像夫坤之簡也是
雖陰陽止於相雜之文而擬諸形容則動靜之
妙用已模寫於全體之內矣象非所以像此者
耶至此則知造化所以開易書之原易書所以
闡造化之妙吉凶貞勝之理又可以他求哉嗟
夫天下之理一而已矣顯於天地載於易書而
未甞不備於吾心也人能體此易簡以至於可
punctuated: 者，以簡焉爾。承天以行，無煩於創始之力；隨帝以入，惟安夫後得之常。廣生焉而無所勞也，效法焉而不自作也。俯察于下，而示人以可見者，有弗簡耶？此固造化貞常之理，而實已具乎畫前之易矣。聖人作易，有弗本於是哉？彼發揮於剛柔，文固生矣，而奇偶之畫，實所以藏造化之秘。一而實者，效夫乾之易也；二而虛者，效夫坤之簡也。是雖剛柔止於對待之體，而究其精蘊，則健順之至理，已默寓于時成之中矣。爻非所以效此者耶？觀變於陰陽，卦固立矣，而消長之妙，實所以通神明之德。陽之自消而息者，像夫乾之易也；陰之自消而息者，像夫坤之簡也。是雖陰陽止於相雜之文，而擬諸形容，則動靜之妙用，已模寫於全體之內矣。象非所以像此者耶？至此，則知造化所以開易書之原，易書所以闡造化之妙，吉凶貞勝之理，又可以他求哉？嗟夫！天下之理，一而已矣。顯於天地，載於易書，而未甞不備於吾心也。人能體此易簡，以至於可
translation_en:
…is simply through simplicity. Following Heaven in its activity, it need not expend the effort of initiating things; following the Lord on High as it enters into action, it rests content with the constant order of attaining its place by following. It brings forth things abundantly without toil; it follows the pattern without acting on its own initiative. Looking downward and examining what it visibly reveals to people, is there anything that is not simple? This is indeed the constant principle of creation and transformation, already fully present in the Changes before the lines of the hexagrams were drawn. When the sage composed the Changes, could he have failed to take this as his foundation?

Through the unfolding of the firm and the yielding, patterns indeed arise; yet the odd and even strokes are precisely what contain the secrets of creation and transformation. The single, solid stroke models the ease of Qian; the divided stroke, open in the middle, models the simplicity of Kun. Although firmness and yielding constitute merely a structure of paired opposites, when their deepest significance is investigated, the ultimate principles of vigor and compliance are already silently lodged within what takes form in its proper time. Are not the lines of the hexagrams the means of modeling this?

By observing changes in yin and yang, the hexagrams are indeed established; yet the subtle workings of waning and waxing are precisely what communicate the potency of spiritual intelligence. Yang, in its spontaneous waning and waxing, images the ease of Qian; yin, in its spontaneous waning and waxing, images the simplicity of Kun. Although yin and yang constitute merely an intermingled pattern, when represented through shapes and forms, the subtle workings of movement and stillness are already depicted within the whole. Are not the images the means of representing this?

At this point we understand how creation and transformation provide the source of the Book of Changes, and how the Book of Changes elucidates the subtleties of creation and transformation. Could the principle governing the constant alternation in the ascendancy of good and ill fortune be sought elsewhere? Ah! The principle of all under Heaven is but one. It is manifest in Heaven and Earth and recorded in the Book of Changes, yet it has always been fully present in our own minds. If people can embody this ease and simplicity, thereby reaching the capacity to…

天地其不愧矣故曰易簡之善配至德

大臣告君謹於用人，因推取善之要焉。夫德統天下之善也，用人謹而取善有要，其斯以爲一德之全功與！伊尹告君，意謂有常固新德之要，用人實新德之資。吾王欲成一德之功，可不致謹於用人哉？彼承綜理之司者，庶官也，必材德之全者，然後論而官之焉。膺輔弼之寄者，左右也，必道德之隆者，然後任而相之焉。蓋以此臣
translation_en:
… enduring and capable of greatness, establishing one's place between them, then the principles of the Changes reside not in the hexagrams and their lines but in one's own heart. One may thus stand without shame before Heaven and Earth. Hence the saying: “The goodness of ease and simplicity matches the highest virtue.”

Book of Documents
“Appoint to office only the worthy and talented; choose only suitable men to serve at your side. Ministers serve virtue in their service to those above, and the people in their service to those below. Be painstaking and cautious; maintain harmony and unity. In cultivating virtue, there is no fixed teacher: take goodness as your teacher. Goodness has no fixed master: bring it into accord with the attainment of unity.”
Wu Daochuan
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔The explanation of the Documents is clear and penetrating; the wording is polished and clean.〕
Associate Examiner Xiao, School Instructor, comments: 〔Neither prolix nor superficial. Select it.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Concise language and clear meaning.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and apposite.〕

A great minister counsels his ruler to exercise care in employing men, and thereby develops the essential principle of adopting what is good. Virtue encompasses all the goodness under Heaven. If one exercises care in employing men and grasps the essential principle of adopting goodness, would this not constitute the complete achievement of unified virtue? In counseling his ruler, Yi Yin meant that constancy is indeed essential to renewing virtue, while employing men supplies the means of renewing it. If our king wishes to achieve unified virtue, can he fail to exercise the utmost care in employing men? Those charged with managing affairs are the various officials: only after finding men complete in both ability and virtue should one assess them and appoint them to office. Those entrusted with assisting and supporting the ruler are the men at his side: only after finding men of eminent moral attainment should one entrust them with responsibility and make them his chief ministers.
