title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
也論思啓沃上焉君德攸關所以端萬化之原
者此也懷保康濟下焉民生攸繫所以成咸和
之治者此也故必於未用也則其難其慎而遴
選之惟嚴於既用也則惟和惟一而誠意之交
孚然用人固所以取善也而豈無其要哉蓋理
本散於萬殊也苟執一而師之或失則狹矣必
大虛受之咸而會萬理於悉備廣師資之益而
集衆善於無方則舍已從人所以取善于博者
不其盡乎理實會於一本也苟執一而主之或
===
失則泛矣必融會于眞積之久而貞一者有以
敦其化貫通于自得之後而資深者有以逢其
原則百慮一致所以會善于約者不其精乎夫
然則善之取也爲有要而人之用也爲不虛德
其有不一哉抑舜之命禹曰惟精惟一伊尹告
太甲曰終始惟一信斯言也則人君事天治民
未有不本于一德者吁老成忠國於此可見
小大之臣咸懷忠良
臧惟一
punctuated:
也，論思啓沃，上焉君德攸關，所以端萬化之原者此也；懷保康濟，下焉民生攸繫，所以成咸和之治者此也。故必於未用也，則其難其慎，而遴選之惟嚴；於既用也，則惟和惟一，而誠意之交孚。然用人固所以取善也，而豈無其要哉？蓋理本散於萬殊也，苟執一而師之，或失則狹矣。必大虛受之咸，而會萬理於悉備，廣師資之益，而集衆善於無方，則舍已從人，所以取善于博者，不其盡乎？理實會於一本也，苟執一而主之，或失則泛矣。必融會于眞積之久，而貞一者有以敦其化；貫通于自得之後，而資深者有以逢其原，則百慮一致，所以會善于約者，不其精乎？夫然，則善之取也爲有要，而人之用也爲不虛，德其有不一哉？抑舜之命禹曰：「惟精惟一。」伊尹告太甲曰：「終始惟一。」信斯言也，則人君事天治民，未有不本于一德者。吁！老成忠國，於此可見。

小大之臣咸懷忠良

臧惟一
translation_en:
…these ministers, through deliberation and reflection, enlighten and nourish their ruler. Above, the ruler’s virtue depends upon them: this is how the source of all transforming influence is set right. Through cherishing and protecting the people, bringing them peace and relief, they sustain the people’s livelihood below: this is how government that brings harmony to all is achieved. Thus, before employing them, the ruler must regard the choice as difficult and exercise caution, selecting them with the utmost rigor. Once they are employed, ruler and ministers must be harmonious and united, with sincerity and mutual trust between them. Employing men is indeed a means of acquiring goodness; but can there be no essential principle governing it?

Principle is originally dispersed among the myriad particulars. If one clings to a single instance and takes it as one’s teacher, the resulting error may be narrowness. One must enlarge one’s capacity to receive everything with an open mind, bringing together the myriad principles in their completeness; broaden the benefits of learning from others, and gather every kind of goodness without restriction. Then, by setting oneself aside and following others, will one not acquire goodness in all its breadth to the fullest extent? Yet principle in truth converges upon a single root. If one clings to one thing and makes it one’s guide, the resulting error may be diffuseness [?]. One must integrate understanding through long and genuine accumulation, so that steadfast unity can deepen its transforming effect; achieve comprehensive understanding through personal realization, so that deeply grounded learning can draw upon its source. Then, with a hundred deliberations converging upon one end, will one not attain the utmost refinement in bringing goodness together within its essentials?

If this is so, the acquisition of goodness will have its essential principle, and the employment of men will not be in vain. How could virtue then fail to be undivided? Moreover, Shun charged Yu, saying, “Be discerning; be single-minded.” Yi Yin told Tai Jia, “From beginning to end, remain single-minded.” If these words are indeed true, no ruler has ever served Heaven and governed the people without taking undivided virtue as his foundation. Ah! Here one can see the seasoned statesman’s loyalty to his country.

“The Ministers, Great and Small, All Cherish Loyalty and Goodness”

Zang Weiyi

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陳　批〔講感懷忠良處明切〕
同考試官學正皇甫　批〔意婉而明詞莊而雅〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔善形容當時忠良意思〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔簡明〕
觀聖世之羣臣皆以道而事君焉甚矣臣道莫
大乎忠良也聖世大小之臣皆懷此以事君焉
其斯以爲純臣矣乎周王舉之以告臣也蓋曰
守位固以嗣德爲先脩德則以賢臣爲輔彼聰
明齊聖文武之德盛矣宜無賴於諸臣之夾輔
===
也然以當時之臣言之自受一命之微有小臣
焉總百僚之位有大臣焉分雖有尊卑均之從
王事也使事有一之不盡其職即非忠良矣今
則合小大而一心隨其所在皆堅勿欺之念協
尊卑而共濟因其所任每殫精白之誠以廸彝
教在五臣固弼直乎文王也庶位之有正有事
者咸思竭忠以盡其倫以廸有祿在四臣固昭
明乎武王也三千之一心一德者咸思篤棐以
行其義慶遭逢之盛莫不以忠而對揚乎天子
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陳　批〔講感懷忠良處明切〕
同考試官學正皇甫　批〔意婉而明詞莊而雅〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔善形容當時忠良意思〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔簡明〕

觀聖世之羣臣，皆以道而事君焉。甚矣，臣道莫大乎忠良也！聖世大小之臣，皆懷此以事君焉，其斯以爲純臣矣乎！周王舉之以告臣也，蓋曰：守位固以嗣德爲先，脩德則以賢臣爲輔。彼聰明齊聖，文武之德盛矣，宜無賴於諸臣之夾輔也。然以當時之臣言之，自受一命之微，有小臣焉；總百僚之位，有大臣焉。分雖有尊卑，均之從王事也。使事有一之不盡其職，即非忠良矣。今則合小大而一心，隨其所在，皆堅勿欺之念；協尊卑而共濟，因其所任，每殫精白之誠。以廸彝教，在五臣固弼直乎文王也，庶位之有正有事者，咸思竭忠以盡其倫；以廸有祿，在四臣固昭明乎武王也，三千之一心一德者，咸思篤棐以行其義。慶遭逢之盛，莫不以忠而對揚乎天子
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: 〔The discussion of what moves them to cherish loyalty and goodness is clear and incisive.〕
Associate Examiner Huangfu, Instructor (xuezheng), comments: 〔The thought is subtle yet clear; the language dignified and elegant.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: 〔Skillfully portrays the spirit of loyalty and goodness at that time.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: 〔Concise and clear.〕

Observe how the assembled ministers of a sagely age all serve their ruler according to the Way. How profound this is! In the way of a minister, nothing is greater than loyalty and goodness. The ministers of a sagely age, great and small alike, all cherish these qualities in serving their ruler. Surely they may thus be regarded as ministers of unalloyed virtue! The king of Zhou cited this in addressing his ministers. His meaning was this: in preserving the throne, continuing the virtue of one’s predecessors must indeed come first; in cultivating virtue, one must have worthy ministers as helpers. Intelligent, discerning, wise, and sagely, Kings Wen and Wu possessed abundant virtue. It would seem that they had no need for the supporting assistance of their ministers.

Yet, speaking of the ministers of that time, there were lesser ministers, beginning with those of the humble first rank of appointment, and there were great ministers, occupying positions that oversaw the hundred officials. Though their stations differed in dignity, all alike attended to the king’s affairs. If in even one matter they failed to fulfill their duties, they could not be called loyal and good. Here, however, great and small united with a single purpose: wherever they served, all held firmly to the resolve never to deceive their ruler. High and low worked in harmony toward a common end: whatever their responsibilities, each gave the fullest expression to a sincerity pure and unsullied. In advancing the constant teachings, the five ministers certainly supported and corrected King Wen; throughout the many offices, the chiefs and those charged with duties all sought to exhaust their loyalty in fulfilling their proper relationships. In guiding the ruler blessed with Heaven’s favor, the four ministers certainly illuminated King Wu’s virtue; the three thousand who shared one heart and one virtue all sought to offer steadfast assistance in carrying out their righteous duties. Rejoicing in the flourishing age they had been fortunate enough to encounter, all loyally acknowledged and extolled the Son of Heaven…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
凡可以養聰明齊聖之體者無不爲也外此而
身使之圖有弗恤焉感知遇之隆莫不以良而
媢嫉于一人凡可以擴聰明齊聖之用者無不
至也外此而謀利之私有弗預焉如是則一人
元良在上庶聖脩之極百官脩輔在下盡有相
之能而周之治於斯爲盛矣今予紹文武之統
者爾羣臣可不效忠良以事之哉大抵君臣者
天地不可逃之分忠良者人臣不容已之心有
所畏而後懷有所覬而後懷皆非懷之至者也
懷吾心不容自已之道以盡天地不可逃之分
斯可以明君父之義斯可以語聖世之忠臣
詩
王奮厥武如震如怒進厥虎臣闞如虓虎
鋪敦淮濆仍執醜虜截彼淮浦王師之
所
王象坤
同考試官教諭區　批〔布格整密造詞雅健當時〕
王師之盛赫然在目
punctuated:
凡可以養聰明齊聖之體者，無不爲也。外此而身使之圖，有弗恤焉。感知遇之隆，莫不以良而媢嫉于一人，凡可以擴聰明齊聖之用者，無不至也。外此而謀利之私，有弗預焉。如是，則一人元良在上，庶聖脩之極；百官脩輔在下，盡有相之能，而周之治於斯爲盛矣。今予紹文武之統者，爾羣臣可不效忠良以事之哉？大抵君臣者，天地不可逃之分；忠良者，人臣不容已之心。有所畏而後懷，有所覬而後懷，皆非懷之至者也。懷吾心不容自已之道，以盡天地不可逃之分，斯可以明君父之義，斯可以語聖世之忠臣。

詩

王奮厥武，如震如怒。進厥虎臣，闞如虓虎。鋪敦淮濆，仍執醜虜。截彼淮浦，王師之所。

王象坤

同考試官教諭區批：〔布格整密，造詞雅健，當時〕王師之盛，赫然在目。
translation_en:
…They do everything that can nurture the substance of the ruler’s intelligence and sagely discernment. Beyond this, they give no thought to schemes for their own advancement [?]. Moved by the extraordinary favor of being recognized and employed, all bring their goodness to bear upon the One Man—though the transcription here reads “envy and resent” [?]. They leave nothing undone that can extend the exercise of his intelligence and sagely discernment. Beyond this, they take no part in private pursuits of profit. Thus, with the One Man supremely good above, sagely cultivation may reach its utmost [?]; with the hundred officials diligently assisting below, they fully exercise their capacity to aid him. Through this, Zhou’s government attained its flourishing condition. “Now that I succeed to the rule of Kings Wen and Wu, can you, my assembled ministers, fail to serve me with loyalty and goodness?” In general, the relationship between ruler and minister is a duty that cannot be escaped anywhere between Heaven and Earth; loyalty and goodness are impulses that a minister’s heart cannot suppress. Attachment arising only from fear, or only from hopes of gain, is never attachment in its fullest sense. Cherishing the Way that our hearts cannot help but follow, and thereby fulfilling the duty that cannot be escaped between Heaven and Earth: this makes clear our obligations toward the ruler as father, and qualifies one to be called a loyal minister of a sagely age.

The Book of Odes

The king roused his martial might,
Like thunder, like raging wrath.
He advanced his tiger-like ministers,
Roaring like fierce tigers.
They deployed in force along the Huai’s banks,
And seized the enemy captives.
They brought order to the shores of the Huai,
Where the royal army was stationed.

Wang Xiangkun

Comment by Associate Examiner Ou, an Instructor: “The composition is closely and neatly structured, its diction elegant and vigorous. The magnificence of the royal army of that time stands vividly before our eyes.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭楊　批〔將士之勇皆本之周王深得詩人之旨〕
同考試官教諭施　批〔鋪叙伐遠之威如得之親覽〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔峻拔不凡〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔謹嚴亦善說詩者〕
詩人美王者之撲夷陳師而得致勝之道也甚
矣兵之所尚者威也周王陳師而上下咸奮焉
夫誰與爲敵哉常武美宣王伐淮夷而作也若
===
曰夷狄王者所不治也顧豈與之計勝負之數
哉惟夫淮夷倡亂則所以蓄威而觀兵者自不
容已矣故即其至徐而言之彼征伐自天子出
將士所視以作止其氣者也今則銳志於攘夷
而天威肅將有如雷之震焉而戢纘夫赫怒之
師聲罪以服遠而神武布昭有如天之怒焉而
克紹夫維揚之烈信爲兵以義動而足以攄華
夏之氣矣由是進厥虎臣以向敵則咸以天子
之心爲心而忠憤激烈蓋將以威懾淮夷而使
punctuated:
同考試官教諭楊，批〔將士之勇，皆本之周王，深得詩人之旨。〕
同考試官教諭施，批〔鋪叙伐遠之威，如得之親覽。〕
考試官教諭劉，批〔峻拔不凡。〕
考試官教諭胡，批〔謹嚴，亦善說詩者。〕
詩人美王者之撲夷陳師而得致勝之道也。甚矣，兵之所尚者威也！周王陳師，而上下咸奮焉，夫誰與爲敵哉？《常武》，美宣王伐淮夷而作也。若曰：夷狄，王者所不治也，顧豈與之計勝負之數哉？惟夫淮夷倡亂，則所以蓄威而觀兵者，自不容已矣。故即其至徐而言之，彼征伐自天子出，將士所視以作止其氣者也。今則銳志於攘夷，而天威肅將，有如雷之震焉，而戢纘夫赫怒之師；聲罪以服遠，而神武布昭，有如天之怒焉，而克紹夫維揚之烈。信爲兵以義動，而足以攄華夏之氣矣。由是進厥虎臣以向敵，則咸以天子之心爲心，而忠憤激烈，蓋將以威懾淮夷而使
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: 〔The courage of the commanders and soldiers is traced entirely to the king of Zhou. This deeply grasps the poet’s intent.〕
Associate Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: 〔The imposing might of the campaign against distant peoples is recounted as though personally witnessed.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Lofty and outstanding; far from ordinary.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Careful and rigorous: this, too, is someone skilled at interpreting the Odes.〕
The poet praises the king for deploying his army to crush the Yi and thereby attaining the means to victory. How greatly warfare prizes awe-inspiring might! When the king of Zhou arrayed his army, those above and below all roused themselves. Who could stand against him? “Constant Martial Might” (Chang wu) was composed to praise King Xuan’s campaign against the Huai Yi. It is as though the poem says: The Yi and Di lie outside the king’s governance; why should he reckon the odds of victory or defeat against them? Yet when the Huai Yi fomented disorder, gathering his might and displaying his troops became unavoidable.
Thus, speaking specifically of his arrival in Xu: punitive expeditions proceed from the Son of Heaven, to whom commanders and soldiers look in rousing or restraining their fighting spirit. Now he set his resolve firmly upon repelling the Yi and solemnly deployed his heavenly might, like the thunder’s shock, gathering and carrying forward [?] that army of blazing wrath. He proclaimed their crimes to subdue those far away, and his divine martial power shone forth like Heaven’s anger, successfully continuing the glorious achievement of martial might exalted. Truly, these were troops set in motion by righteousness, sufficient to give full expression to the spirit of Huaxia.
Thereupon he advanced his tiger-like ministers to face the enemy. All took the Son of Heaven’s purpose as their own, their loyal indignation burning fiercely. They intended to overawe the Huai Yi with their might and make them…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
之莫敢攖者其有量敵而後進者乎厚集其陳
於淮瀆則仗以天子之武爲武而就執醜虜蓋
將以勢示淮夷而使之莫敢抗者其有慮勝而
後會者乎夫君臣同心而將卒用命雖不戰而
可以屈人之兵矣是以截彼淮浦六師之整於
卿士者於是乎止齊焉以決其戰勝之功而謀
夏者自無遑於蔿食師旅之戒於司馬者於是
乎止齊焉以定其攻取之略而干正者又何暇
於整居不爲王師之所乎夫陳兵而威武之著
===
如此淮夷何有于不服而南國何患于不惠也
哉抑謂宣王中興還定安集本以尋如傷者定
之美也而於戰伐每致意焉豈其好動民于險
哉蓋匪茹肆侮不得已而應之其所以勞天下
者正所以安天下也卒之六月薄伐釆芑來威
常武之功成于允塞則其與民休息之意又何
嘗不寓其中此其所以能光昭文武之烈也與
赫赫厥聲濯濯厥靈壽考且寧
張燭
punctuated:
之莫敢攖者，其有量敵而後進者乎？厚集其陳於淮瀆，則仗以天子之武爲武，而就執醜虜，蓋將以勢示淮夷而使之莫敢抗者，其有慮勝而後會者乎？夫君臣同心而將卒用命，雖不戰而可以屈人之兵矣。是以截彼淮浦，六師之整於卿士者，於是乎止齊焉，以決其戰勝之功，而謀夏者自無遑於蔿食；師旅之戒於司馬者，於是乎止齊焉，以定其攻取之略，而干正者又何暇於整居，不爲王師之所乎？夫陳兵而威武之著如此，淮夷何有于不服，而南國何患于不惠也哉？抑謂宣王中興，還定安集，本以尋如傷者定之美也，而於戰伐每致意焉，豈其好動民于險哉？蓋匪茹肆侮，不得已而應之，其所以勞天下者，正所以安天下也。卒之《六月》薄伐，《釆芑》來威，《常武》之功成于允塞，則其與民休息之意，又何嘗不寓其中？此其所以能光昭文武之烈也與！
赫赫厥聲，濯濯厥靈，壽考且寧。
張燭
translation_en:
…so that none dared oppose them: would they first gauge the enemy’s strength before advancing? They massed their formations along the Huai River, relying on the Son of Heaven’s martial power as their own, and proceeded to seize the vile captives. Intending to display their strength to the Huai tribes so that none dared resist, would they first calculate their chances of victory before assembling? When ruler and ministers are of one mind, and commanders and soldiers obey their orders, they can subdue another’s army even without fighting.
Thus they brought order to the banks of the Huai. The Six Armies, marshalled by the high ministers, there halted in ordered ranks to secure victory in battle; those plotting against the Chinese realm naturally had no leisure to prepare their provisions [?]. The troops, admonished by the Minister of War, there halted in ordered ranks to settle their plans of attack and conquest. How could those who defied rightful rule have time to put their settlements in order and keep them from becoming quarters for the royal army? With troops arrayed and martial might displayed in this way, how could the Huai tribes fail to submit? What fear could there be that the southern states would not comply?
Yet King Xuan’s restoration brought settled government and peace back to the people, originally pursuing the excellence of caring for them as though they were injured and bringing them stability [?]. Why, then, did he repeatedly give his attention to warfare? Surely he did not delight in exposing the people to danger! Rather, the enemy failed to consider its own strength and recklessly offered insult; he had no choice but to respond. The very means by which he put all under Heaven to toil were the means by which he brought them peace. In the end, the punitive expedition in “The Sixth Month” (Liu yue), the display of might in “Gathering Millet” (Cai qi), and the achievement of complete success in “Constant Martial Prowess” (Chang wu)—did these not all embody his intention to let the people rest and recuperate? This was how he could gloriously illuminate the achievements of Kings Wen and Wu!
“Resplendent was his renown; manifest was his spiritual might; long-lived and at peace.”
Zhang Zhu

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭區　批〔赫赫濯濯皆詩人善形容名〕
〔威顯赫處微子孰能模寫至此〕
同考試官教諭楊　批〔詩人頌君本意正在得壽字〕
〔中興之盛此作亦場中之超絕者矣〕
同考試官教諭施　批〔以壽考且寧承上二句甚〕
〔是〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔文有思致〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔意足體莊〕
詩人頌商王極名威之著而享永年之慶也夫
===
名威竝著而復久道以成之則致治之盛無以
加矣此商王之中興所以爲可頌與殷武詩人
陳之於登歌之際意謂國家所恃以享靈長之
祚者恒必有不世出之主久于其道以撝恢復
之功我商何幸而有此湯孫之中興乎何則人
君之聯屬天下其實繫者其名必宋甚哉聲之
貴於顯盛也湯孫則敬天畏民自得乎敷譽之
道荊楚由是而通道焉諸侯由是而承聽焉德
音孔昭而爲天下所共聞矣厥聲何赫赫耶人
punctuated:
同考試官教諭區，批〔赫赫濯濯，皆詩人善形容名〕〔威顯赫處，微子孰能模寫至此？〕
同考試官教諭楊，批〔詩人頌君本意，正在得壽字〕〔中興之盛，此作亦場中之超絕者矣。〕
同考試官教諭施，批〔以壽考且寧承上二句，甚〕〔是。〕
考試官教諭劉，批〔文有思致。〕
考試官教諭胡，批〔意足體莊。〕
詩人頌商王極名威之著，而享永年之慶也。夫名威竝著，而復久道以成之，則致治之盛無以加矣。此商王之中興所以爲可頌與！殷武詩人陳之於登歌之際，意謂國家所恃以享靈長之祚者，恒必有不世出之主，久于其道，以撝恢復之功。我商何幸而有此湯孫之中興乎！何則？人君之聯屬天下，其實繫者，其名必宋。甚哉，聲之貴於顯盛也！湯孫則敬天畏民，自得乎敷譽之道。荊楚由是而通道焉，諸侯由是而承聽焉，德音孔昭，而爲天下所共聞矣。厥聲何赫赫耶！人
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Ou, Instructor, comments: “Both ‘resplendent’ and ‘radiant’ show the poet’s skill in depicting the manifest brilliance of reputation and might. Who but you could portray it so well?”
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “The poet’s underlying purpose in praising his ruler lies precisely in capturing, through the word ‘longevity,’ the splendor of the restoration. This composition, too, is an outstanding work among those in the examination.”
Associate Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: “It is entirely right to take ‘long-lived and at peace’ as continuing the preceding two lines.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The composition displays thoughtful refinement.”
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “The ideas are fully developed, and the form is dignified.”
The poet praises the king of Shang for attaining the utmost distinction in reputation and might, and for enjoying the blessing of long life. When reputation and might are both manifest, and steadfast adherence to the Way brings them to fulfillment, the splendor of good government can rise no higher. Is this not why the Shang king’s restoration deserves praise? The poet of ‘Martial Yin’ presented this at the singing in the ceremonial hall. His meaning was that, for a state to enjoy enduring blessings, it must always depend upon a ruler such as appears but rarely, who perseveres in his Way to advance the work of restoration. How fortunate was our Shang to experience this restoration under Tang’s descendant!
Why is this so? In binding all under Heaven together, what truly holds them to the ruler is his reputation [the wording 必宋 is doubtful]. How precious it is that his renown should be illustrious! Tang’s descendant revered Heaven and held the people in awe, thus naturally attaining the way to spread his good name. Through this, Jingchu opened its roads to him, and the feudal lords received and heeded his commands. The fame of his virtue shone brilliantly and was heard throughout all under Heaven. How resplendent was his renown! The people…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
生之鼓舞聳動其德深者其威始著甚哉靈之
難於光明也湯孫則撥亂反正已豫乎建極之
原觀之侯服而順治焉觀之夷服而威嚴焉皇
風丕振而為天下所共見矣厥靈何濯濯耶夫
有是赫赫之聲而使無壽以享之則其聲易竆
有是濯濯之靈而使無壽以維之則其靈或替
今則嘉靖殷邦之主有以克當乎天心使之必
得其壽而凝鼎命於無疆恭默思道之君有以
昭受乎大順又必貽之以安而履帝位於不疚
===
則國家之元氣益以固雖無意於近名而名不
朽國家之神氣益以培雖無心於作威而威日
競矣中興之烈孰有大於此哉此後人之登歌
所以不能已於揄揚也與嗚呼帝王之興雖有
天命然未有無故而能致天下之治者高宗振
起式微應運光復其始終典學乃建立之本也
詩人撻武之歌何徒侈其功業之盛而不及其
本乎蓋宗廟升歌功成而作也尚論高宗者必
合說命而觀之而後其中興之盛始備
punctuated:
生之鼓舞聳動，其德深者，其威始著。甚哉，靈之難於光明也！湯孫則撥亂反正，已豫乎建極之原。觀之侯服而順治焉，觀之夷服而威嚴焉，皇風丕振而為天下所共見矣。厥靈何濯濯耶！夫有是赫赫之聲，而使無壽以享之，則其聲易竆；有是濯濯之靈，而使無壽以維之，則其靈或替。今則嘉靖殷邦之主，有以克當乎天心，使之必得其壽，而凝鼎命於無疆；恭默思道之君，有以昭受乎大順，又必貽之以安，而履帝位於不疚。則國家之元氣益以固，雖無意於近名而名不朽；國家之神氣益以培，雖無心於作威而威日競矣。中興之烈，孰有大於此哉！此後人之登歌，所以不能已於揄揚也與！

嗚呼！帝王之興，雖有天命，然未有無故而能致天下之治者。高宗振起式微，應運光復，其始終典學，乃建立之本也。詩人撻武之歌，何徒侈其功業之盛而不及其本乎？蓋宗廟升歌，功成而作也。尚論高宗者，必合《說命》而觀之，而後其中興之盛始備。
translation_en:
…in inspiring and stirring the people, only when a ruler’s virtue is profound does his majesty become manifest. How difficult it is to make spiritual power shine forth! Tang’s descendant quelled disorder and restored proper rule, having already laid the groundwork for establishing the supreme standard. Look at the domain of the lords: there was obedient government. Look at the domain of the Yi peoples: there was awe-inspiring authority. His august influence flourished mightily and became visible to all under Heaven. How resplendent was his spiritual power! Yet if he possessed such illustrious renown but lacked the longevity to enjoy it, that renown would readily come to an end; if he possessed such resplendent spiritual power but lacked the longevity to sustain it, that power might decline. Now the ruler who brought good order and peace to the state of Yin could fully accord with Heaven’s heart, so that Heaven assured him long life and made his dynastic mandate endure without limit. The sovereign who reverently kept silence and pondered the Way could illustriously receive Heaven’s great favor; Heaven would also surely bestow peace upon him, so that he occupied the imperial throne free from affliction. Thus the state’s vital force grew ever firmer: though he had no intention of seeking fame, his fame was imperishable. The state’s spiritual force was increasingly nurtured: though he had no thought of displaying might, his majesty grew stronger each day. What achievement of restoration could surpass this? This is why later generations, singing in the temple hall, could not cease extolling him!

Alas! Though the rise of emperors and kings rests upon Heaven’s mandate, none has ever brought order to all under Heaven without a cause. Gaozong revived a declining dynasty and, responding to his appointed time, restored its glory. His unwavering devotion to learning was the foundation of what he established. Why, then, does the poet’s song of martial prowess merely celebrate the grandeur of his achievements without touching upon their foundation? It is because songs performed in the ancestral temple hall were composed after the achievements had been accomplished. Those who discuss Gaozong of old must read this song together with the Charge to Yue (Yue ming); only then will the full splendor of his restoration become apparent.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
春秋
夏公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男
曹伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕
苗應元
同考試官教諭錢　批〔詞嚴義正凛然君臣之分予其〕
〔遂於經學者〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔筆法嚴毅〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔據傳成文大分自昭〕
春秋紀重臣與好必常詞以謹大分焉蓋分莫
嚴於君臣也經故於葵丘之會而常詞以待宰
孔與且葵丘曷為而會也齊桓偕六國之君脩
九合之好而有是會爾是役也宰孔寔承王命
而賜胙于桓焉然今日之宰孔與前此之宰咺
一也而獨謂之宰周公焉則是統百官而均四
海位兼師保之崇亮天工以弼一人職專端揆
之寄其任重矣經曷不循殊會之例而顧常詞
以紀之耶蓋君臣者天地之大義而尊卑者人
道之常經彼孔雖貴矣非盡人之臣與吾知位
punctuated:
春秋

夏，公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕

苗應元

同考試官教諭錢批〔詞嚴義正，凛然君臣之分，予其〕〔遂於經學者〕
考試官教諭劉批〔筆法嚴毅〕
考試官教諭胡批〔據傳成文，大分自昭〕

春秋紀重臣與好，必常詞以謹大分焉。蓋分莫嚴於君臣也，經故於葵丘之會而常詞以待宰孔與？且葵丘曷為而會也？齊桓偕六國之君，脩九合之好而有是會爾。是役也，宰孔寔承王命而賜胙于桓焉。然今日之宰孔與前此之宰咺一也，而獨謂之宰周公焉，則是統百官而均四海，位兼師保之崇；亮天工以弼一人，職專端揆之寄，其任重矣。經曷不循殊會之例，而顧常詞以紀之耶？蓋君臣者天地之大義，而尊卑者人道之常經。彼孔雖貴矣，非盡人之臣與？吾知位
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

In summer, the duke met with the chief minister, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi〕

Miao Yingyuan

Associate Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: 〔“The language is stern and the principles correct; the distinction between ruler and minister commands awe. I commend him as one〕〔accomplished in classical learning [?].”〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔“The manner of writing is stern and resolute.”〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔“The composition rests on the commentary; the great distinction becomes clear of itself.”〕

When the Spring and Autumn Annals records a high minister’s participation in friendly relations among states, it invariably uses its ordinary wording to safeguard the great distinction. For no distinction is more inviolable than that between ruler and minister. Is this why the Classic treats Chief Minister Kong with ordinary wording at the meeting at Kuiqiu? And for what purpose was the meeting at Kuiqiu held? Duke Huan of Qi joined the rulers of six states to renew the amity of their nine assemblies: that was all that occasioned this meeting. On this mission, Chief Minister Kong indeed acted upon the king’s command to bestow sacrificial meat upon Duke Huan. Yet Chief Minister Kong here was no different from Chief Minister Xuan earlier, while he alone is called “the chief minister, the Duke of Zhou.” This means that he presided over the hundred officials and brought order throughout the Four Seas, his position combining the eminence of preceptor and guardian. He assisted in Heaven’s work to support the One Man, his office bearing the particular trust vested in the chief minister. His responsibilities were weighty indeed. Why, then, does the Classic not follow its precedent of distinguishing such meetings, but instead record him in ordinary wording?

The relationship between ruler and minister is a great principle of Heaven and Earth, and the distinction between superior and inferior is an enduring rule of human conduct. Though Kong was exalted, was he not wholly another’s minister? I know that his position …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
冢宰而爵上公固云尊矣然即其用舍則有進
退之節焉而篤棐而靖共皆臣子之所有事也
語其出入則有均勞之義焉而效忠而宣力皆
臣職之所當爲也噫吾於伯禹見司空之命焉
嘗進宅乎百揆矣於姬旦見師保之職焉嘗下
均乎四海矣惟玆宰孔亦猶伯禹之於虞也姬
旦之於周也夫固位極人臣者耳是豈首止之
王儲貴有常尊者比哉經故於葵丘之會特書
宰周公於諸侯之上而不殊詞以待之也此義
===
行則天澤之分明而官常以肅屏翰之職謹而
君道以尊春秋之綱維世教豈其微哉抑是會
也仲尼稱其一匡孟子美其爲盛固東周所僅
見者然攷是役晉侯將預會道遇宰孔而止之
桓德其斁矣天顏咫尺之敬微仲敎之或不及
此也補衮之忠仲其有焉君子尚論王道而不
棄桓文之功其以此夫
齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田定公十年
王立身
punctuated:
冢宰而爵上公，固云尊矣。然即其用舍，則有進退之節焉，而篤棐而靖共，皆臣子之所有事也。語其出入，則有均勞之義焉，而效忠而宣力，皆臣職之所當爲也。噫！吾於伯禹見司空之命焉，嘗進宅乎百揆矣；於姬旦見師保之職焉，嘗下均乎四海矣。惟玆宰孔，亦猶伯禹之於虞也，姬旦之於周也，夫固位極人臣者耳。是豈首止之王儲貴有常尊者比哉？經故於葵丘之會，特書宰周公於諸侯之上，而不殊詞以待之也。此義行，則天澤之分明，而官常以肅；屏翰之職謹，而君道以尊。《春秋》之綱維世教，豈其微哉？抑是會也，仲尼稱其一匡，孟子美其爲盛，固東周所僅見者。然攷是役，晉侯將預會，道遇宰孔而止之，桓德其斁矣。天顏咫尺之敬，微仲敎之，或不及此也。補衮之忠，仲其有焉。君子尚論王道，而不棄桓文之功，其以此夫！
齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田，定公十年。
王立身
translation_en:
…holding the office of Grand Steward and the rank of senior duke was certainly exalted. Yet whether he was employed or set aside, there were proper rules governing his advancement and withdrawal; giving devoted assistance and serving with reverent diligence were duties incumbent upon a subject. Whether he served at court or abroad, there was the obligation to share in its labors; displaying loyalty and exerting his strength were what his ministerial office required.
Ah! In Bo Yu we see appointment as Minister of Works, followed by advancement to preside over the hundred officials; in Ji Dan we see the offices of Grand Preceptor and Grand Guardian, followed by his descent to bring equitable order to all within the Four Seas. This Zai Kong likewise stood in relation to Yu as Bo Yu had, and to Zhou as Ji Dan had: he was simply someone who had reached the highest station attainable by a subject. How could he compare with the royal heir at Shouzhi, whose exalted standing was permanently assured? Thus, in recording the meeting at Kuiqiu, the Classic specifically places “the Steward, the Duke of Zhou” above the regional lords, yet does not accord him distinctive wording.
When this principle prevails, the distinction between those above and below—as between heaven and the marsh—is clear, and the regular duties of officials are strictly observed; those serving as the throne’s protective bulwarks attend carefully to their responsibilities, and the ruler’s authority is honored. Can the Spring and Autumn Annals’ role in sustaining moral instruction in the world be called insignificant?
Moreover, Zhongni praised this meeting for setting the world right, and Mengzi extolled its grandeur: it was indeed a rare occurrence in the Eastern Zhou. Yet examination of this occasion shows that the Lord of Jin, on his way to attend the meeting, encountered Zai Kong, who dissuaded him. Huan’s virtue had indeed deteriorated. As for the reverence due to the royal countenance as though it were but a few feet away, had Zhong not instructed him, he might not have attained even this. Zhong indeed possessed the loyalty that repairs defects in the ruler’s ceremonial robe—that is, remedies his faults. When gentlemen discuss the Way of Kings while still acknowledging the achievements of Huan and Wen, is this perhaps the reason?
“The men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.” Tenth year of Duke Ding.
Wang Lishen.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭錢　批〔發揮題意明甚而詞亦鏗鏘〕
〔殆場中之不多見者〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔感化歸地人人能言之獨子叙〕
〔事有體宜試多士〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔語明意盡〕
大國感化而歸地春秋特序其績焉此見三田
之歸而聖人之化有以行於齊矣亦何嫌於序
績也哉且鄆讙龜陰地繼於齊久矣玆曷爲而
來歸耶景以謝過於魯也孜之於經歸地未有
===
書來者此獨書來歸何蓋序其化齊之績耳彼
夾谷有會犂彌設間齊之所以易魯者何如使
無人乎定公之側魯亦殆矣幸而攝相事者有
孔子焉具司馬之從而威足以禦其儔罷野享
之設而詞足以折其衆神人德義之喻以明防
也夷夏盟好之辨以明禮也齊亦有人心者安
得不翻然而歸之地哉以故求從古人之道景
公不能隱其情謝過以質之言晏子有以順其
美於是鄆讙龜陰之田咸章章乎來歸之恐後
punctuated:
同考試官教諭錢　批〔發揮題意明甚，而詞亦鏗鏘〕〔殆場中之不多見者〕。
考試官教諭劉　批〔感化歸地，人人能言之，獨子叙〕〔事有體，宜試多士〕。
考試官教諭胡　批〔語明意盡〕。
大國感化而歸地，春秋特序其績焉。此見三田之歸，而聖人之化有以行於齊矣，亦何嫌於序績也哉？且鄆、讙、龜陰，地繼於齊久矣，玆曷爲而來歸耶？景以謝過於魯也。孜之於經，歸地未有書來者，此獨書來歸，何？蓋序其化齊之績耳。彼夾谷有會，犂彌設間，齊之所以易魯者何如？使無人乎定公之側，魯亦殆矣。幸而攝相事者有孔子焉。具司馬之從，而威足以禦其儔；罷野享之設，而詞足以折其衆。神人德義之喻，以明防也；夷夏盟好之辨，以明禮也。齊亦有人心者，安得不翻然而歸之地哉？以故求從古人之道，景公不能隱其情；謝過以質之言，晏子有以順其美。於是鄆、讙、龜陰之田，咸章章乎來歸之恐後
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Qian, Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning of the topic is developed with great clarity, and the language is sonorous.〕〔Such a piece is seldom encountered in the examination hall.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Anyone can speak of moral transformation leading to the return of territory; you alone narrate〕〔the events with proper form. This is suitable for testing the assembled candidates.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔The language is clear and the meaning fully expressed.〕
A great state was morally transformed and returned territory; the Spring and Autumn Annals specially records this achievement. Here we see the return of the three territories, showing that the sage’s transforming influence had taken effect in Qi. What objection, then, could there be to recording his achievement? The lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin had long remained attached to Qi. Why, now, did Qi come to return them? Duke Jing did so to apologize to Lu for his wrongdoing. Examining [?] the Classic, we find that no previous return of territory was recorded with the word “come.” Why does this entry alone say “came to return”? It is precisely to record his achievement in morally transforming Qi.
At the meeting at Jiagu, Li Mi laid a plot: how contemptuously Qi treated Lu! Had there been no capable man at Duke Ding’s side, Lu would indeed have been in danger. Fortunately, Confucius was there, temporarily performing the minister’s duties. He provided an escort under the Minister of War, and his authority sufficed to repel their company; he stopped the proposed banquet in the open countryside, and his words sufficed to subdue their multitude. His admonition concerning spirits and men, virtue and righteousness, clarified the boundaries to be observed; his distinctions concerning the Yi and Xia, covenants and friendly relations, clarified ritual propriety. The people of Qi, too, possessed human hearts: how could they fail to change their minds at once and return the territory?
Thus, in seeking to follow the way of the ancients, Duke Jing could not conceal his true feelings; through words proposing that the apology be substantiated, Yanzi helped bring his good intention to fulfillment. Thereupon, the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin were all conspicuously returned, with every fear of delay…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
也王道遠於感通神武伸於俄頃是以數千里
之强國而不能有加於魯無惑耳是豈前此之
濟西後此之讙闡出於魯請而得者可同語哉
經故特書來歸而不以序績爲嫌焉若曰此吾
君之功也其與格苗之紀於書降崇之詠於詩
同一揆耳其以天自處之意何如哉雖然非孔
子無以感齊而歸地非晏子無以賛君於令圖
是故外化强齊內孚叔季三年其有成矣晏子
相齊恭儉有文其見於感化道君可攷也使能
===
一變至魯則太公之齊泱泱乎其大風矣謂不
足以表東海也哉惜也書社之封復以一言沮
之謂之知仲尼可乎
禮記
故天降膏露地出醴泉山出器車河出馬
圖鳳皇麒麟皆在郊棷龜龍在宮沼
韓必光
考試官教諭劉　批〔詞藻不浮體裁自別亦塲中〕
僅見者
punctuated:
也。王道遠於感通，神武伸於俄頃。是以數千里之强國，而不能有加於魯，無惑耳。是豈前此之濟西、後此之讙闡，出於魯請而得者，可同語哉？經故特書來歸，而不以序績爲嫌焉。若曰：「此吾君之功也。」其與格苗之紀於《書》、降崇之詠於《詩》，同一揆耳。其以天自處之意何如哉？雖然，非孔子無以感齊而歸地，非晏子無以賛君於令圖。是故外化强齊，內孚叔季，三年其有成矣。晏子相齊，恭儉有文，其見於感化道君可攷也。使能一變至魯，則太公之齊，泱泱乎其大風矣！謂不足以表東海也哉？惜也，書社之封，復以一言沮之，謂之知仲尼可乎？

《禮記》
故天降膏露，地出醴泉，山出器車，河出馬圖，鳳皇麒麟皆在郊棷，龜龍在宮沼。

韓必光

考試官教諭劉，批〔詞藻不浮，體裁自別，亦塲中〕僅見者。
translation_en:
… Such was the far-reaching influence of the kingly Way, and such the manifestation of divine martial power in an instant. It is therefore no wonder that a powerful state extending several thousand li could gain no advantage over Lu. Could this possibly be compared with the earlier recovery of Jixi or the later recovery of Huan and Chan, obtained through requests from Lu? Thus the Classic specifically records that Qi “came and returned” the lands, without scrupling to recount the achievement. It is as though it said, “This is our ruler’s accomplishment.” This follows the same principle as the account in the Book of Documents of bringing the Miao to submission, and the celebration in the Book of Odes of subduing Chong. What, then, was the intention behind assuming Heaven’s position in this judgment?

Nevertheless, without Kongzi, Qi could not have been moved to return the land; without Yanzi, its ruler could not have been assisted toward this worthy undertaking. Thus Kongzi transformed powerful Qi abroad and won the trust of the Shu and Ji clans at home: in three years there would have been results. Yanzi served as chief minister of Qi with reverence, frugality, and refinement; these qualities can be discerned in his influence upon and guidance of his ruler. Had he been able to bring Qi, through a single transformation, to the level of Lu, how grand would have been the prevailing ways of the Grand Duke’s Qi! Could anyone say that it was unfit to serve as an exemplar for the eastern seaboard? Alas, when a fief of registered communities was proposed for Kongzi, Yanzi thwarted it with a single remark. Can he be said to have understood Zhongni?

Book of Rites

“Thus Heaven sends down rich dew, Earth brings forth sweet springs, the mountains yield vessels and carriages, and the River yields the horse chart. Phoenixes and qilin are all found in the outskirts and thickets, and tortoises and dragons inhabit the palace ponds.”

Han Biguang

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “The diction is not frivolous, and the composition has a distinctive form; it is also one of the very few of its kind seen in this examination.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭胡　批〔鋪敘聖世之瑞有法〕
記者備舉聖世之瑞見其有以致之也夫瑞不
易得也而況於諸瑞之畢至乎是故可以徵大
順之感矣禮運記此若曰聖王之在上也順道
成化固其無所為之心而順氣成象乃其不期
然之驗悉而數之寧獨三才之協應已乎是故
仰觀於上其凝而為露者天之常也而其潤若
膏則露之不常有於天者於茲降矣謂非瑞之
見於天乎俯察於下其溢而為泉者地之常也
===
而其甘若醴則泉之不常有於地者於茲出矣
謂非瑞之徵于地乎今夫山嘗見其寶藏興焉
耳矣時則有若器車出焉而圓曲之制若或造
之也天成之巧不於山呈其瑞耶今夫川嘗見
其貨財殖焉耳矣時則有若馬圖出焉而奇偶
之文若或畫之也神道之教不於川洩其瑞耶
以至有道則見非聖不出麟鳳之為祥也宜矣
而招徠之為難也今於郊棷而並集焉則凡為
飛為走之以瑞名者皆得而有之矣吉凶先知
punctuated:
考試官教諭胡，批〔鋪敘聖世之瑞有法〕。

記者備舉聖世之瑞，見其有以致之也。夫瑞不易得也，而況於諸瑞之畢至乎？是故可以徵大順之感矣。《禮運》記此，若曰：聖王之在上也，順道成化，固其無所為之心；而順氣成象，乃其不期然之驗。悉而數之，寧獨三才之協應已乎？是故仰觀於上，其凝而為露者，天之常也；而其潤若膏，則露之不常有於天者，於茲降矣。謂非瑞之見於天乎？俯察於下，其溢而為泉者，地之常也；而其甘若醴，則泉之不常有於地者，於茲出矣。謂非瑞之徵于地乎？今夫山，嘗見其寶藏興焉耳矣。時則有若器車出焉，而圓曲之制，若或造之也。天成之巧，不於山呈其瑞耶？今夫川，嘗見其貨財殖焉耳矣。時則有若馬圖出焉，而奇偶之文，若或畫之也。神道之教，不於川洩其瑞耶？以至有道則見，非聖不出，麟鳳之為祥也宜矣，而招徠之為難也。今於郊棷而並集焉，則凡為飛為走之以瑞名者，皆得而有之矣。吉凶先知
translation_en:
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition of the auspicious signs of a sage’s age is skillfully ordered.〕

The recorder enumerates the auspicious signs of a sage’s age in full, showing that there was something that brought them about. Auspicious signs are not easily obtained; how much less easily do all such signs arrive together! Thus they can attest to the response evoked by the Great Accord. In recording this, the “Evolution of Rites” chapter speaks as though to say: When a sage king rules above, he follows the Way and brings about transformation, his heart assuredly free from any ulterior purpose; harmonious vital energies take visible form, providing confirmation that he had not anticipated. If we enumerate these manifestations exhaustively, are they merely the concerted responses of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity?

Thus, looking upward, we see that moisture condensing into dew is Heaven’s ordinary course. But when its richness resembles unguent, dew of a kind not ordinarily found in Heaven descends here. Can this be denied to be an auspicious sign appearing in Heaven? Looking downward, we see that water welling up into springs is Earth’s ordinary course. But when its sweetness resembles sweet wine, spring water of a kind not ordinarily found on Earth issues forth here. Can this be denied to be an auspicious sign manifested on Earth?

As for mountains, ordinarily we have only seen their stores of treasures come forth. At such a time, however, something like a fashioned carriage emerges, its rounded and curved forms seemingly made by someone. Does not this workmanship, formed by Heaven itself, display its auspicious sign in the mountains? As for rivers, ordinarily we have only seen their material wealth increase. At such a time, however, something like the horse-borne diagram emerges, its pattern of odd and even numbers seemingly drawn by someone. Does not instruction through the numinous Way reveal its auspicious sign in the rivers?

Furthermore, appearing when the Way prevails and coming forth only in the presence of a sage, qilin and phoenixes fittingly constitute auspicious signs; yet attracting them is difficult. Now they gather together in the wooded outskirts, so that all creatures, whether flying or running, renowned as auspicious signs are present. Foreknowing good and ill fortune…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
變化不測龜龍之爲靈也尚矣而騶擾之非易
也今於宮沼而咸若焉則凡爲鱗爲介之以瑞
名者可得而覩之矣要之於數者而一有焉巳
爲間出之禎合數者而兼有焉尤爲卓異之盛
自非大順之世何以得此而求其感召之本亦
曰自脩禮始耳何也蓋脩禮以爲敎則七情治
十義脩人利興人患息中和在我而位育由之
雖諸福之物可致之祥若響答聲若影從表無
或爽者聖人非意之也以順召順其巳定之天
===
則然也否則伏羲舜文之瑞皆可倖致而張子
之所謂志一動氣者誣矣
唯聖人爲能饗帝
劉藎鍾
考試官敎諭劉　批〔士子講聖人能饗帝處類多套襲此作獨體認親切〕
考試官敎諭胡　批〔詞理俱到〕
記者於格天之禮而獨歸之聖焉蓋至不易格
者天也惟聖者能之天人相與之際其難也哉
punctuated:
變化不測，龜龍之爲靈也尚矣，而騶擾之非易也。今於宮沼而咸若焉，則凡爲鱗爲介之以瑞名者，可得而覩之矣。要之，於數者而一有焉，巳爲間出之禎；合數者而兼有焉，尤爲卓異之盛。自非大順之世，何以得此？而求其感召之本，亦曰自脩禮始耳。何也？蓋脩禮以爲敎，則七情治，十義脩，人利興，人患息，中和在我，而位育由之。雖諸福之物、可致之祥，若響答聲，若影從表，無或爽者。聖人非意之也，以順召順，其巳定之天則然也。否則，伏羲、舜、文之瑞皆可倖致，而張子之所謂志一動氣者誣矣。

唯聖人爲能饗帝
劉藎鍾
考試官敎諭劉，批〔士子講聖人能饗帝處，類多套襲，此作獨體認親切。〕
考試官敎諭胡，批〔詞理俱到。〕

記者於格天之禮而獨歸之聖焉。蓋至不易格者，天也；惟聖者能之。天人相與之際，其難也哉！
translation_en:
…Their transformations are unfathomable: tortoises and dragons have long been esteemed as numinous creatures, yet tending and taming them is no easy matter. Now, when all dwell contentedly in palace ponds, every scaled or shelled creature renowned as an auspicious sign may be seen. In sum, the appearance of even one among these several signs already constitutes a rare portent of good fortune; to possess all of them together is an especially extraordinary abundance. How could this be attained except in an age of supreme harmony? If we seek the root of the influence that summons them, we can only say that it begins with the cultivation of ritual propriety. Why? When ritual propriety is cultivated as the means of instruction, the seven emotions are regulated, the ten duties fulfilled, benefits to the people promoted, and their afflictions ended. With equilibrium and harmony within ourselves, Heaven and Earth take their proper places and all things receive their nurture. Even the creatures that embody blessings and the auspicious signs that can be elicited respond like an echo to a sound or a shadow to its gnomon, without any deviation. The sage does not deliberately seek this: harmony summons harmony, as the established pattern of Heaven necessarily dictates. Otherwise, the auspicious signs of Fu Xi, Shun, and King Wen could all be obtained by mere good fortune, and Master Zhang’s statement that a concentrated will moves the vital energy would be false.

“Only the Sage Can Cause the Sovereign on High to Accept His Offering”
By Liu Jinzhong.

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “When candidates explain how the sage can cause the Sovereign on High to accept his offering, most repeat conventional formulations. This composition alone shows an intimate and keen understanding.”
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.”

In discussing the rite by which one reaches Heaven, the recorder attributes this capacity exclusively to the sage. For Heaven is supremely difficult to reach; only the sage can do so. How difficult indeed is this meeting between Heaven and humanity!

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
見於祭義者若曰禮莫重於祭祭莫重於天惟
天吾大造之德則夫思以報之者孰不有以祭
之也惟君隆大報之典則夫有以祭之者又孰
不欲其饗之也自夫德有未至是以禮不虛行
而帝之饗也不能不有待於聖人矣蓋其繼天
立極而篤恭之不顯妙合乎天載者有以端昭
事之本應天以實而至誠之無息潛孚乎於穆
者有以裕祇承之原故其有事於上帝也明德
惟馨已具達於殷薦之始而式禮莫愆自來格
===
于對越之時燔柴告至所以升中于天者猶夫
人也而端物騂犢以膺饗觀之貺則人之所不
能者而聖人獨能之矣用犢貴誠所以祀帝于
郊者猶夫人也而休徵協應以承昭假之祐則
聖人之所獨能者而人不與能矣雖曰神之格
思不可度也若難知其饗矣然自精神之所流
通者測之則上帝之居歆而凜乎其如在者亦
其理之有足信也雖曰天無常親不可諶也若
難必其饗矣然以意氣之所感召者推之則上
punctuated: 見於祭義者若曰：「禮莫重於祭，祭莫重於天。惟天，吾大造之德，則夫思以報之者，孰不有以祭之也？惟君，隆大報之典，則夫有以祭之者，又孰不欲其饗之也？自夫德有未至，是以禮不虛行，而帝之饗也，不能不有待於聖人矣。蓋其繼天立極，而篤恭之不顯，妙合乎天載者，有以端昭事之本；應天以實，而至誠之無息，潛孚乎於穆者，有以裕祇承之原。故其有事於上帝也，明德惟馨，已具達於殷薦之始；而式禮莫愆，自來格于對越之時。燔柴告至，所以升中于天者，猶夫人也；而端物騂犢，以膺饗觀之貺，則人之所不能者，而聖人獨能之矣。用犢貴誠，所以祀帝于郊者，猶夫人也；而休徵協應，以承昭假之祐，則聖人之所獨能者，而人不與能矣。雖曰『神之格思，不可度也』，若難知其饗矣，然自精神之所流通者測之，則上帝之居歆，而凜乎其如在者，亦其理之有足信也。雖曰『天無常親』，『不可諶也』，若難必其饗矣，然以意氣之所感召者推之，則上
translation_en:
What appears in the discussion of the meaning of sacrifice seems to say: “Among rites, none is weightier than sacrifice; among sacrifices, none is weightier than sacrifice to Heaven. Heaven has bestowed upon us the beneficence of creation: who, wishing to repay it, would not offer sacrifice? The ruler alone exalts the ceremony of this great repayment: who, offering sacrifice, would not wish Heaven to accept it? Yet virtue may fall short of perfection. Ritual cannot take effect through empty performance, and the Lord’s acceptance of the offering must therefore await a sage.

“For the sage succeeds Heaven and establishes the supreme standard. His profound reverence, unseen yet wondrously attuned to Heaven’s workings, rectifies the foundation of his luminous service. He responds to Heaven with substance, and his unceasing, utmost sincerity accords imperceptibly with its profound majesty, enriching the source of his reverent obedience. Thus, when he sacrifices to the Lord on High, the fragrance of radiant virtue has already reached Him at the outset of the abundant offerings. As the sage follows the rites without error, the divine presence naturally arrives while he stands reverently before it.

“In burning wood and announcing his arrival, thereby presenting his accomplishments to Heaven, he is like other men. Yet in presenting the proper offering, a red calf, and receiving the favor of divine acceptance and regard [?], the sage alone accomplishes what others cannot. In using a calf and valuing sincerity, thereby sacrificing to the Lord at the suburban altar, he is like other men. Yet auspicious signs respond in harmony, and he receives the blessing of the divine presence: this the sage alone can accomplish, and others cannot share in that ability.

“Although it is said, ‘The coming of the spirits cannot be fathomed,’ so that it seems difficult to know whether the offering is accepted, if we judge by the communion of spiritual essences, then the Lord on High’s acceptance and enjoyment of the offering, His awesome presence as though actually there, are sufficiently credible in principle. Although it is said, ‘Heaven has no constant favorites,’ and ‘It cannot be relied upon,’ so that its acceptance seems difficult to ensure, if we infer from what intent and vital force evoke, then the Lord on High …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
帝之臨女而儼乎其陟降者尤其機之不容間
也於此見聖之饗乎帝者惟德動天而非有所
求也帝之饗於聖者惟天鑒德而非有所私也
孰謂天人之不相及也哉抑聖人之能饗帝固
也亦豈索饗於杳冥之中哉不過一實理而已
蓋天以實理賦之聖人聖人以實理達之天是
故窮神以繼其志知化以述其事則事天如事
親若一氣之相通而喘息呼吸皆不能外而况
於饗之乎故程子曰此體信達順之道聰明睿
知皆由是出以此事天饗帝噫盡之矣
===
第貳場
論
聖人之心純亦不已
韓萃善
同考試官教諭陳　批〔聖人之心惟與道爲體故能同天不息此作發揮透徹豈亦見道者耶〕
同考試官學正皇甫　批〔以川流意發明聖人純一之心見理精妙出諸作錄之不徒以文也〕
punctuated:
帝之臨女，而儼乎其陟降者，尤其機之不容間也。於此見聖之饗乎帝者，惟德動天，而非有所求也；帝之饗於聖者，惟天鑒德，而非有所私也。孰謂天人之不相及也哉？抑聖人之能饗帝固也，亦豈索饗於杳冥之中哉？不過一實理而已。蓋天以實理賦之聖人，聖人以實理達之天。是故窮神以繼其志，知化以述其事，則事天如事親，若一氣之相通，而喘息呼吸皆不能外，而况於饗之乎？故程子曰：「此體信達順之道，聰明睿知皆由是出，以此事天饗帝。」噫！盡之矣！

第貳場
論
聖人之心純亦不已
韓萃善

同考試官教諭陳，批〔聖人之心惟與道爲體，故能同天不息。此作發揮透徹，豈亦見道者耶？〕

同考試官學正皇甫，批〔以川流意發明聖人純一之心，見理精妙，出諸作。錄之不徒以文也。〕
translation_en:
…the Lord on High watches over you, solemnly present in his ascending and descending: still more does this show that the workings of this communion admit no interruption. Here we see that the sage’s offerings are accepted by the Lord on High solely because virtue moves Heaven, not because the sage seeks anything; and that the Lord on High accepts the sage’s offerings solely because Heaven discerns virtue, not because it shows partiality. Who could say that Heaven and humanity cannot reach one another? Yet, granted that the sage can offer sacrifices acceptable to the Lord on High, does he seek their acceptance somewhere in the dark and obscure? It is nothing more than the one true principle. Heaven endows the sage with this true principle, and through this true principle the sage reaches Heaven. Thus, by fathoming the spiritual, he carries on Heaven’s intent; by understanding transformation, he continues Heaven’s work. He serves Heaven as he serves his parents, as though one vital energy flowed between them, so that not even a single breath could fall outside this communion—how much more so his sacrificial offerings! Thus Master Cheng said: “This is the Way of embodying trustworthiness and attaining accord. Acuity of hearing and sight, sagacity and wisdom all issue from it. Through it one serves Heaven and offers sacrifices to the Lord on High.” Ah! This says it all!

Second Session
Discourse
“The Sage’s Heart Is Pure and Unceasing”
Han Cuishan

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: “Only because the sage’s heart takes the Way as its substance can it be unceasing like Heaven. This composition expounds the matter thoroughly and penetratingly. Might its author also be someone who has perceived the Way?”

Associate Examiner Huangfu, Instructor (xuezheng), comments: “Using the idea of a flowing river to elucidate the sage’s pure and undivided heart, this composition displays a subtle and refined understanding of principle and surpasses the other works. Its selection for inclusion is not merely on account of its literary merits.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭劉　批〔體認真切詞意渾融〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔明暢宏博〕
論曰道其原於天乎聖人以心會道以道觀物
要亦天機之自相為感也何也天不息故道不
息道不息故物之與道為體者亦不息然是物
也夫人而見之也夫人見之而不能發之者以
物觀物不以道觀物也不以道觀物者能見於
其所見而不能見於其所不見非其目有遺明
無聖人之心也聖人之心何心哉一天而已矣
===
天以不息之道付之於人與聖人者非有異也
而聖人之心之獨異於人者亦豈能有加於天
之外耶能不失乎天之所與者而已矣心與天
一天與道一道與萬物一則視天下之肖形麗
象凡彌漫於宇宙之大而貫徹于今古之久者
何莫非物則何莫非道亦何莫非天亦何莫而
非吾心之所素畜者乎是故畜之於中觸之於
外觸之於外應之於中亦其天之不容間而機
之不能自已者也昔者夫子有感於川流而發
punctuated:
考試官教諭劉　批〔體認真切，詞意渾融。〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔明暢宏博。〕
論曰：道其原於天乎？聖人以心會道，以道觀物，要亦天機之自相為感也。何也？天不息，故道不息；道不息，故物之與道為體者亦不息。然是物也，夫人而見之也。夫人見之而不能發之者，以物觀物，不以道觀物也。不以道觀物者，能見於其所見，而不能見於其所不見，非其目有遺明，無聖人之心也。聖人之心何心哉？一天而已矣。天以不息之道付之於人，與聖人者非有異也。而聖人之心之獨異於人者，亦豈能有加於天之外耶？能不失乎天之所與者而已矣。心與天一，天與道一，道與萬物一，則視天下之肖形麗象，凡彌漫於宇宙之大而貫徹于今古之久者，何莫非物？則何莫非道，亦何莫非天，亦何莫而非吾心之所素畜者乎？是故畜之於中，觸之於外；觸之於外，應之於中。亦其天之不容間而機之不能自已者也。昔者夫子有感於川流而發
translation_en:
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔The apprehension is genuine and precise; expression and meaning form a harmonious whole.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear, fluent, expansive, and comprehensive.〕
The discourse says: Does not the Way have its source in Heaven? The sage apprehends the Way with his heart and observes things through the Way. In essence, this too is the spontaneous workings of Heaven responding to themselves. Why is this? Heaven never ceases, and so the Way never ceases; the Way never ceases, and so things that embody the Way likewise never cease. Yet these things are visible to everyone. That everyone sees them but cannot elucidate their significance is because they observe things through things, rather than through the Way. Those who do not observe things through the Way can see what is visible to them but cannot see what lies beyond their sight. This is not because their eyes lack acuity, but because they lack the sage’s heart. What kind of heart is the sage’s heart? It is simply one with Heaven.
Heaven bestows its unceasing Way upon human beings, and what it gives the sage is no different. How, then, could the sage’s heart, uniquely different from other people’s, add anything beyond Heaven? It is merely able to preserve what Heaven has bestowed. The heart is one with Heaven, Heaven is one with the Way, and the Way is one with the myriad things. Thus, when we regard all under Heaven that take shape and display visible configurations—all that fill the vastness of the cosmos and extend throughout the long span of past and present—which of them is not a thing? And so, which is not the Way? Which is not Heaven? And which is not something always stored within my own heart? Hence, what is stored within is stirred by contact with what is outside; contact with what is outside calls forth a response within. This, too, is because the Heaven within admits no interruption, and its workings cannot cease of themselves. In former times, the Master was moved by the flowing river and uttered…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
不舍晝夜之嘆程子曰此見聖人之心純亦不
已真知言哉自今觀之天地之闔闢如彼其相
盪而不磨也日月寒暑晝夜之屈伸往來如彼
其相推相禪而不窮也草木之榮枯羽翼角觡
之飛走蟲魚之變化有知無知有情無情之煦
嫗者如彼其相生相育而不可以枚舉而數計
也九夫見而謂之象形而謂之器者莫非物也
果孰爲而孰宰之也夫物之散見者如彼其無
紀極而不有以爲之也不有以宰之也則空虛
===
之殼必無所恃以爲固而散見者亦幾乎息矣
故曰有形者有形形者有象者有象象者夫形
者物也而形形者道也象者物也而象象者道
也道以尸乎其物物以運乎其道而天地萬物
之所以相盪相推相禪相生而無無窮盡者其皆
取足於是道乎是道者非他也根柢於太極分
布於陰陽五行鈞鎔乎品彙全具於人心而所
以命之者天也故董子曰道之大原出於天非
天道何由生非道物何由麗故又曰天者羣物
punctuated: 不舍晝夜之嘆。程子曰：「此見聖人之心純亦不已。」真知言哉！自今觀之，天地之闔闢，如彼其相盪而不磨也；日月寒暑晝夜之屈伸往來，如彼其相推相禪而不窮也；草木之榮枯，羽翼角觡之飛走，蟲魚之變化，有知無知、有情無情之煦嫗者，如彼其相生相育，而不可以枚舉而數計也。九夫見而謂之象、形而謂之器者，莫非物也，果孰爲而孰宰之也？夫物之散見者，如彼其無紀極，而不有以爲之也，不有以宰之也，則空虛之殼必無所恃以爲固，而散見者亦幾乎息矣。故曰：「有形者，有形形者；有象者，有象象者。」夫形者，物也；而形形者，道也。象者，物也；而象象者，道也。道以尸乎其物，物以運乎其道，而天地萬物之所以相盪、相推、相禪、相生而無無窮盡者，其皆取足於是道乎？是道者，非他也，根柢於太極，分布於陰陽五行，鈞鎔乎品彙，全具於人心，而所以命之者，天也。故董子曰：「道之大原出於天。」非天，道何由生？非道，物何由麗？故又曰：「天者，羣物
translation_en:
…the sigh that it “does not cease by day or night.” Master Cheng said: “Here one sees that the sage’s mind is pure and likewise unceasing.” Truly, words of understanding! Viewed from our present standpoint, Heaven and Earth close and open, impelling one another without wearing away. The sun and moon, cold and heat, day and night contract and expand, come and go, advancing and succeeding one another without exhaustion. Plants flourish and wither; creatures with wings fly and those with horns run; insects and fish undergo transformations. The knowing and unknowing, the sentient and insentient, are warmed and nurtured, generating and nourishing one another in such abundance that they cannot be individually enumerated or counted. All that becomes manifest and is called an image, and takes form and is called a vessel, belongs to the realm of things [opening characters doubtful: 九夫]. Who, then, makes them, and who governs them? The scattered manifestations of things are thus without limit. If there were nothing to make them and nothing to govern them, their empty shells would surely have nothing on which to depend for stability, and these scattered manifestations would all but cease.
Thus it is said: “There is that which has form, and there is that which gives form to forms; there is that which has an image, and there is that which gives images to images.” What has form is a thing; what gives form to forms is the Way. What has an image is a thing; what gives images to images is the Way. The Way presides over things, and things put the Way into operation. Is it not entirely from this Way that Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things obtain what enables them to impel, advance, succeed, and generate one another without end [the transcription repeats 無]? This Way is nothing other than that which is rooted in the Supreme Ultimate, distributed through yin and yang and the Five Phases, and molds and casts the myriad kinds of beings. It is fully present in the human mind, and that which ordains it is Heaven. Thus Master Dong said: “The great source of the Way issues from Heaven.” Without Heaven, from what could the Way arise? Without the Way, to what could things adhere? Thus he also said: “Heaven is, for the multitude of things, …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
之祖嘗以是稽諸天矣天以一元之氣流行於
太虛始之以元通之以亨遂之以利成之以貞
而物莫不復命焉天之道至是若幾於息矣而
貞下起元周而復始故易曰乾元亨利貞象曰
天行健君子以自強不息是天之健者乃所以
爲不息而兼此元亨利貞之四德者乃其所以
爲健也神涵於冲穆無朕之中而化溥於萬象
森然之際此固天道之所以爲至妙至妙者乎
而聖人者則合德於天者也融於誠而不雜之
===
以僞純於理而不淆之以欲湛於虛而不牿之
以聞見其心之藏諸用也即天之神而非淪於
無也其心之顯諸仁也即天之化而非滯於有
也其心之靜而無靜動而無動也即天之神化
合一而非無所住也凡不息之理原於天者而
吾夫子以一心契之是故探賾索隱極深研幾
其思之睿也若可息矣而終日不食終夜不寢
之心如故也商羊悟災萍實通謠滄浪契孺子
之歌太山辨婦人之憂其學之博也若可息矣
punctuated: 之祖」。嘗以是稽諸天矣。天以一元之氣流行於太虛，始之以元，通之以亨，遂之以利，成之以貞，而物莫不復命焉。天之道至是若幾於息矣，而貞下起元，周而復始。故《易》曰：「乾，元亨利貞。」《象》曰：「天行健，君子以自強不息。」是天之健者，乃所以爲不息，而兼此元亨利貞之四德者，乃其所以爲健也。神涵於冲穆無朕之中，而化溥於萬象森然之際，此固天道之所以爲至妙至妙者乎！而聖人者，則合德於天者也。融於誠而不雜之以僞，純於理而不淆之以欲，湛於虛而不牿之以聞見。其心之藏諸用也，即天之神，而非淪於無也；其心之顯諸仁也，即天之化，而非滯於有也；其心之靜而無靜、動而無動也，即天之神化合一，而非無所住也。凡不息之理原於天者，而吾夫子以一心契之。是故探賾索隱，極深研幾，其思之睿也，若可息矣，而終日不食、終夜不寢之心如故也。商羊悟災，萍實通謠，滄浪契孺子之歌，太山辨婦人之憂，其學之博也，若可息矣。
translation_en:
…the ancestor of all things.” I have sought to verify this by examining Heaven. Heaven circulates the qi of the primal unity through the Great Void: it initiates things through origination, brings them to fulfillment through flourishing, advances them through benefit, and completes them through constancy. Thus all things return to their allotted destiny. At this point, Heaven’s Way might seem almost to cease; yet beneath constancy, origination arises anew, and the cycle begins again. Thus the Book of Changes says: “Qian: origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy.” The Commentary on the Images says: “Heaven moves with vigor; the noble man accordingly strengthens himself without ceasing.” Heaven’s vigor is what makes it unceasing, and its possession of all four virtues—origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy—is what makes it vigorous. Its numinous efficacy abides within serene profundity, without perceptible trace, while its transforming activity extends throughout the myriad phenomena in their profusion. Surely this is what makes Heaven’s Way supremely wondrous, supremely wondrous!

The sage is one whose virtue accords with Heaven. He is wholly immersed in sincerity, unmixed with falsehood; pure in principle, unconfused by desire; and deeply grounded in emptiness, unconstrained by what he hears and sees. When his mind is concealed within its functioning, it is Heaven’s numinous efficacy, yet does not sink into nothingness. When his mind manifests itself in benevolence, it is Heaven’s transforming activity, yet does not become stuck in being. When his mind is still yet without fixed stillness, and active yet without fixed activity, it is the unity of Heaven’s numinous efficacy and transformation, yet is not without an abiding ground. All the principles of ceaseless activity originate in Heaven, and our Master accords with them through his single mind.

Thus he explored the abstruse and sought out the hidden, plumbed the depths and investigated the subtlest beginnings. In the penetration of his thought, he might seem able to rest; yet the resolve that led him to spend an entire day without eating and an entire night without sleeping remained as before. From the shangyang bird he recognized impending calamity; through the duckweed fruit he understood a popular rhyme; at Canglang he grasped the meaning of a boy’s song; at Mount Taishan he discerned the cause of a woman’s sorrow. In the breadth of his learning, he might seem able to rest…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
而多聞多識之心如故也自志學以至從心其
道之成也若可息矣而忘食忘憂之心如故也
祖述憲章其尚友有如此者而見賢思齊之心
不息也助之禮而問焉之官而問焉萇之樂
而問焉其取善有如此者而三人我師之心不
息也憤而啓悱而發兩端必竭四教雅言其教
人有如此者而無行不與之心不息也削迹於
宋絶糧於陳喪狗譏於鄭衰鳳歌於楚其身若
窮焉無所入矣而栖栖環轍以道易天下之心
===
不息也宰中都而羔豚不餙價男女别於途沈
猶不飲羊攝魯相而歸侵田却萊兵其道若小
試矣而老安少懷綏來動和之心不息也夫其
可息而不息者非强焉爲之也使强而爲之則
矯拂之私必難乎有恒而情之所不樂者其去
之必速矣而烏足以語聖人之心乎聖人之心
之不息是亦天之健而已天與心一而天之外
無心心與道一而心之外無道道與物一而道
之外無物是故自其心之所不息者而呈之於
punctuated:
而多聞多識之心如故也。自志學以至從心，其道之成也若可息矣，而忘食忘憂之心如故也。祖述憲章，其尚友有如此者，而見賢思齊之心不息也。助之禮而問焉，之官而問焉，萇之樂而問焉，其取善有如此者，而三人我師之心不息也。憤而啓，悱而發，兩端必竭，四教雅言，其教人有如此者，而無行不與之心不息也。削迹於宋，絶糧於陳，喪狗譏於鄭，衰鳳歌於楚，其身若窮焉，無所入矣，而栖栖環轍、以道易天下之心不息也。宰中都而羔豚不餙價，男女别於途，沈猶不飲羊；攝魯相而歸侵田，却萊兵，其道若小試矣，而老安少懷、綏來動和之心不息也。

夫其可息而不息者，非强焉爲之也。使强而爲之，則矯拂之私必難乎有恒，而情之所不樂者，其去之必速矣，而烏足以語聖人之心乎？聖人之心之不息，是亦天之健而已。天與心一，而天之外無心；心與道一，而心之外無道；道與物一，而道之外無物。是故自其心之所不息者而呈之於
translation_en:
…yet his commitment to hearing and learning widely remained as before. From setting his heart on learning to following his heart’s desires, his attainment of the Way might have allowed him to rest; yet his absorption, in which he forgot food and sorrow, remained as before. He transmitted the teachings of earlier sages and took their institutions as his models: such was his fellowship with the worthy of antiquity. Yet his resolve to equal the worthy whenever he saw them never ceased. He asked about ritual [the wording is corrupt: ?], asked about official offices [the wording is incomplete: ?], and asked about Chang’s music [?]. Such was his seeking out what was good in others; yet his conviction that among three people there must be a teacher for him never ceased. He enlightened those struggling to understand and gave expression to those struggling to speak; he fully explored both ends of a question, taught through four subjects, and used the standard language. Such was his instruction of others; yet his commitment to sharing every aspect of his conduct with his disciples never ceased. His traces were effaced in Song; his provisions ran out in Chen; in Zheng he was mocked as a stray dog; in Chu a song lamented him as a phoenix in decline. He seemed personally to have reached an impasse, with nowhere to find acceptance; yet his restless resolve to travel about and transform the world through the Way never ceased. When he served as magistrate of Zhongdu, lambs and piglets were sold without deceptive pricing, men and women kept apart on the roads, and Shen You no longer made his sheep drink water before selling them. When he served as acting chief minister of Lu, he secured the return of encroached-upon lands and repelled the troops of Lai. His Way seemed to have received a small trial in practice; yet his resolve to bring repose to the aged and affection to the young, to draw people to him by bringing them peace and bring them into harmony through his actions, never ceased.

That he did not rest when he might have rested was not a matter of forcing himself. Had he forced himself, the private effort of coercing and thwarting his nature would surely have been difficult to sustain; and what his feelings did not delight in, he would surely soon have abandoned. How could this suffice to describe the sage’s heart? The ceaseless activity of the sage’s heart is simply the vigor of Heaven. Heaven and the heart are one, and outside Heaven there is no heart; the heart and the Way are one, and outside the heart there is no Way; the Way and things are one, and outside the Way there are no things. Thus, taking what is ceaseless in his heart, he manifests it in…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
物自其物之所不息者而會之於心而川上之
嘆具亦天機之相爲流通者乎今夫陽燧遇日
然而爲火方諸遇月津而爲水物類之相動其
機固如此也聖人以心契道以道觀物則視天
下之覆者載者錯行而代明者根着而蠕動者
無非道者而况乎川流之不舍尤其可指而易
見者乎是故其淵然而澄者與吾心之静遇其
沛然而往者與吾心之動遇其冲然而虚者與
吾心之靈遇以彼之天觸我之天以我之天契
===
彼之天若有以媒之使合也而特不得其故若
有以叩之使應也而特不通其朕若有以期之
使會也而特不察其所自來故曰天機之相爲
感也不然川上之流非一日之積見之者亦非
一人矣而不舍晝夜之妙獨自夫子發之何哉
蓋其陰濁勝而物欲行攻取蔽而湛一擾則有
間之心不足以合天心而物之體乎道者與我
略不相涉矣故鍾律具而莫或聽者無師曠之
耳也浮沉集而莫或釣者無詹何之技也道體
punctuated: 物，自其物之所不息者而會之於心，而川上之嘆，具亦天機之相爲流通者乎？今夫陽燧遇日，然而爲火；方諸遇月，津而爲水。物類之相動，其機固如此也。聖人以心契道，以道觀物，則視天下之覆者、載者、錯行而代明者、根着而蠕動者，無非道者，而况乎川流之不舍，尤其可指而易見者乎？是故其淵然而澄者，與吾心之静遇；其沛然而往者，與吾心之動遇；其冲然而虚者，與吾心之靈遇。以彼之天觸我之天，以我之天契彼之天，若有以媒之使合也，而特不得其故；若有以叩之使應也，而特不通其朕；若有以期之使會也，而特不察其所自來。故曰天機之相爲感也。不然，川上之流非一日之積，見之者亦非一人矣，而不舍晝夜之妙，獨自夫子發之，何哉？蓋其陰濁勝而物欲行，攻取蔽而湛一擾，則有間之心不足以合天心，而物之體乎道者，與我略不相涉矣。故鍾律具而莫或聽者，無師曠之耳也；浮沉集而莫或釣者，無詹何之技也。道體
translation_en: …to things, and from what never ceases in things, apprehend it within the mind. Was the sigh beside the river also an instance of Heaven’s workings flowing between them [?]? Now, when a burning mirror encounters the sun, it kindles fire; when a moon mirror encounters the moon, it exudes water. Such indeed is the mechanism by which things of corresponding kinds move one another. The sage accords with the Way through his mind and observes things through the Way. Thus, throughout the world, he sees that which covers above and bears below, those bodies that travel across the sky and shine in turn, and things rooted in the earth or crawling upon it: none is other than the Way. How much more so the ceaseless flow of a river, which is especially easy to point out and see! Thus its deep clarity meets the stillness of my mind; its abundant onward flow meets the activity of my mind; and its open emptiness meets the numinous awareness of my mind. What is of Heaven in it touches what is of Heaven in me, and what is of Heaven in me accords with what is of Heaven in it. It is as though something mediates between them and brings them together, yet we cannot discover the cause; as though something strikes them and makes them respond, yet we cannot discern its traces; as though something appoints a meeting and makes them converge, yet we cannot perceive whence it comes. Hence we call this the mutual resonance of Heaven’s workings. Otherwise, the river’s flow had accumulated over more than a single day, and more than a single person had seen it: why was the wondrous significance of its “never ceasing day or night” revealed by the Master alone? When the dark and turbid prevail and material desires run free, when striving and grasping obscure the mind and disturb its lucid unity, a mind subject to interruptions cannot accord with Heaven’s mind. Then the embodiment of the Way in things has scarcely any connection with me. Thus, though bells and their pitches are all present, no one hears them, for no one has Shi Kuang’s ear; though things floating and sinking gather [?], no one catches them, for no one has Zhan He’s skill. The substance of the Way…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
活潑而莫或察之者無聖人之心也天下之人
之心同出於天則聖人之心豈有以異於人乎
物至而人化人之自異於聖人而非其初也而
其大之不息者亦未盡泯也是故赤子匍匐爲
我心惻怛也凌波而先濟跂而望乎後之人恕
也嘑爾蹴其爾而不食嗟來之謝恥也大人之心
莫隱於惻怛莫便於恕莫大於恥而隨感以見如
此則信乎人之心即聖人之心而不能充其不
息之道者是棄天也今夫盆水在庭清之終日
===
不能見眉睫濁之不過一撓焉而不能別方圓
人之心易濁而難清是盆水之類也況旦旦撓
之乎噫此純亦不已之心有非聖人不能及也
載稽諸古明此以帝則堯之兢兢舜之業業者
此心也明此以王則禹之不自滿假湯之日躋
文武之緝熙敬勝而不遑暇食者此心也明此
以相則周公之握髮吐哺而夜以繼日坐以待
旦者此心也然則夫子之心其諸堯舜之心乎
禹湯文武周公之心乎千載一人若接踵而生
punctuated:
活潑而莫或察之者，無聖人之心也。天下之人之心同出於天，則聖人之心豈有以異於人乎？物至而人化，人之自異於聖人，而非其初也。而其大之不息者，亦未盡泯也。是故赤子匍匐，爲我心惻怛也；凌波而先濟，跂而望乎後之人，恕也；嘑爾蹴其爾，而不食嗟來之謝，恥也。大人之心，莫隱於惻怛，莫便於恕，莫大於恥，而隨感以見如此，則信乎人之心即聖人之心，而不能充其不息之道者，是棄天也。

今夫盆水在庭，清之終日，不能見眉睫；濁之不過一撓焉，而不能別方圓。人之心易濁而難清，是盆水之類也，況旦旦撓之乎？噫！此純亦不已之心，有非聖人不能及也。

載稽諸古，明此以帝，則堯之兢兢、舜之業業者，此心也；明此以王，則禹之不自滿假、湯之日躋、文武之緝熙敬勝而不遑暇食者，此心也；明此以相，則周公之握髮吐哺，而夜以繼日、坐以待旦者，此心也。然則夫子之心，其諸堯舜之心乎？禹湯文武周公之心乎？千載一人，若接踵而生
translation_en:
…is lively and active, yet none perceive it because they lack the mind of a sage. The minds of all people under Heaven alike originate in Heaven: how, then, could the sage’s mind differ from those of other people? Things impinge upon people and transform them; people thus make themselves different from sages, but this is not their original condition. Yet the greatness of their minds, with its ceaseless activity, has not been wholly extinguished. Thus, a little child crawling stirs compassion in my mind. Having crossed the waves first, one stands on tiptoe to look back for those behind: this is sympathetic consideration. Refusing food offered with a shout or kicked toward one, and rejecting the apology for the insulting summons to eat [?]: this is a sense of shame. In the mind of the great person, nothing is more inward than compassion, more readily exercised than sympathetic consideration, or greater than shame. Since these manifest themselves in response to stimuli in this way, we may indeed trust that the ordinary person’s mind is precisely the sage’s mind. To fail to develop fully its ceaseless Way is to abandon Heaven.

Consider a basin of water in the courtyard. Though one spends the whole day clearing it, one cannot see one’s eyebrows and eyelashes reflected in it [?]; to muddy it takes only a single stirring, after which one cannot distinguish square from round. The human mind, easily muddied but difficult to clear, resembles this basin of water. How much worse if one stirs it up every day! Alas! This mind, pure and likewise unceasing, has a quality that none but a sage can attain.

Examining antiquity, we find that when this was made manifest in the exercise of imperial rule, it was this mind that appeared in Yao’s vigilance and Shun’s wariness. When it was made manifest in kingship, it was this mind that appeared in Yu’s refusal to rest in self-satisfaction, Tang’s daily advancement, and Wen and Wu’s continuous cultivation of brightness and mastery through reverence, leaving them no leisure even to eat. When it was made manifest in service as a minister, it was this mind that appeared in the Duke of Zhou’s grasping his unbound hair and spitting out his food to receive visitors, continuing his work from day into night, and sitting in wait for dawn. Then was not the Master’s mind the mind of Yao and Shun? Was it not the mind of Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, and the Duke of Zhou? Though such a person appears but once in a thousand years, they seem to have been born one directly after another…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
數聖一心不剖符而合非不能外乎此心也不
能外乎天也而未至乎此者當何如亦曰格致
以啓其端克復以踐其實而又慎獨以研其幾
則聖人安焉吾勉焉而純亦不已之心可馴致
矣譬則百川之學海而至於海也厥後孟子得
之而爲原泉之論則曰有本者如是噫有本者
固其所以不息者也
表
擬宋以張載爲崇文院校書謝表〔熙寧二〕
年
===
蔄應元
同考試官教諭錢　批〔校書本以闡明理奥繼往　開來興道致治非爲口耳記誦場中士子類多燕冗　此作深得題旨且措詞騈麗用事典核尤長於四六者　宜錄以式〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔表得宋體僅見此作〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔體正詞葩可誦〕
熙寧二年某月某日伏蒙
punctuated:
數聖一心，不剖符而合。非不能外乎此心也，不能外乎天也。而未至乎此者當何如？亦曰格致以啓其端，克復以踐其實，而又慎獨以研其幾，則聖人安焉，吾勉焉，而純亦不已之心可馴致矣。譬則百川之學海而至於海也。厥後孟子得之，而爲原泉之論，則曰：「有本者如是。」噫！有本者，固其所以不息者也。

表

擬宋以張載爲崇文院校書謝表〔熙寧二〕年

蔄應元

同考試官教諭錢批〔校書本以闡明理奥，繼往開來，興道致治，非爲口耳記誦。場中士子類多燕冗，此作深得題旨，且措詞駢麗，用事典核，尤長於四六者，宜錄以式。〕

考試官教諭劉批〔表得宋體，僅見此作。〕

考試官教諭胡批〔體正詞葩，可誦。〕

熙寧二年某月某日，伏蒙
translation_en:
…Several sages share one mind, agreeing without having to match the halves of a tally. It is not that they cannot go beyond this mind; they cannot go beyond Heaven. What, then, should those who have not yet attained this state do? Investigate things and extend knowledge to initiate the process; overcome the self and return to ritual propriety to put it into practice; and remain watchful when alone to examine the subtlest stirrings. Then, what the sage rests in naturally, I strive toward, and a mind of unceasing purity can gradually be attained. It is like the hundred rivers taking the sea as their model and eventually reaching it. Later, Mencius grasped this and, in his discussion of a wellspring, said: “Such is that which has a source.” Ah! Having a source is indeed what enables it to flow without ceasing.

Memorial

A simulated memorial of thanks for the Song appointment of Zhang Zai as Proofreader in the Institute for the Veneration of Literature. 〔Second year of Xining〕 (1069).

By Man Yingyuan 蔄應元.

Comment by Associate Examiner Qian, Instructor: 〔The purpose of proofreading is fundamentally to elucidate the profound principles, carry forward the past and open the way for the future, promote the Way, and bring about good government. It is not a matter of merely repeating what one has heard or memorizing and reciting. Candidates in the examination hall mostly produce idle and prolix writing [?]. This composition grasps the intent of the topic deeply; moreover, its phrasing is elegantly parallel, and its allusions are grounded in the classics and accurate. It is particularly accomplished in prose of four- and six-character phrases and should be recorded as a model.〕

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔Among the memorials, this is the only composition I have seen that captures the Song style.〕

Comment by Examiner Hu, Instructor: 〔Correct in form and splendid in diction: worthy of recitation.〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖恩授臣戴崇文院校書者伏以
紫禁敷綸瑞啓圖書之府青藜秉燭光騰奎
壁之躔運實際乎
離明寵叟踰于晉接臣戴誠惶誠恐稽首頓
首竊惟皇王之大道備載典墳天地之秘
藏丕彰丘索五車四庫累世難窮諸子百
家殊方靡究自尼父刪脩之後文獻昭回
逮嬴秦煨燼之餘簡編澌盡石渠稱制異
論盈庭虎觀談經同聲聚訟河平下遺書
===
之詔閣振弌微江陵俢古蹟之儲何裨孔
棘謠傳版盤疇誇甲族名流治謝垂裳徒
勤乙夜御覽况當五代之亂壯士橫戈致
茲羣籍之湮儒生倚席天開
皇宋星聚文奎像賛孔顏吾道昭于日月經頌
洞院斯文沛若江河式袪戰代之風適展
詩書之業橫經論道歷世已然稽古考文
于
今特盛茲蓋伏遇
punctuated:
聖恩授臣戴崇文院校書者。伏以：紫禁敷綸，瑞啓圖書之府；青藜秉燭，光騰奎壁之躔。運實際乎離明，寵叟踰于晉接。臣戴誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。
竊惟皇王之大道，備載典墳；天地之秘藏，丕彰丘索。五車四庫，累世難窮；諸子百家，殊方靡究。自尼父刪脩之後，文獻昭回；逮嬴秦煨燼之餘，簡編澌盡。石渠稱制，異論盈庭；虎觀談經，同聲聚訟。河平下遺書之詔，閣振弌微；江陵俢古蹟之儲，何裨孔棘？謠傳版盤，疇誇甲族名流；治謝垂裳，徒勤乙夜御覽。况當五代之亂，壯士橫戈；致茲羣籍之湮，儒生倚席。天開皇宋，星聚文奎；像賛孔顏，吾道昭于日月；經頌洞院，斯文沛若江河。式袪戰代之風，適展詩書之業。橫經論道，歷世已然；稽古考文，于今特盛。茲蓋伏遇
translation_en:
…the imperial favor appointing your servant Dai [?; Zhang Zai in the preceding context] as Collator in the Chongwen Academy. I humbly reflect: from the Purple Forbidden Palace the imperial pronouncement issues, auspiciously opening the repository of books; a green goosefoot staff is held aloft as a torch, its radiance rising to the celestial stations of Kui and Bi. Our age truly encounters the brightness of Li; the favor bestowed upon this old man surpasses even the repeated audiences signified by Jin. Your servant Dai [?] is profoundly awed and fearful, bowing his head and knocking his forehead upon the ground.
I privately consider that the great Way of the august sovereigns and kings is fully recorded in the ancient canons, while the hidden treasures of Heaven and Earth are magnificently revealed in the ancient collections Qiu and Suo. Five cartloads of books and the four library divisions could scarcely be exhausted over successive generations; the various masters and hundred schools could not be thoroughly explored even throughout distant regions. After Father Ni—Confucius—made his deletions and revisions, the written heritage shone brilliantly; after the embers left by the Qin of the Ying house, the bamboo slips and bound texts were utterly destroyed. At the Shiqu Pavilion, imperial rulings were pronounced, yet conflicting opinions filled the court; at the White Tiger Hall, the Classics were discussed, yet the assembled voices joined in dispute. During the Heping era an edict commanded the recovery of lost books, reviving the declining imperial library [?]; at Jiangling, a collection of ancient writings was assembled, but how could it help amid desperate crisis? Reports circulated of printing blocks and boards [?]; who could boast of eminent clans and celebrated scholars? Government fell short of the effortless rule symbolized by the sovereign’s hanging robes; in vain did the ruler labor over his reading late into the night. Moreover, amid the disorders of the Five Dynasties, warriors brandished their weapons, bringing about the disappearance of these many books, while Confucian scholars leaned upon their mats [?].
Heaven inaugurated our august Song, and stars gathered in Kui, the constellation of literary culture. Portraits and eulogies honored Confucius and Yan Hui, and our Way shone like the sun and moon; the Classics were recited in the academy of the grotto [?], and this cultural tradition flowed abundantly like the Yangzi and Yellow Rivers. Thus the habits of the warring age were dispelled, and the study of the Odes and Documents was duly advanced. Expounding the Classics and discussing the Way had already been practiced through successive ages; investigating antiquity and examining texts flourish especially today. This is surely because we have humbly encountered…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
睿謨天授
聖德日躋駕三皇五帝之鴻猷宅中圖大承
一祖
四宗之燕翼裕後光前
虎變乎占
龍飛快覩崇儒而員增三舍重道則學表六經
猶謂典旨微詞兼收載籍將欲擬莫茹實
須籍編摩按天祿之章程愼秘書之掄選
本天咫尺金匱深嚴必得光明辨博之才
叅通述作庶備顧問論思之列仰賛
===
聖明臣載闘隴腐儒章縫末學孫吳蚤悅原非
蓬境僊儔佛老晩逃敢覬瀛洲妙選薦拔
頃緣乎宰執甄收特出於
宸衷班視邇臣竝入紅蘭之省職聯史館叨親
白玉之規俯錄其長俾從所便臣敢不殫
心遂古遐搜孔壁羣書肆力鑽研徧閱鄴
侯萬卷頻訂魯魚之謬仍分亥豕之訛磨
punctuated:
睿謨天授，聖德日躋，駕三皇五帝之鴻猷，宅中圖大，承一祖四宗之燕翼，裕後光前。虎變乎占，龍飛快覩。崇儒而員增三舍，重道則學表六經。猶謂典旨微詞，兼收載籍，將欲擬莫茹實，須籍編摩。按天祿之章程，愼秘書之掄選。本天咫尺，金匱深嚴，必得光明辨博之才，叅通述作，庶備顧問論思之列，仰賛聖明。
臣載闘隴腐儒，章縫末學，孫吳蚤悅，原非蓬境僊儔；佛老晩逃，敢覬瀛洲妙選？薦拔頃緣乎宰執，甄收特出於宸衷。班視邇臣，竝入紅蘭之省；職聯史館，叨親白玉之規。俯錄其長，俾從所便。臣敢不殫心遂古，遐搜孔壁羣書，肆力鑽研，徧閱鄴侯萬卷，頻訂魯魚之謬，仍分亥豕之訛，磨
translation_en:
…Your sagacious plans are Heaven-bestowed, and your sacred virtue advances daily. Surpassing the grand designs of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, you occupy the center and plan great undertakings. You inherit the provision made for descendants by the one founding ancestor and four ancestral sovereigns, enriching posterity and bringing glory to your predecessors. The divination foretells the tiger’s transformation; all rejoice to behold the dragon’s ascent. In honoring Confucian learning, you increase enrollment in the Three Colleges; in esteeming the Way, you make the Six Classics the standard of learning. Yet you consider that canonical meanings and subtle expressions must be gathered comprehensively from written records. To undertake assessment, nothing equals substantive evidence [?]; compilation and editing are therefore indispensable. Following the regulations of the Tianlu imperial library, you exercise care in selecting library officials. Heaven is but a short distance away [?], and the golden book chests lie deep within guarded precincts. You must obtain men of lucid understanding, discernment, and broad learning, conversant with transmitting and composing texts, so that they may join the ranks of those consulted on affairs and engaged in deliberation, assisting your sacred wisdom.
Your servant is a pedantic rustic scholar [?], a humble student wearing the Confucian cap. Early fond of the military writings of Sun and Wu, I was never one of the immortal companions of Penglai; only late did I escape Buddhism and Daoism—how could I aspire to the distinguished company of Yingzhou? My recent recommendation and advancement came through the chief councilors, but my selection proceeded especially from Your Majesty’s own heart. Ranked alongside your intimate attendants, I enter with them the offices fragrant with red orchids; appointed to the Historiography Institute, I am unworthily privileged to draw near the white-jade rule. You graciously recognize my strengths and allow me to pursue work suited to them. How dare your servant fail to devote his whole mind to remote antiquity, searching far and wide through the books preserved in Confucius’s wall, exerting himself in close study, and reading through the ten thousand volumes of the Marquis of Ye? I shall repeatedly correct errors confusing lu with yu, and distinguish mistaken substitutions of hai and shi, grinding…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
丹而注前經㝠考夫立功立德淸墨以寘
舊史爰稽其紀動紀言赤手校讎畀任昉
尚傳疑于五世白頭來作慨樂天猶滯迹
于九江兀兀窮年不避餐錢之利孳孳屈
首寧辭食肉之譏儻于方冊之浩繁有得
聖賢之精蘊持之進
御用以備觀模範宛在乎目前治道可運諸掌
上少攄涓滴仰答
洪深伏願
===
聖學緝熙道集萬年之統
皇猷允塞治臻三代之隆
斂福極以錫民堪輿溥溥
建中和而成化比屋風行臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
punctuated:
丹而注前經，㝠考夫立功立德；淸墨以寘舊史，爰稽其紀動紀言。赤手校讎畀任昉，尚傳疑于五世；白頭來作慨樂天，猶滯迹于九江。兀兀窮年，不避餐錢之利；孳孳屈首，寧辭食肉之譏？儻于方冊之浩繁，有得聖賢之精蘊，持之進御，用以備觀，模範宛在乎目前，治道可運諸掌上。少攄涓滴，仰答洪深。伏願：
聖學緝熙，道集萬年之統；皇猷允塞，治臻三代之隆。斂福極以錫民，堪輿溥溥；建中和而成化，比屋風行。臣無任瞻天仰聖激切屛營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
translation_en:
…cinnabar to annotate the ancient classics, searching deeply into the establishment of meritorious deeds and moral virtue; with clear ink applied to the old histories, I examine their records of actions and words. Entrusted with collating texts empty-handed, Ren Fang still transmitted uncertainties concerning five generations [?]; coming to this work white-haired, I lament that Letian likewise remained stranded at Jiujiang [?]. Toiling throughout the year, I do not shun the benefit of a meal allowance; diligently bowing my head to the task, how could I shrink from the reproach of eating meat at public expense? If, amid the vast abundance of books, I can grasp the profound essence of the sages and worthies, I shall present it for Your Majesty’s perusal. Their exemplary models will stand vividly before your eyes, and the Way of government may be wielded as readily as something in your palm. Thus may I offer some small contribution, a mere drop, in repayment of your boundless and profound favor. I humbly pray:
May your sagely learning shine ever more brightly, and may the Way unite in you the succession of ten thousand years; may your imperial designs be fully realized, and may your government attain the flourishing excellence of the Three Dynasties. Gather the blessings of the supreme standard and bestow them upon the people, extending them throughout heaven and earth; establish centrality and harmony to accomplish moral transformation, spreading it like the wind from household to household. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain his intense emotion and utmost awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude and make it known to Your Majesty.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
第叄場
策
第一問
王象坤
同考試官教諭施　批
天昭上瑞我
聖祖我
皇上所以綿億萬之基實徵於此是作揄揚詳盡末復以
聖壽爲得
===
天之慶恩愛之忱溢於
祝頌宜錄以
獻
同考試官教諭楊　批　我
聖祖甘露論我
皇上
欽天記頌莫非敬
天精蘊場中士子類能鋪張其盛未若此作推見本原能知
神聖之心其亦涵濡
punctuated:
第叄場
策
第一問
王象坤

同考試官教諭施　批：天昭上瑞，我聖祖、我皇上所以綿億萬之基，實徵於此。是作揄揚詳盡，末復以聖壽爲得天之慶，恩愛之忱溢於祝頌，宜錄以獻。

同考試官教諭楊　批：我聖祖《甘露論》，我皇上《欽天記頌》，莫非敬天精蘊。場中士子類能鋪張其盛，未若此作推見本原，能知神聖之心，其亦涵濡
translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Wang Xiangkun

Comment by Associate Examiner Shi, Instructor:
Heaven has manifested a supreme auspicious sign. Here indeed is evidence that the foundation laid by our Sagely Founder and our Emperor will endure for countless ages. This essay offers detailed and comprehensive praise. At its close, it further presents His Majesty’s longevity as a blessing received from Heaven. Sincere gratitude and affection overflow in its prayers and praises. It deserves to be transcribed and presented to the throne.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor:
Our Sagely Founder’s Discourse on Sweet Dew and our Emperor’s Record and Eulogy on Revering Heaven both embody the essential meaning of reverence for Heaven. Candidates in the examination generally can expound at length upon the grandeur of these things, but none equals this essay in tracing them to their source and comprehending the mind of the divine sage. Its author, too, must have been steeped in…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖化之深者與主司當爲
國家得人慶
同考試官教諭區　批　甘露上瑞特應
郊報
天心篤祐先後同符我
聖祖我
皇上潛孚默運之機玄矣神矣此篇發明感通之理獨爲至切非
學究天人者不能也取之
考試官教諭劉　批　事
===
天格
天本於敬德皆我
聖祖我
皇上孚感之盛超越萬古所以
上玄純祐
神貺洊臻稽之載籍誠罕儷者子獨能揚厲無遺眞得誦述之
體矣允宜錄之
考試官教諭胡　批　心本忠愛體得對揚是能鳴
國家之盛者
punctuated:
聖化之深者與？主司當爲國家得人慶。

同考試官教諭區，批：甘露上瑞，特應郊報。天心篤祐，先後同符。我聖祖、我皇上潛孚默運之機，玄矣，神矣！此篇發明感通之理，獨爲至切，非學究天人者不能也。取之。

考試官教諭劉，批：事天、格天，本於敬德，皆我聖祖、我皇上孚感之盛，超越萬古。所以上玄純祐，神貺洊臻，稽之載籍，誠罕儷者。子獨能揚厲無遺，眞得誦述之體矣，允宜錄之。

考試官教諭胡，批：心本忠愛，體得對揚，是能鳴國家之盛者。
translation_en:
…one who has been deeply imbued with the sage ruler’s transforming influence? The presiding examiners should rejoice that the state has gained a worthy man.

Associate Examiner Ou, Instructor, comments: “Sweet dew, a supreme auspicious sign, responded specifically to the suburban sacrifice of thanksgiving. Heaven’s gracious protection was abundant, and the signs accorded alike in the earlier and later reigns. How mysterious, how divine, the workings through which our sagely founder and our reigning emperor have silently accorded with Heaven and exerted their influence unseen! This essay elucidates the principle of sympathetic communication with Heaven with exceptional pertinence. Only someone whose learning thoroughly encompasses Heaven and humanity could achieve this. Accept it.”

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Serving Heaven and moving Heaven are rooted in reverence and virtue. In both, the fullness of the sincere influence exerted by our sagely founder and our reigning emperor surpasses all antiquity. Thus Heaven above bestows abundant protection, and divine gifts arrive repeatedly. Examining the written records, one finds truly few parallels. You alone have been able to celebrate this fully, leaving nothing out: you have truly grasped the proper form of laudatory exposition. It certainly deserves to be included in the record.”

Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “Its sentiments are rooted in loyalty and love for the sovereign; its form aptly expresses acknowledgment and praise of imperial grace. This is a work capable of proclaiming the flourishing grandeur of the state.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
有帝王事天之敬有帝王格天之德欽崇
內藴者帝王事天之敬也敬涵於心由是
宥密以基命祗承以協帝所以爲祈天永
命之本者莫非昭事之精也中和建極者
帝王格天之德也德格於天由是迓祥靈
之祉衍昌明之祚所以爲祈天永命之應
者莫非孚祐之徵也大哉敬乎其帝王所
以上承天心益久而益純者乎至哉德乎
其帝王所以上荷天眷愈久而愈隆者乎
===
知乎此則我
聖祖我
皇上
璇穹錫眷
景貺昭垂皆應於
郊報之日而同符不爽者必其有合冲穆之原
協
玄元之秘有未易以窺測者矣故
特著爲甘露論
punctuated: 有帝王事天之敬，有帝王格天之德。欽崇內藴者，帝王事天之敬也。敬涵於心，由是宥密以基命，祗承以協帝，所以爲祈天永命之本者，莫非昭事之精也。中和建極者，帝王格天之德也。德格於天，由是迓祥靈之祉，衍昌明之祚，所以爲祈天永命之應者，莫非孚祐之徵也。大哉敬乎！其帝王所以上承天心，益久而益純者乎！至哉德乎！其帝王所以上荷天眷，愈久而愈隆者乎！知乎此，則我聖祖、我皇上，璇穹錫眷，景貺昭垂，皆應於郊報之日而同符不爽者，必其有合冲穆之原、協玄元之秘，有未易以窺測者矣。故特著爲《甘露論》，
translation_en: There is the reverence with which emperors and kings serve Heaven, and there is the virtue with which they move Heaven. Veneration cherished within is the reverence with which emperors and kings serve Heaven. When reverence resides in the heart, they thereby establish the foundation of the Mandate through profound tranquility, and accord with the Lord on High through reverent obedience. Everything that forms the basis for praying to Heaven for an enduring Mandate is the consummate expression of their illustrious service. Establishing the supreme standard through equilibrium and harmony is the virtue with which emperors and kings move Heaven. When virtue reaches Heaven, they thereby welcome auspicious blessings and prolong the fortune of an age of flourishing enlightenment. Every response to their prayers to Heaven for an enduring Mandate is evidence of Heaven’s answering protection. Great indeed is reverence! Is it not that by which emperors and kings accord with Heaven’s intent above, becoming ever purer with time? Perfect indeed is virtue! Is it not that by which emperors and kings receive Heaven’s favor above, becoming ever more exalted with time? Understanding this, we see that, for our Sagely Ancestor and our August Emperor, the jeweled vault of Heaven has bestowed its favor and illustrious blessings have manifestly descended.
