That these all came in response on the days of the suburban sacrifices of thanksgiving, matching like the halves of a tally without discrepancy, must mean that there is an accord with the source of profound serenity and a harmony with the mysteries of the primal origin, which cannot readily be fathomed. Thus a Discourse on Sweet Dew was specially composed, …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
特製爲
欽天記頌
聖明兼備而述作耀於後先精誠流通而天人
逮於感應雖謂我
太祖我
皇上敬天之心卽
天之心可也謂我
太祖我
皇上格天之德卽
===
天之德可也愚生涵濡誦之久矣請因明問
而對揚之可乎蓋聞聖人以精純邃穆之
德值一元清淑之會決玄波以横流揚仁
風於翔洽舉含生之類莫不浸潤煦育於
渾噩之中故太和薰蒸而上瑞應焉稽之
物瑞軒轅之精注爲膏露食之壽人故曰
聖德上及太清下及萬靈則甘露零又曰
王者德至於天和氣感則甘露零于松栢
其爲殊應何如也考之帝王世紀堯之時
punctuated: 特製爲《欽天記頌》。聖明兼備，而述作耀於後先；精誠流通，而天人逮於感應。雖謂我太祖、我皇上敬天之心卽天之心，可也；謂我太祖、我皇上格天之德卽天之德，可也。愚生涵濡誦之久矣，請因明問而對揚之，可乎？蓋聞聖人以精純邃穆之德，值一元清淑之會，決玄波以横流，揚仁風於翔洽，舉含生之類，莫不浸潤煦育於渾噩之中。故太和薰蒸，而上瑞應焉。稽之物瑞，軒轅之精注爲膏露，食之壽人。故曰：「聖德上及太清，下及萬靈，則甘露零。」又曰：「王者德至於天，和氣感，則甘露零于松栢。」其爲殊應何如也！考之《帝王世紀》，堯之時，
translation_en:
…specially composed the Eulogy on the Record of Revering Heaven. Sageliness and illumination are both fully present, and their writings shine across successive ages; perfect sincerity flows freely, bringing Heaven and humanity into mutual response. It is indeed permissible to say that the heart with which our Taizu and our Emperor revere Heaven is Heaven’s own heart; it is likewise permissible to say that the virtue through which our Taizu and our Emperor move Heaven is Heaven’s own virtue. This humble student has long steeped himself in these writings and recited them. May I respond to your illuminating question by expounding and praising their meaning?

I have heard that the sage, possessing virtue of perfect purity, profound depth, and solemn serenity, encounters a moment when the primal unity is clear and beneficent. He releases the mysterious waters to flow far and wide and spreads the influence of benevolence until it pervades all [?]. Every kind of living being is moistened, warmed, and nurtured within a state of pristine simplicity. Thus supreme harmony suffuses all, and the highest auspicious signs appear in response. Examining auspicious signs in the natural world, we find that the vital essence of Xuanyuan pours forth as rich dew, whose consumption prolongs human life. Thus it is said: “When sagely virtue reaches upward to the realm of highest purity and downward to the myriad spirits, sweet dew falls.” It is also said: “When a true king’s virtue reaches Heaven and harmonious vital energies respond, sweet dew falls upon pines and cypresses.” How extraordinary an auspicious response this is! Consulting the Chronicles of Emperors and Kings (Diwang shiji), we find that in Yao’s time…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
景星燦翼軫矣昴星耀河渚矣河圖出矣
醴泉溢矣蓂莢生矣神禾茂矣鳳巢阿閣
矣龍遊宮沼矣神龜獻自越裳矣惟甘露
爲堯之上瑞焉然要其事天之敬則曰欽
若曰敬授要其格天之德則曰廣運曰允
恭聖人之所以得天者何其盛與洪惟我
太祖高皇帝開
天立極圖大宅中
鴻猷駿烈之盛卓冠百王鳳儀獸舞之化涵
濡萬類丕凝二極之和茂介三靈之祜大
順所召而諸福之物臻焉如彩霞絢而耀
漢卿雲爛以浮空赤烏集翔白兔馴伏寶
雞挺五穗之秀句容獻同蔕之瓜夫我
聖祖之瑞非不種種薦奇也然惟甘露之應
郊而零者尤見
帝心之特應焉初零于
乾清宮則頌獻于宋濂矣再零于鍾山則頌
獻于劉基矣迨洪武乙卯至日行
punctuated:
景星燦翼軫矣，昴星耀河渚矣，河圖出矣，醴泉溢矣，蓂莢生矣，神禾茂矣，鳳巢阿閣矣，龍遊宮沼矣，神龜獻自越裳矣，惟甘露爲堯之上瑞焉。然要其事天之敬，則曰欽若，曰敬授；要其格天之德，則曰廣運，曰允恭。聖人之所以得天者，何其盛與！
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，開天立極，圖大宅中，鴻猷駿烈之盛，卓冠百王；鳳儀獸舞之化，涵濡萬類。丕凝二極之和，茂介三靈之祜，大順所召，而諸福之物臻焉。如彩霞絢而耀漢，卿雲爛以浮空，赤烏集翔，白兔馴伏，寶雞挺五穗之秀，句容獻同蔕之瓜。夫我聖祖之瑞，非不種種薦奇也，然惟甘露之應郊而零者，尤見帝心之特應焉。初零于乾清宮，則頌獻于宋濂矣；再零于鍾山，則頌獻于劉基矣。迨洪武乙卯至日，行
translation_en:
…the auspicious star shone brilliantly in the lunar lodges Yi and Zhen; the Mao stars gleamed over the river islets; the River Chart appeared; springs of sweet water overflowed; the mingjia plant grew; divine grain flourished; phoenixes nested in the tiered pavilion; dragons swam in the palace pools; and a divine tortoise was presented from Yueshang. Yet sweet dew was Yao’s supreme auspicious sign. If we consider the reverence with which he served Heaven, it is described as “reverently following” and “reverently granting”; if we consider the virtue by which he reached Heaven, it is described as “far-reaching” and “truly reverent.” How magnificent was the sage’s attainment of Heaven’s favor!
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao opened Heaven and established the supreme standard, planned great undertakings, and occupied the center. The magnificence of his grand designs and mighty achievements surpassed that of all former kings; his transforming influence, which brought phoenixes to appear in stately bearing and beasts to dance, permeated and nourished all beings. He abundantly gathered the harmony of Heaven and Earth and richly received the blessings of the three celestial powers. Summoned by this great accord, all manner of objects betokening good fortune arrived: colorful clouds gleamed in the Milky Way; auspicious clouds floated resplendently through the sky; red crows gathered and soared; white rabbits submitted tamely; Baoji produced grain bearing five ears on a stalk; and Jurong presented melons sharing a single stem. Our sagely founder certainly received many wondrous auspicious signs in succession. Yet the sweet dew that fell in response to the suburban sacrifice especially revealed the particular response of the Heavenly Sovereign’s heart. When it first fell at the Palace of Heavenly Purity, Song Lian presented a eulogy; when it fell again at Zhongshan, Liu Ji presented a eulogy. Then, on the winter solstice of the yimao year of the Hongwu reign [1375], he performed …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
大報于
圜丘是夕也
聖祖方詣
齋宮省視壇壝而甘露即零于
齋宮之青松焉凝枝被杪上下懸垂瑩若明
珠甘若餳糖既
命從行諸臣共採而嘗之矣而我
聖祖敬天之心益祗畏而不敢懈也因
特著爲甘露論以示羣臣焉嘗伏讀而莊誦之
===
曰孔子覩麟而絕筆舜得鳳凰來儀而天下
安言徵符之協運也
曰嘉禎之心固篤爲善之心不厚言感召之
有本也
曰鬼神之機人莫可測言幾微之可畏也
曰聞祥而憂覩禎而慮言脩省之匪懈也
曰心驚晝夜如履薄氷言對越之匪寧也凡
若此者何莫非
聖祖一念之欽上通於
punctuated: 大報于圜丘。是夕也，聖祖方詣齋宮，省視壇壝，而甘露即零于齋宮之青松焉。凝枝被杪，上下懸垂，瑩若明珠，甘若餳糖。既命從行諸臣共採而嘗之矣，而我聖祖敬天之心益祗畏而不敢懈也。因特著爲《甘露論》，以示羣臣焉。嘗伏讀而莊誦之：曰：「孔子覩麟而絕筆，舜得鳳凰來儀而天下安。」言徵符之協運也。曰：「嘉禎之心固篤，爲善之心不厚。」言感召之有本也。曰：「鬼神之機，人莫可測。」言幾微之可畏也。曰：「聞祥而憂，覩禎而慮。」言脩省之匪懈也。曰：「心驚晝夜，如履薄氷。」言對越之匪寧也。凡若此者，何莫非聖祖一念之欽，上通於
translation_en:
…the great sacrifice of thanksgiving at the Circular Mound. That evening, just as the Sagely Founder went to the Palace of Abstinence to inspect the altar and its enclosing walls, sweet dew descended upon the palace’s green pines. It congealed on the branches and covered their tips, hanging at every height, lustrous as bright pearls and sweet as malt sugar. He ordered the officials accompanying him to gather and taste it together. Yet our Sagely Founder’s reverence for Heaven grew still more solemn and awestruck, and he dared not relax his vigilance. He therefore specially composed the Discourse on Sweet Dew to show his assembled officials. I have humbly read it and solemnly recited it:
It says: “Confucius beheld the qilin and laid down his brush; Shun had phoenixes come and display their stately bearing, and all under Heaven was at peace.” This speaks of auspicious signs accordant with the course of destiny.
It says: “The desire for auspicious omens is indeed strong, but the resolve to do good is not deep.” This speaks of the underlying basis for eliciting such responses.
It says: “The workings of ghosts and spirits are beyond human fathoming.” This speaks of the awe inspired by the slightest, incipient signs.
It says: “On hearing of auspicious signs, I worry; on beholding favorable omens, I reflect anxiously.” This speaks of unremitting self-cultivation and self-examination.
It says: “My heart is fearful day and night, as though treading on thin ice.” This speaks of never resting easy in reverently serving Heaven. Of all such expressions, which does not reveal the Sagely Founder’s single-minded reverence reaching upward to …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
天者乎
列聖相承雍熙累洽肆我
皇上
恭默握
神之符
明聖得
天之統
建中建極達馨治於神明
盡制盡倫符精誠於
===
聖祖
玄麻日迓
帝眷雲臻灝氣昭融而
神貺駢集焉瑞穎秀於
御籍嘉穀挺於鄭梁衡精萃雙孕之禎玉蘂繞
太皓之色甲現四靈之兆芝蕃二氣之□
大我
皇上之瑞非不穰穰滋至也然惟甘露之應
郊而零者尤見
punctuated:
天者乎？

列聖相承，雍熙累洽。肆我皇上，恭默握神之符，明聖得天之統，建中建極，達馨治於神明；盡制盡倫，符精誠於聖祖。玄麻日迓，帝眷雲臻，灝氣昭融，而神貺駢集焉。瑞穎秀於御籍，嘉穀挺於鄭梁，衡精萃雙孕之禎，玉蘂繞太皓之色，甲現四靈之兆，芝蕃二氣之□。大我皇上之瑞，非不穰穰滋至也。然惟甘露之應郊而零者，尤見
translation_en:
…Heaven?

The successive sage emperors inherited the throne, and harmony and prosperity grew ever more pervasive. Thus our Emperor, reverent and reserved, holds the token of divine authority; enlightened and sagely, he has received Heaven’s succession. He establishes the mean and the supreme standard, making the fragrance of his good government reach the spirits. He fulfills every institution and every human relationship, matching the Sacred Progenitor in perfect sincerity. “Dark hemp” [?] is welcomed daily; the favor of the Lord on High arrives like gathering clouds. The vast vital breath shines in harmonious brilliance, and divine gifts arrive in profusion. Auspicious ears of grain flourish in the imperial ploughing field; excellent grain rises in Zheng and Liang. The essence of Heng [?] concentrates in the auspicious sign of paired offspring; jade blossoms encircle the coloration of Taihao [?]. A shell displays an omen of the Four Numinous Creatures; numinous fungi proliferate through the two vital breaths’ [illegible]. The auspicious signs of our great Emperor have indeed arrived in ever-increasing abundance. Yet the sweet dew that fell in response to the suburban sacrifice especially reveals…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
帝心之特應焉蓋嘉靖辛卯至日行
大報于
圜丘是夕也珠星濩于銀漢瑞色藹於蒼欄而
甘露旋零于
皇考棲神之地焉既
命宗伯卜吉具儀以謝
帝之既矣而我
皇上敬天之心益祇畏而不敢懈也因
特製爲
===
欽天記頌以
頒勳輔焉嘗伏讀而莊誦之
曰上荷
簡在銘心欽戴
曰上荷
眷殊罔敢自娛是時幾之勑也
曰典禮肅雍戒誓惟恭
曰禮嚴禋燎仰瞻
帝容是肆類之誠也
punctuated:
帝心之特應焉。蓋嘉靖辛卯至日，行大報于圜丘。是夕也，珠星濩于銀漢，瑞色藹於蒼欄，而甘露旋零于皇考棲神之地焉。既命宗伯卜吉具儀，以謝帝之既矣，而我皇上敬天之心益祇畏而不敢懈也。因特製爲《欽天記頌》，以頒勳輔焉。嘗伏讀而莊誦之。
曰：「上荷簡在，銘心欽戴。」曰：「上荷眷殊，罔敢自娛。」是時幾之勑也。
曰：「典禮肅雍，戒誓惟恭。」曰：「禮嚴禋燎，仰瞻帝容。」是肆類之誠也。
translation_en:
…a special response from the heart of the Lord on High. On the winter solstice of the xinmao year of Jiajing, the great sacrifice of thanksgiving was performed at the Circular Mound. That evening, pearl-like stars spread across the Silver River, auspicious radiance gathered about the azure balustrades, and sweet dew soon descended upon the place where the spirit of the Emperor’s deceased father rested. He then commanded the Minister of Rites to divine an auspicious day and prepare the ceremonies to offer thanks to the Lord on High [the wording here is doubtful: 帝之既矣]. Yet our Emperor’s reverence for Heaven grew ever more devout and apprehensive, and he dared not relax his vigilance. He therefore personally composed the Record and Hymn on Revering Heaven (Qintian ji song), which he distributed to meritorious nobles and assisting ministers. I have reverently read it and solemnly recited it.
It says: “Favored from above with selection, I engrave this upon my heart and reverently bear it.” It says: “Favored from above with exceptional care, I dare not indulge in pleasure.” This is an admonition to vigilance over the times and the first stirrings of events [?].
It says: “The prescribed rites are solemn and harmonious; in admonitions and injunctions, all is reverence.” It says: “The rites of pure sacrifice and burnt offerings are solemn; looking upward, I behold the countenance of the Lord on High.” This is sincerity in performing the lei sacrifice to Heaven.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
曰敢廿自侈夙夜勉脩
曰誠惶誠恐懼惟弗遑是昭格之敬也
曰
神功惟
祖受
天之祜
曰
玄德惟
考荷
===
天之保是繹思之孝也
曰滋我禾稼賜我豐年
曰兆民其綏五福是徵是勤恤之仁也凡若
此者何莫非我
皇上一念之欽上通於
天者乎夫甘露上瑞也一零於乙卯
郊報之日一零於辛卯
郊報之日益瑞也蓋卯木也於四序爲春令於
東方爲長生我
punctuated:
曰：「敢廿自侈，夙夜勉脩。」曰：「誠惶誠恐，懼惟弗遑。」是昭格之敬也。曰：「神功惟祖，受天之祜。」曰：「玄德惟考，荷天之保。」是繹思之孝也。曰：「滋我禾稼，賜我豐年。」曰：「兆民其綏，五福是徵。」是勤恤之仁也。
凡若此者，何莫非我皇上一念之欽，上通於天者乎？夫甘露，上瑞也。一零於乙卯郊報之日，一零於辛卯郊報之日，益瑞也。蓋卯，木也；於四序爲春令，於東方爲長生。我
translation_en:
…It says: “Would I dare indulge in extravagance [?]? Morning and night I strive to cultivate myself.” It says: “In utmost trepidation and fear, apprehensive, I have no leisure.” This is the reverence that brings the spirits to manifest their presence. It says: “My forebear, whose achievements were divine, received Heaven’s blessing.” It says: “My late father, whose virtue was profound, enjoyed Heaven’s protection.” This is the filial devotion of sustained remembrance. It says: “Nourish our grain crops; grant us an abundant year.” It says: “May the myriad people be at peace; may the five blessings be made manifest.” This is the benevolence of diligent care for the people.
Of all such utterances, which does not express a single reverent thought of our August Sovereign reaching upward to Heaven? Sweet dew is a supreme auspicious sign. That it descended once on the yimao day of the suburban sacrifice of thanksgiving, and once on the xinmao day of the suburban sacrifice of thanksgiving, makes it still more auspicious. For mao corresponds to Wood; among the four seasons it governs spring, and in the east it signifies the beginning of life. Our …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
明以土德王而木以生火爲土之祖焉故
郊期而輙應者烝之元也靈之會也
玄元篤祜之極也非我
聖祖我
皇上心純於敬德純於天其曷以媲虞庭之盛
而超萬禩之隆也哉此其感通乎格之妙
有非末學所能窺測者而執事又欲鋪張
而推原之愚則以爲我
聖祖我
===
皇上之敬穆穆乎不可窺也而敬之著於外者
益以精我
聖祖我
皇上之德蕩蕩乎不可名也而德之溢於政者
益以大是故敬以純此心則爲事天德以
養此心則爲格天其理非有二也事天之
心既誠則格天之驗益著其機亦非有二
也嘗觀我
聖祖養心之學而見其得
punctuated: 明以土德王，而木以生火，爲土之祖焉。故郊期而輙應者，烝之元也，靈之會也，玄元篤祜之極也。非我聖祖、我皇上心純於敬、德純於天，其曷以媲虞庭之盛，而超萬禩之隆也哉？此其感通乎格之妙，有非末學所能窺測者。而執事又欲鋪張而推原之，愚則以爲我聖祖、我皇上之敬，穆穆乎不可窺也，而敬之著於外者益以精；我聖祖、我皇上之德，蕩蕩乎不可名也，而德之溢於政者益以大。是故敬以純此心，則爲事天；德以養此心，則爲格天。其理非有二也。事天之心既誠，則格天之驗益著，其機亦非有二也。嘗觀我聖祖養心之學，而見其得
translation_en:
…Ming rules through the potency of Earth, while Wood, by generating Fire, is the ancestor of Earth. Thus, that auspicious responses invariably occur at the appointed suburban sacrifices represents the primal source of abundance [?], the convergence of numinous powers, and the culmination of profound blessings from the mysterious Origin. Had our Sagely Ancestor and our Emperor not possessed hearts devoted purely to reverence and virtue wholly aligned with Heaven, how could they have matched the splendor of Shun’s court and surpassed the magnificence of ten thousand ages? The marvel of this sympathetic communion and reaching Heaven [?] is beyond the capacity of a scholar of shallow learning to fathom. Yet you, honored examiners, wish me to expound upon it and trace its source.

In my humble view, the reverence of our Sagely Ancestor and our Emperor is so solemn and majestic that it cannot be fathomed; yet its outward manifestations grow ever more refined. The virtue of our Sagely Ancestor and our Emperor is so vast that it cannot be named; yet its expression in government grows ever greater. Thus, to purify this heart through reverence is to serve Heaven; to nourish this heart through virtue is to move Heaven. These are not two distinct principles. Once the heart that serves Heaven is sincere, the evidence of its moving Heaven becomes ever more manifest. Nor are there two distinct workings here. I have considered our Sagely Ancestor’s learning in nourishing the heart and have seen how he attained…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
天之本矣告
南郊之詔則曰人以一心對越上帝動天地感
鬼神惟誠與敬嚴祭祀之章則曰精誠則
福至怠慢則禍生大哉
王言所以預養是心者無一念而非
天心矣故以此心而事神焉則
郊社羣祀之有制也
四廟祫祭之有儀也嶽瀆名臣之封號不濫也
先農大歲之常祀不略也事神之敬在是
===
省之誠在是矣以此心而子民焉則肆赦
齋禱禁中臨祭而反覩䢵聽上契冲漠脩
矣以此心而脩省焉則遇災而席藁露坐
有
詔以示欽恤蠲租有
詔以惠困窮至於假暑日之農而甘徒步因賑
濟之緩而罪中書子民之仁在是矣若此
者莫非敬也莫非德也則亦莫非
天之心也我
punctuated: 天之本矣。告南郊之詔則曰：「人以一心對越上帝，動天地，感鬼神，惟誠與敬。」嚴祭祀之章則曰：「精誠則福至，怠慢則禍生。」大哉，王言！所以預養是心者，無一念而非天心矣。故以此心而事神焉，則郊社羣祀之有制也，四廟祫祭之有儀也，嶽瀆名臣之封號不濫也，先農大歲之常祀不略也，事神之敬在是，省之誠在是矣。以此心而子民焉，則肆赦，齋禱禁中，臨祭而反覩䢵聽，上契冲漠脩矣。以此心而脩省焉，則遇災而席藁露坐，有詔以示欽恤；蠲租，有詔以惠困窮。至於假暑日之農而甘徒步，因賑濟之緩而罪中書，子民之仁在是矣。若此者，莫非敬也，莫非德也，則亦莫非天之心也。我
translation_en: …the foundation for winning Heaven’s favor. The edict announcing the sacrifice at the Southern Suburb declares: “With a single heart a person stands reverently before the Lord on High. What moves Heaven and Earth and touches the spirits is sincerity and reverence alone.” The proclamation enjoining solemnity in sacrifices declares: “Perfect sincerity brings blessings; negligence and disrespect bring calamity.” How great are these royal words! In thus nurturing this heart beforehand, not a single thought departs from the heart of Heaven. Thus, when he serves the spirits with this heart, there are established regulations for the suburban sacrifices, the sacrifices at the altars of soil, and the various other rites; prescribed ceremonies for the joint sacrifice at the four ancestral temples; no indiscriminate bestowal of titles upon the sacred peaks, waterways, and illustrious ministers; and no neglect of the regular sacrifices to the First Farmer and the deity of the year. Herein lies his reverence in serving the spirits; herein lies the sincerity of his self-examination [?]. When he treats the people as his children with this heart, he proclaims general pardons, fasts and prays within the palace, and personally attends sacrifices, turning his sight and hearing inward [?] and attaining accord above with the silent, formless realm [?]. When he cultivates and examines himself with this heart, he responds to calamities by sitting on straw in the open air and issuing edicts to display reverent concern; he remits taxes and issues edicts to benefit those in hardship and poverty. He even gives farmers respite on hot summer days and willingly travels on foot [?], and punishes the Secretariat for delays in distributing relief. Herein lies his benevolence in treating the people as his children. All such acts are reverence; all are virtue; and all therefore express the heart of Heaven. Our…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖祖所以事
天格
天眷何其至耶又嘗觀我
皇上養心之學而見其得
天之本矣
敬一之箴
曰匪敬弗聚匪一弗純
曰郊則恭誠廟嚴孝趨
曰肅于明庭愼于閑居大哉
===
王言所以涵養是心者亦無一念而非
天心矣故以此心而享
帝享
親也則上
泰壇之號正分祀之儀而享
帝之典以備肇
九廟之明禋定
明堂之配享而
尊親之義以隆非仁孝之精乎以此心而畏
punctuated: 聖祖所以事天、格天眷，何其至耶！又嘗觀我皇上養心之學，而見其得天之本矣。《敬一之箴》曰：「匪敬弗聚，匪一弗純。」曰：「郊則恭誠，廟嚴孝趨。」曰：「肅于明庭，愼于閑居。」大哉王言！所以涵養是心者，亦無一念而非天心矣。故以此心而享帝、享親也，則上泰壇之號，正分祀之儀，而享帝之典以備；肇九廟之明禋，定明堂之配享，而尊親之義以隆，非仁孝之精乎？以此心而畏
translation_en:
…How consummate were the ways in which our sagely founder served Heaven and drew Heaven’s favor! I have also considered our emperor’s learning in nurturing the mind and perceived therein the foundation by which he gains Heaven’s favor. His Admonition on Reverence and Oneness states: “Without reverence, the mind cannot be gathered together; without oneness, it cannot be pure.” It also states: “At the suburban sacrifice, be reverent and sincere; in the ancestral temple, proceed solemnly and filially.” And again: “Be solemn in the public court and cautious in private retirement.” Great indeed are these royal words! In nurturing this mind, not a single thought departs from the mind of Heaven.
Thus, when he brings this mind to offering sacrifices to the Supreme Lord and to his ancestors, he bestows the designation ‘Great Altar’ and rectifies the ceremonies of separate sacrifice, thereby completing the rites for sacrificing to the Supreme Lord. He inaugurates the pure sacrifices at the Nine Ancestral Temples and determines the associated worship in the Hall of Light, thereby exalting the principle of honoring his forebears. Is this not the purest expression of benevolence and filial piety? When he brings this mind to standing in awe…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
大事
天也則星變有
勑以謹時幾除夕有
作以寓惕勵因風霾而感上天之警遇旱潦
而竭恭禱之虔非誠敬之極乎以此心而
敷政勤民也則
豳風
無逸之構念稼穡之惟艱
先農壇
===
穀祈之章重農桑之大本發
內帑以賑貧窮
詔慎獄以重民命非勤民之政乎若此者莫非
敬也莫非德也則亦莫非法
祖之心也我
皇上所以事
天格
天者何其至耶夫惟敬以合
天心則
punctuated: 大事天也，則星變有勑，以謹時幾；除夕有作，以寓惕勵；因風霾而感上天之警，遇旱潦而竭恭禱之虔，非誠敬之極乎？以此心而敷政勤民也，則豳風、無逸之構，念稼穡之惟艱；先農壇穀祈之章，重農桑之大本；發內帑以賑貧窮，詔慎獄以重民命，非勤民之政乎？若此者，莫非敬也，莫非德也，則亦莫非法祖之心也。我皇上所以事天格天者，何其至耶！夫惟敬以合天心，則
translation_en: …in serving Heaven in great affairs [?], when stellar anomalies occur, he issues an edict to attend carefully to the incipient signs of the times; on New Year’s Eve, he composes a work expressing vigilance and self-admonition. Winds and dust storms move him to heed Heaven’s warnings; droughts and floods draw forth the utmost sincerity of his reverent prayers. Is this not sincerity and reverence carried to their highest degree? When he applies this same heart to administering government and caring diligently for the people, the structures associated with the Odes of Bin (Bin feng) and Against Ease (Wu yi) express his concern for the hardships of sowing and reaping. His composition on praying for grain at the Altar of the First Farmer [?] honors agriculture and sericulture as the great foundation. He releases funds from the palace treasury to relieve the poor and destitute, and commands caution in adjudicating criminal cases out of regard for the people’s lives. Is this not government devoted to the people? All such acts embody reverence; all embody virtue; and all therefore embody the resolve to emulate the ancestors. How consummate are the means by which our Emperor serves Heaven and moves Heaven to respond! For only through reverence does one accord with Heaven’s heart; then…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
天祐彌昌德以格
天心則
天眷愈篤此所以綿萬禩之
洪禧開億齡之泰運豈非理數之必然者與雖
然愚猶有說焉惟天聰明惟聖時憲我
皇上敬一之德卽
天之德
聖祖之德也書言惟時惟幾而首言勑天之命
詩言上天之載而復約之以儀刑文王萬
===
邦作孚是敬一者所以法
祖卽所以敬
天也天之道其神不已其運不積如環無端我
皇上會天地翕聚恒久之理於一心則天下之
精神命脈自我而萃之豈非
聖壽萬年配
天無極之徵驗與文王之詩曰昭事上帝聿懷
多福天保之詩曰萬壽無疆如南山之壽
敢以是頌
punctuated:
天祐彌昌；德以格天心，則天眷愈篤。此所以綿萬禩之洪禧，開億齡之泰運，豈非理數之必然者與？雖然，愚猶有說焉。惟天聰明，惟聖時憲。我皇上敬一之德，卽天之德、聖祖之德也。《書》言「惟時惟幾」，而首言「勑天之命」；《詩》言「上天之載」，而復約之以「儀刑文王，萬邦作孚」。是敬一者，所以法祖，卽所以敬天也。
天之道，其神不已，其運不積，如環無端。我皇上會天地翕聚恒久之理於一心，則天下之精神命脈自我而萃之，豈非聖壽萬年、配天無極之徵驗與？《文王》之詩曰：「昭事上帝，聿懷多福。」《天保》之詩曰：「萬壽無疆，如南山之壽。」敢以是頌
translation_en:
…Heaven’s blessings become ever more abundant; when virtue moves Heaven’s heart, Heaven’s favor grows ever deeper. This is how great blessings are extended through ten thousand years and an auspicious course is opened for a hundred million years. Is this not the inevitable outcome of principle and cosmic destiny? Even so, I, in my humble judgment, have something further to say. Heaven alone is discerning and wise, and the sage takes it as his model. Our emperor’s virtue of reverent single-mindedness is precisely the virtue of Heaven and of the sagely ancestor. The Book of Documents speaks of attending to proper timing and the first stirrings of events, but first speaks of heeding Heaven’s mandate. The Book of Odes speaks of Heaven’s workings above, then sums up its teaching with: “Take King Wen as your model, and the myriad states will trust you.” Thus, reverent single-mindedness is the means of emulating the ancestor and, thereby, of revering Heaven.
Heaven’s Way is unceasing in its spiritual efficacy; its movement never stagnates, like a ring without an endpoint. Our emperor gathers within his single heart the principles by which Heaven and Earth unite and endure. Thus, the spiritual energies and vital lifeblood of all under Heaven converge through our sovereign. Is this not evidence that his sagely life will last ten thousand years, matching Heaven without limit? The ode “King Wen” says: “Illustriously he served the Lord on High, thereby cherishing manifold blessings.” The ode “Heaven Protects” says: “May your myriad years know no bounds, enduring like the Southern Mountain.” With these words I venture to praise…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖天子得天之慶
第二問
米成道
同考試官教諭吳　批〔論學不在詞章歸本道德且於心術邪正名實誠僞之辨剖析幾微子之學可知矣〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔是作商確古今評品學術卓有定見是學古而有獲者〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔議論精到可錄〕
學一也而古今異焉心迹之間而已矣心
===
一也而古今異焉內外之辨而已矣古之
人惟其求諸內也則大本旣立而博物洽
聞無非養吾心者是以心與迹一而爲國
爲民莫非學也亦莫非道也此德業益懋
而詩書爲經世之大典今之人惟其求諸
外也則大本旣撥而博物洽聞無非爲乎
人者是以心與迹戾而狥名狥利莫非學
也亦莫非利也此德業無聞而詩書爲埀
世之虛文然則古之所以大過人者非夫
punctuated:
聖天子得天之慶。

第二問
米成道

同考試官教諭吳　批〔論學不在詞章，歸本道德，且於心術邪正、名實誠僞之辨，剖析幾微，子之學可知矣。〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔是作商確古今，評品學術，卓有定見，是學古而有獲者。〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔議論精到，可錄。〕

學一也，而古今異焉，心迹之間而已矣。心一也，而古今異焉，內外之辨而已矣。古之人惟其求諸內也，則大本旣立，而博物洽聞，無非養吾心者。是以心與迹一，而爲國爲民，莫非學也，亦莫非道也。此德業益懋，而詩書爲經世之大典。今之人惟其求諸外也，則大本旣撥，而博物洽聞，無非爲乎人者。是以心與迹戾，而狥名狥利，莫非學也，亦莫非利也。此德業無聞，而詩書爲埀世之虛文。然則古之所以大過人者，非夫
translation_en:
…the blessings that the sagely Son of Heaven receives from Heaven.

Second Question
Mi Chengdao

Associate Examiner Wu, an Instructor, comments: 〔In discussing learning, you locate its foundation in moral virtue rather than literary composition. Moreover, you closely analyze the subtle distinctions between depravity and rectitude in the workings of the mind, and between reputation and reality, sincerity and falsity. From this, the character of your learning can be discerned.〕

Examiner Liu, an Instructor, comments: 〔This essay weighs past and present and evaluates approaches to learning with notably firm judgment. Its author has gained something from studying antiquity.〕

Examiner Hu, an Instructor, comments: 〔The argument is penetrating and precise; it merits selection.〕

Learning is one, yet it differs between antiquity and the present. This is simply a matter of the relationship between the mind and outward conduct. The mind is one, yet it differs between antiquity and the present. This is simply a matter of distinguishing the inward from the outward. Precisely because the ancients sought within themselves, their great foundation was established, and their extensive knowledge of things and broad learning all served to nourish their minds. Thus mind and conduct were united: everything they did for the state and the people was learning, and everything accorded with the Way. Consequently, their virtue and accomplishments grew ever more splendid, and the Book of Odes and Book of Documents served as great canons for governing the world.

Precisely because people today seek outside themselves, their great foundation is undermined, and their extensive knowledge of things and broad learning all serve to impress others. Thus mind and conduct are at odds: their pursuit of reputation and profit is all counted as learning, yet it is all a pursuit of gain. Consequently, their virtue and accomplishments go unheard of, while the Book of Odes and Book of Documents become empty writings handed down to the world. Thus, what enabled the ancients so greatly to surpass others was not something that everyone…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
人而能之也詩書之道歸焉耳今之所以
不古若者非詩書之敎使然也人自外之
耳學其可發乎哉孔子曰古之學者爲已
今之學者爲人又曰君子喻於義小人喻
於利明乎此而學術誠僞之判世道升降
之機可得而言矣愚請以是爲明問復且
國風雅頌之前果無詩乎擊壤康衢卿雲
南薰惟自適其性情而不規規於歌詠之
體故其惇厚和平權輿三百而亦未嘗以
===
詩名也孔子懼夫性情不明於後世由是
六義之中分爲四始音比節合皆可以被
諸管弦肄諸學校無非欲人諷詠涵濡以
爲身心性情之資齊治均平之本返古復
始而已典謨訓誥之前果無書乎取火結
繩造曆制市惟自立其政事而不屑屑于
紀注之迹故其正大光明卓冠百王而亦
未嘗以書名也孔子懼夫政事不明于後
世由是歷代之書釐爲四卷文異治同皆
punctuated:
人而能之也，詩書之道歸焉耳。今之所以不古若者，非詩書之敎使然也，人自外之耳。學其可發乎哉？孔子曰：「古之學者爲已，今之學者爲人。」又曰：「君子喻於義，小人喻於利。」明乎此，而學術誠僞之判、世道升降之機，可得而言矣。愚請以是爲明問復。
且國風雅頌之前，果無詩乎？擊壤、康衢、卿雲、南薰，惟自適其性情，而不規規於歌詠之體，故其惇厚和平，權輿三百，而亦未嘗以詩名也。孔子懼夫性情不明於後世，由是六義之中，分爲四始，音比節合，皆可以被諸管弦，肄諸學校，無非欲人諷詠涵濡，以爲身心性情之資、齊治均平之本，返古復始而已。
典謨訓誥之前，果無書乎？取火、結繩、造曆、制市，惟自立其政事，而不屑屑于紀注之迹，故其正大光明，卓冠百王，而亦未嘗以書名也。孔子懼夫政事不明于後世，由是歷代之書，釐爲四卷，文異治同，皆
translation_en:
…men alone being capable of it; it was simply that the Way of the Odes and Documents found its home in them. That people today do not equal the ancients is not the result of the teachings of the Odes and Documents: people themselves stand outside them. Can learning, then, be brought forth [?]? Confucius said, “Those who studied in antiquity did so for themselves; those who study today do so for others.” He also said, “The gentleman understands righteousness; the petty man understands profit.” Once this is understood, we can discuss the distinction between sincerity and falsity in learning, and the critical factors in the rise and decline of the moral order. I humbly offer this in reply to your discerning question.
Moreover, before the Airs of the States, the Elegantiae, and the Hymns, were there truly no poems? The songs Beating the Earth (Ji rang), The Broad Highway (Kang qu), Auspicious Clouds (Qing yun), and The Southern Breeze (Nan xun) simply gave free expression to people's nature and feelings, without narrowly adhering to the forms of song. Their sincerity, generosity, harmony, and peace thus foreshadowed the Three Hundred Odes, yet they were never designated as the Odes. Confucius feared that human nature and feelings would not be understood by later generations. Accordingly, within the six principles of poetry he distinguished the four beginnings. With their sounds coordinated and rhythms harmonized, all could be set to pipes and strings and rehearsed in the schools. His sole intention was that people should recite and sing them and become steeped in them, making them a resource for cultivating body, mind, nature, and feelings, and a foundation for ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing equity and peace—all simply to return to antiquity and recover the beginnings.
Before the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements, were there truly no documents? Making fire, knotting cords, devising a calendar, and establishing markets were simply ways of instituting government, without fussing over the outward forms of written records. Their uprightness, greatness, brilliance, and clarity thus surpassed those of the hundred kings, yet they were never designated as the Documents. Confucius feared that government would not be understood by later generations. Accordingly, he arranged the documents of successive ages into four volumes. Their writings differed, but their principles of government were the same; all…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
可以竝列學宮廣置博士無非欲人沈潛
參考以審理欲危微之幾治亂存亡之迹
返朴還淳而已是故苟有得于性情則不
必博觀風雅而溫柔敦厚之教存苟有得
于政事則不必徧閱訓誥而疏通知遠之
教立傅說所謂學古有獲者學此者也非
後世玩物喪志之謂此儒者所以守之也
子路所謂何必讀書者廢此者也非聖門
神明默成之旨此孔子所以疾之也稷契
===
皐夔都俞吁咈于一堂之上者皆精一執
中之旨推之於佐理則時雍風動之化成
焉人事之所在卽墳典之所在也何必求
之於簡編之末謨明協和于海隅之外者
皆明良喜起之盛紀之於載籍則德業勳
名之範垂焉今之墳典皆古之人事也又
何必考其誦讀之原伊尹左右商王纘禹
舊服奄甸萬姓格于皇天說者謂其出于
誦讀矣而不知其學心學也稷契皐夔之
punctuated: 可以竝列學宮，廣置博士，無非欲人沈潛參考，以審理欲危微之幾、治亂存亡之迹，返朴還淳而已。是故苟有得于性情，則不必博觀風雅，而溫柔敦厚之教存；苟有得于政事，則不必徧閱訓誥，而疏通知遠之教立。傅說所謂「學古有獲」者，學此者也，非後世玩物喪志之謂，此儒者所以守之也。子路所謂「何必讀書」者，廢此者也，非聖門神明默成之旨，此孔子所以疾之也。稷契皐夔都俞吁咈于一堂之上者，皆精一執中之旨，推之於佐理，則時雍風動之化成焉。人事之所在，卽墳典之所在也，何必求之於簡編之末？謨明協和于海隅之外者，皆明良喜起之盛，紀之於載籍，則德業勳名之範垂焉。今之墳典，皆古之人事也，又何必考其誦讀之原？伊尹左右商王，纘禹舊服，奄甸萬姓，格于皇天，說者謂其出于誦讀矣，而不知其學，心學也，稷契皐夔之
translation_en:
…could all be placed together in the schools, with Erudites appointed in ample numbers. The sole purpose was to have people immerse themselves in study and compare the texts, discerning the subtle workings of moral principle and human desire, the precarious human mind and the subtle moral mind, and the traces of order and disorder, survival and ruin, so as to return to simplicity and purity.

Thus, if one has gained an understanding of human nature and feeling, one need not read widely through the Airs and Odes for their teaching of gentleness, sincerity, and generosity to be present. If one has gained an understanding of government, one need not read all the Instructions and Announcements for their teaching of penetrating understanding and knowledge of the distant past to be established. What Fu Yue called “gaining something through studying antiquity” means learning these things; it does not mean the later practice of losing one’s purpose through fixation on external things. This is why Confucian scholars uphold such learning. Zilu’s remark, “Why must one read books?” discards this learning; it does not express the sages’ teaching of spiritual understanding and silent accomplishment. This is why Confucius deplored it.

When Ji, Qi, Gao Yao, and Kui voiced approval and dissent together in one hall, all their words embodied the principle of refinement, singleness of purpose, and holding fast to the mean. Applied to assisting in government, this brought about a transformation in which all lived in harmony and responded as though moved by the wind. Wherever human affairs are found, there too are the ancient canonical writings. Why must one seek them in the secondary details of written texts? The enlightened counsels and concord that reached beyond the shores of the seas all expressed the flourishing cooperation of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers, rejoicing and rousing themselves to action. Recorded in books, these handed down models of virtue, achievement, meritorious service, and renown. Today’s ancient canonical writings are all the human affairs of antiquity. Why, then, must one investigate the origins of their recitation and reading?

Yi Yin assisted the king of Shang, continued Yu’s former undertakings, brought the myriad families under his governance, and reached August Heaven. Commentators say that these accomplishments arose from recitation and reading, but they do not understand that his learning was the learning of the mind—the learning of Ji, Qi, Gao Yao, and Kui…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
學也其告太甲曰德無常師主善爲師善
無常主協于克一則師且無常也而誦讀
果足以盡其學與太公涼彼武王會朝清
明作師礪褓表兹東海說者疑其出于陰
謀矣而不知其學心學也稷契皐夔之學
也其答武王曰敬勝怠者吉怠勝敬者滅
義勝欲者從欲勝義者凶則誦讀且不足
道也而陰謀果可以擬之與後世事其外
而遺其內徇其迹而不究其心公孫弘當
===
元光之際詔應賢良擢居第一則海上春
秋之學宜其敷陳尊王賤霸之古無媿于
仲舒矣何其多詐無實致轅固曲學之譏
兹非學春秋而不知春秋者乎谷永値建
始之時舉由慶忌待詔公車則博學經書
之後宜其有直言敢諫之風不忝于更生
矣何其倚勢固位諛王鳳申伯之忠兹非
博經書而不知經書者乎桓榮備給力學
不窺家園後以敷奏經書致位少傅所遇
punctuated: 學也。其告太甲曰：「德無常師，主善爲師；善無常主，協于克一。」則師且無常也，而誦讀果足以盡其學與？太公涼彼武王，會朝清明，作師礪褓，表兹東海。說者疑其出于陰謀矣，而不知其學，心學也，稷契皐夔之學也。其答武王曰：「敬勝怠者吉，怠勝敬者滅；義勝欲者從，欲勝義者凶。」則誦讀且不足道也，而陰謀果可以擬之與？後世事其外而遺其內，徇其迹而不究其心。公孫弘當元光之際，詔應賢良，擢居第一，則海上春秋之學，宜其敷陳尊王賤霸之古，無媿于仲舒矣。何其多詐無實，致轅固曲學之譏？兹非學春秋而不知春秋者乎？谷永値建始之時，舉由慶忌，待詔公車，則博學經書之後，宜其有直言敢諫之風，不忝于更生矣。何其倚勢固位，諛王鳳申伯之忠？兹非博經書而不知經書者乎？桓榮備給力學，不窺家園，後以敷奏經書，致位少傅，所遇
translation_en:
…learning. He told Tai Jia: “In cultivating virtue there is no constant teacher; take goodness as your teacher. Goodness has no constant master; accord with the ability to remain single-minded.” If even one’s teacher is not fixed, can recitation and reading truly encompass all his learning? Taigong assisted King Wu; at their morning assembly all was clear and bright. He served as a teacher, a whetstone, and a protector [?], and became an exemplar in the eastern coastal region. Commentators suspect that his achievements arose from secret stratagems, yet they do not understand that his learning was the learning of the mind—the learning of Ji, Xie, Gao, and Kui. He answered King Wu: “When reverence overcomes indolence, there is good fortune; when indolence overcomes reverence, there is destruction. When righteousness overcomes desire, things go well; when desire overcomes righteousness, there is disaster.” Here even recitation and reading scarcely merit mention; can secret stratagems truly be compared with his learning? Later generations attend to its exterior and neglect its interior, follow its traces without probing its heart.

During the Yuanguang era, Gongsun Hong responded to an imperial summons for worthy and good men and was ranked first. With his learning in the Spring and Autumn Annals acquired by the sea, he ought to have expounded the ancient teaching [?] of honoring true kings and devaluing hegemons, without falling short of Zhongshu. Why, then, was he so full of deceit and devoid of substance that he provoked Yuan Gu’s criticism of his bending learning to suit others? Was he not someone who studied the Spring and Autumn Annals without understanding it?

During the Jianshi era, Gu Yong was recommended by Qingji and awaited an imperial summons at the Office of the Majors in Charge of Official Carriages. After his extensive study of the classics, he ought to have displayed a disposition to speak frankly and remonstrate boldly, without falling short of Gengsheng. Why, then, did he rely on powerful patrons to secure his position, flattering Wang Feng by attributing to him the loyalty of the Earl of Shen? Was he not someone extensively versed in the classics who nevertheless did not understand them?

Huan Rong provided for his needs [?] and studied diligently, never even looking into his home garden. Later, through his presentations and expositions of the classics, he rose to the position of Junior Preceptor. The circumstances he encountered…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
不爲不偶矣至輜車乘馬之賜會勉諸生
不知稽古之力豈爲是乎無惑乎其自謂
執經連年無補萬分也馬融從遊摯恂博
通經籍後以典校祕書重詣東觀其望不
爲不隆矣至教授生徒之際後列女樂不
知範物之地當如是乎何怪乎其晚節黨
附權勢爲正直羞也開心明目讀書之益
大矣何乃有不識剛正字若張禹者不識
進退字若孔光者不識忠孝字若許敬宗
===
者不識節義字若柳宗元者則其博聞強
記不過爲獵華躡要之階操觚染翰之具
耳所謂買櫝還珠者非耶經術經世安石
之說似矣何乃謂天變不足畏人言不足
恤祖宗之法不足守則其苦心力學不過
借周官已試之法以濟强辯執拗之見耳
所謂操戈入室者非耶蓋三代而上學本
于身心故誦讀雖約而能獨究夫民彝天
理之微三代而下學出于口耳故誦讀雖
punctuated: 不爲不偶矣。至輜車乘馬之賜，會勉諸生，不知稽古之力豈爲是乎？無惑乎其自謂執經連年，無補萬分也。馬融從遊摯恂，博通經籍，後以典校祕書，重詣東觀，其望不爲不隆矣。至教授生徒之際，後列女樂，不知範物之地當如是乎？何怪乎其晚節黨附權勢，爲正直羞也。開心明目，讀書之益大矣。何乃有不識剛正字若張禹者，不識進退字若孔光者，不識忠孝字若許敬宗者，不識節義字若柳宗元者？則其博聞強記，不過爲獵華躡要之階、操觚染翰之具耳。所謂買櫝還珠者，非耶？經術經世，安石之說似矣。何乃謂天變不足畏，人言不足恤，祖宗之法不足守？則其苦心力學，不過借周官已試之法，以濟强辯執拗之見耳。所謂操戈入室者，非耶？蓋三代而上，學本于身心，故誦讀雖約，而能獨究夫民彝天理之微；三代而下，學出于口耳，故誦讀雖
translation_en:
…his circumstances could hardly be called unpropitious. Yet when he received the gift of a baggage carriage and a team of four horses, he assembled his students to encourage them. Did he not understand that the purpose of studying antiquity could hardly be this? Little wonder that he himself said that, despite years of expounding the Classics, he had contributed not even one ten-thousandth of what was needed.

Ma Rong studied under Zhi Xun and gained a comprehensive command of the Classics. Later, charged with collating the imperial library’s books, he went again to the Eastern Pavilion. His reputation could hardly be called anything but eminent. Yet when teaching his students, he stationed female musicians behind him. Did he not understand how one ought to conduct oneself in a position that served as a model for others? Why wonder that in his later years he attached himself to the powerful and brought shame upon the upright?

Reading opens the mind and clarifies the vision: its benefits are great indeed. Why, then, were there men like Zhang Yu, who did not understand the words “firmness and rectitude”; Kong Guang, who did not understand “advancing and withdrawing”; Xu Jingzong, who did not understand “loyalty and filial piety”; and Liu Zongyuan, who did not understand “integrity and righteousness”? Their extensive learning and powerful memories were merely stepping-stones for hunting out literary flowers and pursuing essentials, implements for wielding the writing tablet and wetting the brush. Were they not examples of what is called “buying the casket and returning the pearl”?

To order the world through classical learning: Anshi’s doctrine seemed sound. Why, then, did he say that celestial anomalies need not be feared, others’ criticism need not be heeded, and ancestral institutions need not be preserved? His painstaking study merely borrowed the already tested institutions of the Offices of Zhou to advance his contentious and obstinate views. Was this not what is called “taking up a spear and entering the chamber” to attack one’s own teacher?

For in the Three Dynasties and earlier, learning was rooted in the person and the mind. Thus, although people’s reading and recitation were limited, they could independently fathom the subtleties of the constant norms of human relations and the principles of Heaven. After the Three Dynasties, learning proceeded merely from mouth and ear. Thus, although their reading and recitation were…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
博而卒同歸于詞章利祿之習論者因謂
霍光承扆圖之重寄安漢之功炳耀史氏
矣顧春秋之斷失于不疑擁立之策決于
延年是無俟于學而可以樹勳也究而言
之光之不負天子由其稟沉靜詳審之資
而卒不得與伊尹同功者則不學之過也
不然何以有芒刺驂乘陰妻邪謀之禍耶
濂溪倡千載之絕學道統之傳光啓宋儒
矣顧太極之圖得之默契易通之旨不由
===
師傳是無俟于學而可以明道也究而言
之頤之能自得師由其博學力行之功而
卒能以接孔孟正脈者則善學之驗也不
然又安有中正仁義主靜立極之說耶用
是而知學之不可以已也學者苟能別心
迹辨內外遺時致主則以一身任斯世之
重爲唐虞之稷契皋夔爲商周之伊呂傅
說而子孟不足齒矣況于懷祿苟容者乎
抱朴含章則以一心會斯道之全爲春秋
punctuated:
博，而卒同歸于詞章利祿之習。論者因謂：「霍光承扆圖之重寄，安漢之功炳耀史氏矣。顧春秋之斷失于不疑，擁立之策決于延年，是無俟于學而可以樹勳也。」究而言之，光之不負天子，由其稟沉靜詳審之資；而卒不得與伊尹同功者，則不學之過也。不然，何以有芒刺驂乘、陰妻邪謀之禍耶？濂溪倡千載之絕學，道統之傳光啓宋儒矣。顧太極之圖得之默契，易通之旨不由師傳，是無俟于學而可以明道也。究而言之，頤之能自得師，由其博學力行之功；而卒能以接孔孟正脈者，則善學之驗也。不然，又安有中正仁義、主靜立極之說耶？用是而知學之不可以已也。
學者苟能別心迹，辨內外，遺時致主，則以一身任斯世之重，爲唐虞之稷契皋夔，爲商周之伊呂傅說，而子孟不足齒矣，況于懷祿苟容者乎？抱朴含章，則以一心會斯道之全，爲春秋
translation_en:
…extensive, yet ultimately all alike succumb to the pursuit of literary composition, profit, and official emoluments. Some commentators therefore say: “Huo Guang was entrusted with the weighty charge of serving as regent; his achievement in securing the Han shines brilliantly in the historical records. Yet in judgment based on the Spring and Autumn Annals he fell short of Buyi, and his decision about enthroning a ruler depended on Yannian. Thus one can establish great merit without learning.” On closer examination, however, Guang did not betray the Son of Heaven because he possessed a calm disposition and careful judgment. That he ultimately failed to equal Yi Yin’s achievement was the fault of his lack of learning. Otherwise, how could there have been the troubles of his riding beside the emperor and making him feel as though pricked by thorns, and of his wife’s clandestine, wicked plotting [?]?
Lianxi revived learning that had been lost for a thousand years, illuminating the transmission of the Way for the Confucians of the Song. Yet his Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate came from silent understanding, and the purport of his Penetrating the Changes was not transmitted by a teacher. Thus, it might seem, one can illuminate the Way without learning. On closer examination, however, Yi’s ability to find a teacher for himself [?] derived from his extensive learning and vigorous practice; that he ultimately continued the authentic lineage of Confucius and Mencius demonstrates his skill in learning. Otherwise, how could he have formulated the teachings of centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness, and of making stillness primary and establishing the Supreme Ultimate? From this we know that learning must never cease.
If scholars can distinguish inward intention from outward conduct, and discern the internal and external, then, when the times afford an opportunity to bring their ruler to perfection [?], they can personally shoulder the weight of the world. They can become the Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, and Kui of the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, or the Yi Yin, Lü Shang, and Fu Yue of the Shang and Zhou. Zimeng would then scarcely merit mention beside them—how much less those who cling to their emoluments and merely seek to remain in favor! If they embrace simplicity and keep their brilliance within, they can comprehend the entirety of this Way in their own minds and become, for the Spring and Autumn period…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
之孔子而茂叔亦其侶矣安有枉道求售
者乎此則愚生之見竊有志焉而未逮者
也抑又有說焉世之儒者至有筌蹄六經
桎梏萬事自謂直截捷逕妙契道體其于
心學將無同與蓋心無內外聖賢之學亦
無內外好古敏求外矣而未嘗不內也默
識無言內矣而未嘗不外也世俗之學不
失之內則失之外此訓詁聲華所以卑而
無用也不失之外則失之內此超達頓悟
所以虛而無實也二者雖閒以言乎害道
則均焉傳曰性之德也合內外之道也此
孔子之學而夫人所當潛心者也謹對
===
第三問
韓必光
考試官教諭劉　批〔姓氏詳知源委且以仁義〕
〔宗法爲敦化厚俗之道亦知本之論〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔考究精詳條答明悉博〕
〔雅之士〕
punctuated:
之孔子，而茂叔亦其侶矣，安有枉道求售者乎？此則愚生之見，竊有志焉而未逮者也。抑又有說焉：世之儒者，至有筌蹄六經、桎梏萬事，自謂直截捷逕、妙契道體，其于心學將無同與？蓋心無內外，聖賢之學亦無內外。好古敏求，外矣，而未嘗不內也；默識無言，內矣，而未嘗不外也。世俗之學，不失之內則失之外，此訓詁聲華所以卑而無用也；不失之外則失之內，此超達頓悟所以虛而無實也。二者雖閒，以言乎害道則均焉。傳曰：「性之德也，合內外之道也。」此孔子之學，而夫人所當潛心者也。謹對。

第三問
韓必光
考試官教諭劉，批〔姓氏詳知源委，且以仁義〕〔宗法爲敦化厚俗之道，亦知本之論。〕
考試官教諭胡，批〔考究精詳，條答明悉，博〕〔雅之士。〕
translation_en:
…a Confucius, with Maoshu likewise as his companion. How could such a person bend the Way to seek acceptance? Such is this humble student's view: I privately aspire to it but have yet to attain it.

There is, however, something further to say. Among the scholars of our age, some go so far as to treat the Six Classics as mere fish traps and rabbit snares, and the myriad affairs as fetters. They claim that their approach is direct, a shortcut, and that they wondrously accord with the substance of the Way. Might their approach be the same as the learning of the mind? The mind, however, has neither an inside nor an outside; neither does the learning of sages and worthies. Loving antiquity and diligently seeking knowledge appear outward, yet have never been without an inward dimension. Silently retaining knowledge without words appears inward, yet has never been without an outward dimension. Worldly learning, if it does not err toward the inward, errs toward the outward: this is why textual glossing and literary renown are shallow and useless. If it does not err toward the outward, it errs toward the inward: this is why transcendent understanding and sudden enlightenment are empty and without substance. Although the two differ [?], they are equal in the harm they do to the Way. The commentary says: “It is the virtue of one's nature, the Way that unites the inward and the outward.” This is the learning of Confucius, to which everyone should devote the mind. Respectfully submitted.

Third Question
Han Biguang

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “He has a detailed knowledge of the origins and development of surnames and clan names. Moreover, he takes benevolence, righteousness, and the lineage system as means of deepening moral transformation and enriching customs. This, too, is an argument that understands the fundamentals.”

Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “His investigations are precise and thorough, and his answers to the individual points are clear and comprehensive. A scholar of broad learning and refinement.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
聖王所以繫天下之民者其姓氏之法乎
夫姓以著其生也所以統天下之同氏以
明其世也所以辨天下之異統同則勢不
渙而天親之懿以惇辨異則分不淆而天
秩之常以叙其所裨于世教而繫乎人心
者不亦大哉執事策諸生以此豈不以聖
王敦睦之所先而示天下知所嚮風與愚
也敢誦所聞爲執事質焉且姓氏之說何
始乎書稱禹曰錫土姓左氏曰天子建德
===
因生賜姓胙之土而命之氏姓氏之說其
由來遠也羲皇而上邈矣史稱黃帝顓帝
帝嚳帝堯帝舜姓皆爲姬姓所同也黃帝
爲有熊顓帝爲高陽帝嚳爲高辛帝堯爲
陶唐帝舜爲有虞各自爲氏氏所異也所
同者原其本所異者別其生姓氏之義章
矣周官太宰以九兩繫邦國之民有曰宗
以族得民小宰掌系世宗伯掌三族法彬
彬乎具矣秦併六國世以淪夷子孫忘其
punctuated:
聖王所以繫天下之民者，其姓氏之法乎？夫姓以著其生也，所以統天下之同；氏以明其世也，所以辨天下之異。統同則勢不渙，而天親之懿以惇；辨異則分不淆，而天秩之常以叙。其所裨于世教而繫乎人心者，不亦大哉！執事策諸生以此，豈不以聖王敦睦之所先，而示天下知所嚮風與？愚也敢誦所聞，爲執事質焉。
且姓氏之說何始乎？書稱禹曰：「錫土姓。」左氏曰：「天子建德，因生賜姓，胙之土而命之氏。」姓氏之說，其由來遠也。羲皇而上，邈矣。史稱黃帝、顓帝、帝嚳、帝堯、帝舜，姓皆爲姬，姓所同也。黃帝爲有熊，顓帝爲高陽，帝嚳爲高辛，帝堯爲陶唐，帝舜爲有虞，各自爲氏，氏所異也。所同者原其本，所異者別其生，姓氏之義章矣。周官太宰以九兩繫邦國之民，有曰：「宗以族得民。」小宰掌系世，宗伯掌三族，法彬彬乎具矣。秦併六國，世以淪夷，子孫忘其
translation_en:
Was it not through the system of ancestral surnames (xing) and lineage names (shi) that the sage kings bound together the people of the realm? An ancestral surname makes a person’s origins manifest, thereby uniting those throughout the realm who share a common ancestry; a lineage name clarifies a person’s descent, thereby distinguishing the different branches throughout the realm. Uniting those of common ancestry prevents their strength from dispersing and deepens the excellence of natural kinship. Distinguishing different branches prevents confusion in their respective stations and preserves the proper order of Heaven’s enduring hierarchy. Is this not a great contribution to moral instruction in society and to binding people’s hearts together? In setting this policy question for us students, do you not take up what the sage kings made their first concern in fostering kinship and harmony, showing the realm an example to follow? In my ignorance, I venture to recite what I have heard and submit it for your judgment.
Where, then, did the account of ancestral surnames and lineage names begin? The Book of Documents says of Yu: “He bestowed lands and surnames.” The Zuo Commentary says: “The Son of Heaven establishes the virtuous in office, grants them ancestral surnames according to their birth, endows them with land, and assigns them lineage names.” The system of ancestral surnames and lineage names thus has a distant origin. The age of Fuxi and earlier is remote indeed. The histories state that Huangdi, Emperor Zhuan, Emperor Ku, Emperor Yao, and Emperor Shun all bore the ancestral surname Ji [?]: this was what they shared in ancestral surname. Huangdi was Youxiong, Emperor Zhuan was Gaoyang, Emperor Ku was Gaoxin, Emperor Yao was Taotang, and Emperor Shun was Youyu. Each had his own lineage name: this was how their lineage names differed. What they shared traced their common root; what distinguished them marked their separate origins. Thus the meaning of ancestral surnames and lineage names is clear. According to the Offices of Zhou, the Grand Steward bound together the people of the states through nine bonds, one of which was: “The lineage head secures the people through kinship.” The Vice Steward oversaw genealogical succession, and the Minister of Rites oversaw the three kinship groups. How fully and elegantly the institutions were established! When Qin annexed the six states, the social order consequently declined, and descendants forgot their …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
本始失其支系非惟姓不可傳而氏亦莫
能知矣漢興司馬遷採世本世系以作帝
紀撫周譜國語以作世家所明者帝王之
世賢哲之裔其他蓋闕如也晉宋以後譜
牒紛然以出君子亦藉以考其世焉若王
僧儒則有百家譜徐勉之則有百官牒後
魏河南則有官氏志諸儒則有氏族志柳
冲則有姓系錄路淳則有衣冠譜韋述則
有開元譜柳芳則有永泰譜非不粲然具
===
也但言人人殊私見歧出或主偏旁或主
聲音或主貴賤或主升沉不能合古聖人
之法焉自今考之先代之姓一而已而子
孫之氏不能以不繁以所封之國而氏則
虞夏商周魯衛齊宋之類也以先代之謚
而氏則楚莊魯僖康叔宣伯之後之類也
以爵而氏則皇王公侯公乘公士之類也
居傳巖徙稽山祀東家守橋山非以居而
氏乎少康以實田千秋以車微子之白馬
punctuated:
本始，失其支系，非惟姓不可傳，而氏亦莫能知矣。漢興，司馬遷採《世本》世系以作帝紀，撫《周譜》《國語》以作世家，所明者帝王之世、賢哲之裔，其他蓋闕如也。晉宋以後，譜牒紛然以出，君子亦藉以考其世焉。若王僧儒則有《百家譜》，徐勉之則有《百官牒》，後魏河南則有《官氏志》，諸儒則有《氏族志》，柳冲則有《姓系錄》，路淳則有《衣冠譜》，韋述則有《開元譜》，柳芳則有《永泰譜》，非不粲然具也。但言人人殊，私見歧出，或主偏旁，或主聲音，或主貴賤，或主升沉，不能合古聖人之法焉。

自今考之，先代之姓一而已，而子孫之氏不能以不繁。以所封之國而氏，則虞、夏、商、周、魯、衛、齊、宋之類也；以先代之謚而氏，則楚莊、魯僖、康叔、宣伯之後之類也；以爵而氏，則皇、王、公、侯、公乘、公士之類也。居傳巖，徙稽山，祀東家，守橋山，非以居而氏乎？少康以實，田千秋以車，微子之白馬
translation_en:
…their origins and lost track of their lineage branches; not only could their ancestral surnames (xing) no longer be transmitted, but even their branch surnames (shi) became unknowable. When the Han arose, Sima Qian drew on the genealogies in the Origins of Lineages (Shiben) to compose his Basic Annals, and consulted the Genealogies of Zhou and the Discourses of the States to compose his Hereditary Houses. What he clarified were the lineages of emperors and kings and the descendants of worthy and wise men; the rest he generally left unrecorded. After the Jin and Song, genealogical records appeared in profusion, and gentlemen also relied on them to investigate their ancestry. Thus Wang Sengru had his Genealogies of the Hundred Families; Xu Mianzhi [?], his Register of the Hundred Officials; Henan under the Later Wei [?], its Treatise on Official Clans; various scholars, their Treatise on Clans; Liu Chong, his Record of Surname Lineages; Lu Chun, his Genealogies of Official Families; Wei Shu, his Kaiyuan Genealogies; and Liu Fang, his Yongtai Genealogies. These were indeed splendidly comprehensive. Yet their accounts differed from person to person, and private opinions diverged: some took the graphic components of characters as their basis, others pronunciation, others high or low status, and still others advancement or decline. They could not accord with the methods of the ancient sages.

Examining the matter today, we find that an ancestral surname in earlier generations was just one, while the branch surnames of descendants could not help multiplying. Surnames taken from the states granted as fiefs include Yu, Xia, Shang, Zhou, Lu, Wei, Qi, and Song. Surnames taken from ancestors’ posthumous titles include those of the descendants of King Zhuang of Chu, Duke Xi of Lu, Kang Shu, and Xuan Bo. Surnames taken from ranks include Huang, Wang, Gong, Hou, Gongcheng, and Gongshi. Dwelling at Chuanyan [?], moving to Jishan, maintaining sacrifices at Dongjia, and guarding Qiaoshan—were these not cases of taking surnames from places of residence? Shao Kang’s surname derived from “shi” [?], Tian Qianqiu’s from “che” (carriage), and Weizi’s “Baima” (white horse) …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
魏初之青牛非以事而氏乎夫本之尚書
左氏其名著矣質之史記其實徵矣叅之
譜牒其說備矣雖其言有詳畧之殊其發
明姓氏之原一也何足多議哉葢嘗因是
而求之姓之爲言生也賜之姓以立其宗
所以明其生而使之不渙氏之爲言屬也
命之氏以合其姓所以別其屬而使之不
淆姓統其祖考之所自出百世而不變者
也氏別其子孫之所自分數世而一變者
===
也故古者自仁率親等而上之至於祖名
曰輕而分自明姓氏之源不可得而忘也
自義率祖順而下之至于禰名曰重而恩
愈篤姓氏之傳不可得而易也親親故尊
祖尊祖故敬宗戚單而係之以姓世遠而
綴之以食昭穆序而禮義別教化洽而風
俗同士庶人則世其家卿大夫則世其族
諸侯則世其國聯屬天下之勢以成雍熙
泰和之治行葦常棣之風至今猶可想見
punctuated:
魏初之青牛，非以事而氏乎？夫本之《尚書》《左氏》，其名著矣；質之《史記》，其實徵矣；叅之譜牒，其說備矣。雖其言有詳畧之殊，其發明姓氏之原一也，何足多議哉？
葢嘗因是而求之：姓之爲言，生也。賜之姓以立其宗，所以明其生而使之不渙。氏之爲言，屬也。命之氏以合其姓，所以別其屬而使之不淆。姓統其祖考之所自出，百世而不變者也；氏別其子孫之所自分，數世而一變者也。
故古者，自仁率親，等而上之至於祖，名曰輕，而分自明，姓氏之源不可得而忘也；自義率祖，順而下之至于禰，名曰重，而恩愈篤，姓氏之傳不可得而易也。親親故尊祖，尊祖故敬宗。戚單而係之以姓，世遠而綴之以食。昭穆序而禮義別，教化洽而風俗同。士庶人則世其家，卿大夫則世其族，諸侯則世其國。聯屬天下之勢，以成雍熙泰和之治，《行葦》《常棣》之風，至今猶可想見。
translation_en:
…and the “Blue Ox” of early Wei: were these not cases of taking a lineage name from an event? If we trace these names through the Book of Documents and the Zuo Commentary, they are clearly recorded; if we test them against the Records of the Grand Historian, the facts are corroborated; if we consult genealogical registers, the explanations are complete. Although these accounts differ in their degree of detail, they agree in elucidating the origins of surnames and lineage names. What need is there for further dispute?
I have therefore sought to investigate this matter. The word for surname, xing, signifies birth, sheng. Bestowing a surname establishes a descent group: it makes its origins clear and prevents it from dispersing. The word for lineage name, shi, signifies affiliation. Assigning a lineage name brings its members together under their surname: it distinguishes their affiliations and prevents confusion. A surname encompasses the common origin of one's forebears and remains unchanged for a hundred generations; a lineage name distinguishes the branches into which their descendants divide and changes once every few generations.
Thus, in antiquity, benevolence guided attachment to one's kin. Proceeding upward by degrees to the ancestors, the designation became “lighter” [?], while distinctions became clear of themselves; the origins of surnames and lineage names could not be forgotten. Righteousness guided reverence for ancestors. Proceeding downward in order to one's deceased father, the designation became “heavier” [?], while affection grew ever deeper; the transmission of surnames and lineage names could not be altered. Affection for kin therefore led to honoring ancestors, and honoring ancestors led to reverence for the lineage. When kinship ties grew thin, people were bound together by their surname; when generations grew distant, they were joined by “food” [?]. The alternating ancestral ranks of zhao and mu were properly ordered, and distinctions of ritual and righteousness were maintained. Moral instruction spread everywhere, and customs became uniform. Men of service and commoners perpetuated their households; ministers and grand masters perpetuated their lineages; the regional lords perpetuated their states. The constituent parts of the realm were thus bound together to achieve a flourishing reign of concord and profound peace. The spirit of the Odes “The Reeds” (Xing Wei) and “The Cherry Tree” (Chang Di) can still be imagined today.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
猗與休哉鄭樵曰繩繩秩秩各歸其宗使
千餘年湮源斷緒之典燦然在目如雲歸
於山川歸於淵日月星辰麗於天百穀草
木麗於地則姓氏之當明足徵矣然愚猶
有說焉易婁爲劉漢祖賜之易徐爲李唐
祖賜之命出於尊不敢違也跡廣之後去
足而爲東鴻漸之生筮卦而爲陸安所取
義哉夫以皆羽之賢而有是况其他乎歐
陽子九十三族之表詳矣君子不稱焉丁
===
維皐百二十家之説雖備識者議之亦以
姓氏之原無所據耳甚哉姓氏之難言也
古之氏族繁而知之者易今之氏族簡而
知之者難傳之愈遠衍之愈蕃曰姓曰氏
人莫知其所自出况尚婚姻者先外族尚
冠冕者慕榮華尚貴戚者狥勢利或一戶
而六七其姓或一人而二三其氏豈知姓
之爲氏乎氏之爲姓乎人無反本之思士
鮮睦族之義安望其親親以尊其上而臻
punctuated:
猗與休哉！鄭樵曰：「繩繩秩秩，各歸其宗，使千餘年湮源斷緒之典燦然在目，如雲歸於山，川歸於淵，日月星辰麗於天，百穀草木麗於地。」則姓氏之當明足徵矣。然愚猶有說焉：易婁爲劉，漢祖賜之；易徐爲李，唐祖賜之。命出於尊，不敢違也。跡廣之後，去足而爲東；鴻漸之生，筮卦而爲陸，安所取義哉？夫以皆羽之賢而有是，况其他乎？歐陽子九十三族之表詳矣，君子不稱焉；丁維皐百二十家之説雖備，識者議之，亦以姓氏之原無所據耳。甚哉，姓氏之難言也！

古之氏族繁而知之者易，今之氏族簡而知之者難。傳之愈遠，衍之愈蕃，曰姓曰氏，人莫知其所自出。况尚婚姻者先外族，尚冠冕者慕榮華，尚貴戚者狥勢利，或一戶而六七其姓，或一人而二三其氏，豈知姓之爲氏乎？氏之爲姓乎？人無反本之思，士鮮睦族之義，安望其親親以尊其上而臻
translation_en:
Ah, how splendid! Zheng Qiao said: “In unbroken succession and orderly arrangement, each returns to its ancestral line, bringing records whose sources had been obscured and whose threads had been severed for more than a thousand years vividly before our eyes: like clouds returning to the mountains, rivers returning to the depths, the sun, moon, and stars adhering to heaven, and grains, grasses, and trees adhering to earth.” This sufficiently demonstrates why ancestral surnames (xing) and lineage names (shi) must be clarified. Yet I, in my ignorance, have something further to say. Lou was changed to Liu by a grant from the founding emperor of the Han; Xu was changed to Li by a grant from the founding emperor of the Tang. These commands came from a superior, and none dared disobey. But the descendants of Ji Guang [?] removed the “foot” component from their surname to make Dong [?]; and Hongjian acquired the surname Lu through divination with a hexagram. What justification was there for these choices? If even men as worthy as Jie [?] and Yu did such things, how much more would others! Master Ouyang’s table of ninety-three clans is detailed, yet gentlemen do not commend it. Ding Weigao’s account of one hundred and twenty families is comprehensive, yet knowledgeable men criticize it, likewise because its explanations of the origins of surnames lack supporting evidence. How very difficult it is to speak of surnames!

In antiquity, lineage groups were numerous, yet knowing them was easy; today, lineage groups are fewer, yet knowing them is difficult. The longer their transmission and the more numerous their branches, the less people know whence their ancestral surnames and lineage names originated. Moreover, those who prize marriage alliances give precedence to their relatives by marriage; those who prize official rank covet glory and splendor; those who prize ties to noble relatives pursue power and profit. Sometimes a single household has six or seven surnames, or a single person has two or three lineage names. How could they understand how an ancestral surname becomes a lineage name, or how a lineage name becomes an ancestral surname? People have no thought of returning to their roots, and few scholars possess a sense of duty to maintain harmony within their clans. How can one hope that they will cherish their kin, thereby honor their superiors, and attain…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
淳化之理也夫姓氏之傳莫考矣而宗子
之法不猶可行乎禮曰別子爲祖繼別爲
宗繼禰爲小宗有百世不遷之宗有五世
則遷之宗百世不遷之宗宗其繼
別子者也有五世則遷之宗宗其繼高祖
者也知此義焉不必遐思而擬之如輔氏
之於智伯也不必倚勢而附之如郭崇韜
之於子儀也擇其親近而有傳者宗焉統
之以大宗使知尊祖而不忘其本統之以
小宗使知敬禰而不弛其親可以收族可
以嚴祀社稷重庶民安協氣嘉生薰爲太
和不有以臻成周至治之極乎然程子曰
宗子無法則朝廷無世臣立宗子則朝廷
之勢自尊張子亦曰宗法立則朝廷大有
所益蓋能重其本則世守其家而忠愛之
心益篤能親其族則世濟其美而翊戴之
義益隆移孝爲忠蓋相資以有成也宗社
篤無疆之祜則世臣亦永有聞哉
第四問
punctuated:
淳化之理也？夫姓氏之傳莫考矣，而宗子之法不猶可行乎？禮曰：「別子爲祖，繼別爲宗，繼禰爲小宗。有百世不遷之宗，有五世則遷之宗。百世不遷之宗，宗其繼別子者也；有五世則遷之宗，宗其繼高祖者也。」知此義焉，不必遐思而擬之，如輔氏之於智伯也；不必倚勢而附之，如郭崇韜之於子儀也。擇其親近而有傳者宗焉，統之以大宗，使知尊祖而不忘其本；統之以小宗，使知敬禰而不弛其親。可以收族，可以嚴祀，社稷重，庶民安，協氣嘉生，薰爲太和，不有以臻成周至治之極乎？然程子曰：「宗子無法，則朝廷無世臣；立宗子，則朝廷之勢自尊。」張子亦曰：「宗法立，則朝廷大有所益。」蓋能重其本，則世守其家，而忠愛之心益篤；能親其族，則世濟其美，而翊戴之義益隆。移孝爲忠，蓋相資以有成也。宗社篤無疆之祜，則世臣亦永有聞哉！

第四問
translation_en:
…the orderly rule brought about by a thorough moral transformation?

The transmission of surnames and clan names can no longer be verified; yet could the institution of lineage heirs not still be put into practice? The Book of Rites says: “A son who establishes a separate branch becomes its founding ancestor; his successor becomes the head of its major lineage, while a successor to a deceased father becomes the head of a minor lineage. There are lineages whose headship does not shift for a hundred generations, and lineages whose headship shifts after five generations. In a lineage whose headship does not shift for a hundred generations, the successor to the branch-founding son is honored as its head. In a lineage whose headship shifts after five generations, the successor to the great-great-grandfather is honored as its head.”

Once this principle is understood, there is no need to imagine remote connections and claim kinship, as the Fu clan did with Zhi Bo; nor need one attach oneself to another by relying on power, as Guo Chongtao did with Guo Ziyi. Choose as lineage head someone closely related whose descent is documented. Unite the members under a major lineage, so that they learn to honor their ancestors and never forget their roots; unite them under minor lineages, so that they learn to revere their deceased fathers and never allow their bonds of kinship to slacken. Thus the clan can be gathered together and its sacrifices conducted with solemnity. The altars of soil and grain will command respect, the common people will be secure, and harmonious vital forces and flourishing living things will combine to produce supreme harmony. Would this not provide a means of attaining the perfection of good government achieved by the Zhou?

Master Cheng said: “Without an established system of lineage heirs, the court will have no hereditary ministers. Establish lineage heirs, and the court’s authority will naturally command respect.” Master Zhang also said: “Once the lineage system is established, the court will benefit greatly.” For if people can honor their roots, they will preserve their families from generation to generation, and their feelings of loyalty and love will grow ever stronger. If they can cherish their clans, they will carry forward their virtues from generation to generation, and their commitment to supporting the sovereign will grow ever greater. Filial devotion is transferred into loyalty: the two sustain one another and thereby attain fulfillment. When the dynastic ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain enjoy abundant, boundless blessings, hereditary ministers too will surely enjoy lasting renown!

Fourth Policy Question

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
英道傳
同考試官教諭陳　批〔論兵不廢乎法亦不泥乎法惟其隨機應變運用在心可謂得兵家之要矣〕
同考試官學正皇甫　批〔評品允確議論明盡蓋嘗究心於兵法者〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔用兵通變之法獨得古將勝算遺意非書生之空談也〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔似素閑兵略者錄之〕
善用兵者尚其法善用法者尚其神蓋將
之於兵也以一人而馭三軍之衆苟非法
以率之則渙而無紀其兵不足支也兵之
有法也以坐籌而決千里之勝苟非神以
運之則固而不通其法不足恃也故知法
===
而後可以用兵書曰不愆於六步七步不
愆于四伐五伐六伐七伐其法之謂乎如
是則以戰以守有餘能焉而制勝之具在
我矣知神而後可以用法志曰微乎微乎
至于無形神乎神乎至于無聲其神之謂
punctuated:
英道傳

同考試官教諭陳　批〔論兵不廢乎法，亦不泥乎法，惟其隨機應變，運用在心，可謂得兵家之要矣。〕
同考試官學正皇甫　批〔評品允確，議論明盡，蓋嘗究心於兵法者。〕
考試官教諭劉　批〔用兵通變之法，獨得古將勝算遺意，非書生之空談也。〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔似素閑兵略者，錄之。〕

善用兵者尚其法，善用法者尚其神。蓋將之於兵也，以一人而馭三軍之衆，苟非法以率之，則渙而無紀，其兵不足支也。兵之有法也，以坐籌而決千里之勝，苟非神以運之，則固而不通，其法不足恃也。故知法而後可以用兵。《書》曰：「不愆於六步七步，不愆于四伐五伐六伐七伐。」其法之謂乎？如是，則以戰以守有餘能焉，而制勝之具在我矣。知神而後可以用法。志曰：「微乎微乎，至于無形；神乎神乎，至于無聲。」其神之謂
translation_en:
Ying Daochuan

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “In discussing warfare, he neither dispenses with rules nor clings rigidly to them. Rather, he adapts to changing circumstances, applying them through his own judgment. He may be said to have grasped the essentials of the military strategists.”
Associate Examiner Huangfu, School Instructor, comments: “His assessments are sound and accurate, and his arguments clear and exhaustive. He must have devoted serious thought to the methods of warfare.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “On adapting methods to changing circumstances in warfare, he has singularly grasped the surviving import of ancient generals’ calculations for victory. This is no scholar’s empty talk.”
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “He seems long familiar with military strategy. Accept this essay.”

Those skilled in employing troops prize method; those skilled in applying method prize inspired mastery. A general, after all, is one man commanding the multitude of the Three Armies. Unless he leads them by method, they will scatter without discipline, and his forces will be unable to hold out. Methods in warfare enable one, through deliberation at headquarters, to determine victory a thousand li away. Unless inspired mastery directs their application, however, they become rigid and inflexible, and cannot be relied upon. Thus only after understanding method can one employ troops. The Book of Documents says: “Do not exceed six or seven paces; do not exceed four, five, six, or seven strikes.” Does this not refer to method? With this, one has ample capacity both to attack and to defend, and the means of securing victory lie within one’s own control. Only after understanding inspired mastery can one apply method. The record says: “Subtle, so subtle, reaching the point of formlessness; wondrous, so wondrous, reaching the point of soundlessness.” This speaks of inspired mastery …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
手如是則以正以奇有餘巧焉而必勝之
機在我矣使兵可無法是人足戰也何以
云銳卒之不如節制也使法不必神是人
足將也何以云可意授而不可語傳也法
者人之所及見神者人之所不及知是二
者恒相須以有成也愚生非知兵者也執
事乃詢古人已試之法而振之以請纓之
風誠不容默焉已請以所嘗究心者而就
正焉可乎夫天生五材不能去兵久矣誅
===
伐之不可廢于天下也然兵者凶器戰者
危事不得已而後用之故必先之以法自
軒轅氏教熊羆貔貅貙虎之士七十戰而
兵不殆而法所由起王制則有五戎之習
周禮則有四時之教而孔子曰以不教民
戰是謂棄之故必兵識將意將識士情而
後可與戰也而亦有不盡然者孫武之於
吳也試以婦人而遽云可赴水火遂取信
闔閭而卒西破强楚北威齊晉稱一世之
punctuated:
手？如是，則以正以奇有餘巧焉，而必勝之機在我矣。使兵可無法，是人足戰也，何以云銳卒之不如節制也？使法不必神，是人足將也，何以云可意授而不可語傳也？法者，人之所及見；神者，人之所不及知。是二者恒相須以有成也。愚生非知兵者也，執事乃詢古人已試之法，而振之以請纓之風，誠不容默焉已。請以所嘗究心者而就正焉，可乎？
夫天生五材，不能去兵，久矣誅伐之不可廢于天下也。然兵者凶器，戰者危事，不得已而後用之，故必先之以法。自軒轅氏教熊羆貔貅貙虎之士，七十戰而兵不殆，而法所由起。王制則有五戎之習，周禮則有四時之教，而孔子曰：「以不教民戰，是謂棄之。」故必兵識將意，將識士情，而後可與戰也。而亦有不盡然者。孫武之於吳也，試以婦人，而遽云可赴水火，遂取信闔閭，而卒西破强楚，北威齊晉，稱一世之
translation_en:
…[The opening character 手 is unclear; apparently the end of a question.]
Thus, in employing both orthodox and unorthodox methods, one has skill to spare, and the means of certain victory lie in one’s own hands. If troops could dispense with method, anyone would be capable of fighting; why, then, is it said that crack troops are inferior to disciplined forces? If method did not require inspired mastery, anyone would be capable of commanding; why, then, is it said that this can be imparted through understanding but cannot be transmitted in words? Method is what people can perceive; inspired mastery is what lies beyond their comprehension. These two always depend upon one another for success. I, an ignorant student, am no expert in military affairs. Yet you, honored examiners, inquire into the proven methods of the ancients and stir us with the spirit of volunteering for military service. Truly, I cannot remain silent. May I present what I have previously studied closely and submit it for your correction?
Heaven produced the five materials, and weapons cannot be dispensed with: punitive warfare has long been something that cannot be abolished from the world. Yet weapons are instruments of ill omen, and warfare is a perilous undertaking; they should be employed only when unavoidable. Therefore, instruction in method must come first. Xuanyuan trained warriors likened to bears, brown bears, pi, xiu, chu, and tigers [?]; through seventy battles his forces suffered no peril. Here military method originated. The Royal Regulations prescribes practice with the five kinds of weapons, and the Rites of Zhou prescribes training in all four seasons. Confucius said: “To lead untrained people into battle is to abandon them.” Thus, soldiers must understand their commander’s intentions, and the commander must understand his men’s circumstances; only then can they be taken into battle.
Yet there are also cases in which this was not entirely so. When Sun Wu served Wu, he conducted a trial with women and immediately declared that they could be sent through water and fire. He thereby won the confidence of Helü and ultimately defeated mighty Chu in the west and overawed Qi and Jin in the north, gaining renown as his age’s …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
雄韓信之於漢也戰以市人而遽云破趙
會食遂收功泜水而竟北定燕地東下齊
城建佐命之烈彼其申令惟謹隊長必狥
武之法所可見者此耳至其令行於小試
而事集於俄頃前此且未之聞焉而况於
敎乎馳壁拔幟置亡後存信之法所可見
者此耳至其傳發於夜半而決勝於崇朝
諸將且未與聞焉而况於敎乎蓋必有神
以運於法之外不可得而知也至若孫臏
===
减竈以勝魏矣而峭谷之行虞詡則增竈
而羌衆遂不敢逼王翦用衆以破楚矣而
赤壁之戰周瑜則用寡而曹操竟走華容
李廣之治軍以簡也故士樂為之用而屡
立奇功然程不識則煩而亦以破虜與之
並稱于漢郭子儀之治軍以寬也故人樂
盡其力而奄復兩京然李光弼則嚴而亦
以顯名與之媲美于唐彼其所為可考而
知焉馬陵之伏利在誘敵臏蓋强而示之
punctuated: 雄。韓信之於漢也，戰以市人，而遽云「破趙會食」，遂收功泜水，而竟北定燕地，東下齊城，建佐命之烈。彼其申令惟謹，隊長必狥，武之法所可見者此耳。至其令行於小試，而事集於俄頃，前此且未之聞焉，而况於敎乎？馳壁拔幟，置亡後存，信之法所可見者此耳。至其傳發於夜半，而決勝於崇朝，諸將且未與聞焉，而况於敎乎？蓋必有神以運於法之外，不可得而知也。至若孫臏减竈以勝魏矣，而峭谷之行，虞詡則增竈，而羌衆遂不敢逼；王翦用衆以破楚矣，而赤壁之戰，周瑜則用寡，而曹操竟走華容。李廣之治軍以簡也，故士樂為之用，而屡立奇功；然程不識則煩，而亦以破虜與之並稱于漢。郭子儀之治軍以寬也，故人樂盡其力，而奄復兩京；然李光弼則嚴，而亦以顯名與之媲美于唐。彼其所為，可考而知焉。馬陵之伏，利在誘敵，臏蓋强而示之
translation_en:
…a hero of his age. When Han Xin served the Han, he took townsmen into battle and abruptly declared, “We shall defeat Zhao and then gather for a meal.” He duly won victory at the Zhi River, ultimately pacified the lands of Yan to the north, took the cities of Qi to the east, and achieved glorious deeds in helping establish the dynasty. As for carefully reiterating commands and having the company leaders executed as a warning [?], these are the only visible aspects of Sun Wu’s methods. Yet his orders were obeyed in a small trial, and the undertaking was accomplished in an instant: beforehand, those involved had not even heard of such things, much less been trained in them! Galloping into the enemy’s camp and uprooting its banners, placing men in a position of destruction before securing their survival—these are the only visible aspects of Han Xin’s methods. Yet he issued his orders at midnight and secured victory within a morning: even his generals had not been informed beforehand, much less been trained in them! Surely there was an inspired mastery operating beyond established methods, something that cannot be fathomed.

Consider Sun Bin, who reduced his cooking fires to defeat Wei. Yet during the march through the steep valleys, Yu Xu increased his cooking fires, and the Qiang forces consequently dared not press him. Wang Jian used a large force to defeat Chu. Yet at the battle of Chibi, Zhou Yu used a small force, and Cao Cao ultimately fled by way of Huarong. Li Guang administered his army with simplicity, so his soldiers gladly served him, and he repeatedly achieved extraordinary victories. Cheng Bushi, however, employed elaborate procedures, yet his victories over the enemy won him renown alongside Li Guang under the Han. Guo Ziyi administered his army with leniency, so his men gladly exerted their utmost strength, and he swiftly recovered the two capitals. Li Guangbi, however, was strict, yet his distinguished reputation likewise rivaled Guo’s under the Tang. What these men did can be examined and understood. In the ambush at Maling, the advantage lay in luring the enemy: Sun Bin was strong, but presented himself to them as…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
弱也謝則虜衆我少所貴先聲非示强其
何以爲自全之計屢勝之兵慮在輕敵翦
蓋先爲不可勝也瑜則乘勞因釁以十擊
百惟出奇斯有以邀必勝之功無恃其不
來恃吾有以待之不識之煩者法也而法
令省而不煩李廣之簡非法乎審法制明
賞罰使民有必戰之心光弼之嚴者法也
而視卒如嬰兒子儀之寛非法乎是其所
異者法也其所同者神也吾安得而執之
===
以法也先據北山趙奢之勝秦何智也馬
謖踵其故轍而喪師不知武安勸兵屋瓦
皆振而奢之遣間夜馳出其不意要在疾
如風以奪其魄故得地形則勝謖乃舉措
煩擾而於計左矣安能免街亭之敗耶一
卒爲神田單之復齊何奇也王則襲其餘
謀而就擒不知卽墨城守危在旦夕而單
之設謀怒士約降懈敵特事假神威以疑
其心故縱火牛而克則乃以逆犯順而其
punctuated:
弱也。謝則虜衆我少，所貴先聲，非示强，其何以爲自全之計？屢勝之兵，慮在輕敵，翦蓋先爲不可勝也。瑜則乘勞因釁，以十擊百，惟出奇，斯有以邀必勝之功。「無恃其不來，恃吾有以待之」，不識之煩者，法也。而「法令省而不煩」，李廣之簡，非法乎？「審法制，明賞罰，使民有必戰之心」，光弼之嚴者，法也。而「視卒如嬰兒」，子儀之寛，非法乎？是其所異者，法也；其所同者，神也。吾安得而執之以法也？

先據北山，趙奢之勝秦，何智也！馬謖踵其故轍而喪師。不知武安勸兵，屋瓦皆振，而奢之遣間夜馳，出其不意，要在疾如風以奪其魄，故得地形則勝。謖乃舉措煩擾，而於計左矣，安能免街亭之敗耶？一卒爲神，田單之復齊，何奇也！王則襲其餘謀而就擒。不知卽墨城守，危在旦夕，而單之設謀怒士，約降懈敵，特事假神威以疑其心，故縱火牛而克。則乃以逆犯順，而其
translation_en:
…weakness. Xie, however, faced an enemy host with few troops of his own; what mattered was to establish his prestige first. Without displaying strength, how could he devise a plan to preserve his forces? With troops repeatedly victorious, the danger lies in underestimating the enemy; Wang Jian therefore first made himself invincible. Zhou Yu, by contrast, exploited the enemy’s exhaustion and vulnerabilities, striking a hundred with ten. Only through surprise could he secure certain victory. “Do not rely on their not coming; rely on our having the means to meet them.” Cheng Bushi’s elaborate precautions were a method. Yet “laws and orders should be few and uncomplicated”: was Li Guang’s simplicity not also a method? “Scrutinize regulations, make rewards and punishments clear, and give the people a determination to fight”: Li Guangbi’s strictness was a method. Yet “regard your soldiers as infants”: was Guo Ziyi’s leniency not also a method? What differed among them were their methods; what they shared was inspired mastery. How could I confine them to fixed methods?

By occupying the northern mountain first, Zhao She defeated Qin: how wise he was! Ma Su followed in his footsteps and lost his army. He failed to understand that at Wu’an the troops were urged on until even the roof tiles shook [?], while Zhao She dispatched spies and hurried onward by night, catching the enemy unprepared. The essential point was to move swiftly as the wind and rob the enemy of their nerve; thus, by securing advantageous terrain, he won. Ma Su’s actions, however, were confused and disruptive, and his planning went astray. How could he have escaped defeat at Jieting?

By making a single soldier into a spirit, Tian Dan recovered Qi: what an extraordinary stratagem! Wang Ze appropriated his remaining devices and was captured. He failed to understand that the defense of Jimo was in imminent peril, and that Tian Dan devised schemes to rouse his soldiers’ anger and offered surrender to make the enemy relax their vigilance. He merely borrowed divine awe to unsettle their minds; thus he released the fire-bearing oxen and won. Wang Ze, however, opposed legitimate authority through rebellion, and his…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
術窮矣安能負貝州之固耶父書可讀也
而膠柱鼓瑟不知合變如趙括者顧可使
乎長平之敗邯鄲幾亡何其殞身而無悔
也弟子輿尸之凶其括之謂矣古法可遵
也而引用浮華大言無當如房琯者顧可
任乎陳濤斜之奔牛車爲燼宜其折北而
不支也䒢車三百之法琯葢未之知矣若
是者豈法之罪哉不善用法者之罪也甚
哉兵之可以法用而不可泥之以法也故
===
曰聲不過五五聲之變不可勝聽也色不
過五五色之變不可勝觀也兵不過奇正
奇正之變不可勝窮也奇正還相生如環
之無端而其稱曰用兵如神是故當正而
正則王翦程不識李光弼之謹守而人不
得以爲拘當奇而奇則李廣周瑜郭子儀
之通變而人不得以爲誕以正爲奇以奇
爲正則孫武趙奢孫臏田單韓信虞詡之
參伍錯綜隨時變化而人莫知其所自出
punctuated: 術窮矣，安能負貝州之固耶？父書可讀也，而膠柱鼓瑟，不知合變，如趙括者，顧可使乎？長平之敗，邯鄲幾亡，何其殞身而無悔也！弟子輿尸之凶，其括之謂矣。古法可遵也，而引用浮華，大言無當，如房琯者，顧可任乎？陳濤斜之奔，牛車爲燼，宜其折北而不支也。䒢車三百之法，琯葢未之知矣。若是者，豈法之罪哉？不善用法者之罪也。甚哉，兵之可以法用，而不可泥之以法也！故曰：「聲不過五，五聲之變，不可勝聽也；色不過五，五色之變，不可勝觀也；兵不過奇正，奇正之變，不可勝窮也。奇正還相生，如環之無端。」而其稱曰：「用兵如神。」是故當正而正，則王翦、程不識、李光弼之謹守，而人不得以爲拘；當奇而奇，則李廣、周瑜、郭子儀之通變，而人不得以爲誕；以正爲奇，以奇爲正，則孫武、趙奢、孫臏、田單、韓信、虞詡之參伍錯綜，隨時變化，而人莫知其所自出。
translation_en:
…his stratagems were exhausted. How could he rely on Beizhou’s strong defenses? One may read one’s father’s books, but could someone like Zhao Kuo be entrusted with command, when he glued the tuning bridges in place to play the zither and did not understand how to adapt to changing circumstances? After the defeat at Changping, Handan was nearly lost. How could he go to his death without repenting! The ominous saying, “Lesser commanders cart back corpses,” surely refers to someone like Kuo. Ancient methods may be followed, but could someone like Fang Guan be entrusted with responsibility, when he promoted frivolous men and made grand claims that did not fit the circumstances? In the rout at Chentaoxie, his ox-drawn carts were reduced to ashes; it was only to be expected that he should suffer defeat and fail to hold out. Guan apparently did not understand the method of the three hundred war chariots [?]. In cases like these, is the fault with the methods? The fault lies with those who do not know how to employ them. How crucial it is that troops can be employed according to established methods, yet must not be fettered by them!

Thus it is said: “There are no more than five notes, yet their variations cannot all be heard; there are no more than five colors, yet their variations cannot all be seen. In warfare there are only the unorthodox and the orthodox, yet their variations cannot be exhausted. The unorthodox and the orthodox generate one another in turn, like a ring without an endpoint.” This is what is called “employing troops with divine skill.” Thus, when orthodox action is appropriate, act orthodoxly: the vigilant defensive conduct of Wang Jian, Cheng Bushi, and Li Guangbi could not be dismissed as rigid. When unorthodox action is appropriate, act unorthodoxly: the adaptability of Li Guang, Zhou Yu, and Guo Ziyi could not be dismissed as reckless. As for making the orthodox unorthodox and the unorthodox orthodox, Sun Wu, Zhao She, Sun Bin, Tian Dan, Han Xin, and Yu Xu interwove and recombined their methods, adapting to circumstances so that no one could discern the source of their moves…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
至於趙括馬謖房琯之徒則奇正兩失而
爲兵家之所忌矣雖然此自兵家者流言
之也執事猶欲博覽載籍而定其準焉不
尤有進於是者乎是故孔子大聖人也而
其言曰我戰則克若疑於迂闊而不足信
及觀其攝相而墮三都於立談之頃不啻
折枝兵萊夷於樽俎之間若斃犬豕使其
國安於泰山而敵人震駭歸田之恐後焉
斯固有不言而信不怒而威者矣其天下
===
之至神至神乎而法不足言之也至其告
子路又曰臨事而懼好謀而成夫其懼也
斯吾之所謂法也夫其成也斯吾之所謂
神也豈非萬世談兵者之凖乎管見如斯
惟執事進而敎之幸甚
第五問
苗應元
同考試官教諭錢　批　究極弊源區畫明當殆有
志於用世者
punctuated:
至於趙括、馬謖、房琯之徒，則奇正兩失，而爲兵家之所忌矣。雖然，此自兵家者流言之也。執事猶欲博覽載籍而定其準焉，不尤有進於是者乎？是故孔子，大聖人也，而其言曰：「我戰則克。」若疑於迂闊而不足信，及觀其攝相而墮三都於立談之頃，不啻折枝；兵萊夷於樽俎之間，若斃犬豕，使其國安於泰山，而敵人震駭，歸田之恐後焉。斯固有不言而信、不怒而威者矣。其天下之至神至神乎！而法不足言之也。至其告子路，又曰：「臨事而懼，好謀而成。」夫其懼也，斯吾之所謂法也；夫其成也，斯吾之所謂神也。豈非萬世談兵者之凖乎？管見如斯，惟執事進而敎之，幸甚。
第五問
苗應元
同考試官教諭錢，批：究極弊源，區畫明當，殆有志於用世者。
translation_en:
As for men such as Zhao Kuo, Ma Su, and Fang Guan, they failed in both unconventional and conventional warfare and thus became cautionary examples for military strategists. Yet this is merely to speak from the standpoint of military specialists. You, sir, wish to survey the written records broadly and establish a standard. Is there not something that advances still further than this?
Confucius was a great sage, and he said: “If I fought, I would prevail.” One might suspect this of being impractical and unworthy of belief. Yet consider how, while acting as chief minister, he demolished the fortifications of the three cities in the time it takes to hold a brief conversation, as easily as breaking a branch; and how, amid the wine vessels and sacrificial stands, he used force against the Lai tribesmen as though killing dogs and swine. He made his state as secure as Mount Tai, while his enemies trembled in alarm, fearing they would be too late in returning its lands. Here indeed was someone trusted without speaking and commanding awe without anger. Was this not the utmost, the utmost in wondrous efficacy under Heaven? Mere methods are inadequate to describe it.
Yet when instructing Zilu, he also said: “One who approaches an undertaking with apprehension, who delights in planning and brings it to completion.” His apprehension is precisely what I call method; his accomplishment is precisely what I call wondrous efficacy. Is this not a standard for all who discuss warfare through the ages? Such is my narrow understanding. I would be most grateful if you, sir, would offer further instruction.
Fifth Question
Miao Yingyuan
Comment by Associate Examiner Qian, Instructor: He thoroughly probes the sources of the abuses, and his proposed measures are clear and appropriate. He appears to be someone intent on putting his abilities to use in public service.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭劉　批〔論救弊八條切中民情物〕
〔理鑿鑿可行末復歸重守令得人誠根極之論〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔一方利弊斟酌有條子〕
〔其識時務者與〕
天下之患最不可爲者莫大乎狃於故習
而其實有不測之憂夏時憫事者起而欲
更之則人情溺于故習之安而不吾信坐
視而不爲之所將必至于大壞極敝而不
可支必如何而後可是在利之而已矣夫
===
聖人立法何甞不欲爲天下利哉利之失
也必趨於弊雖聖人不容爲其後者計也
故欲興天下之利者必求其弊之所自起
蓋弊袪而利行乎其中矣欲革天下之弊
者必究其法之所從失蓋法立而弊自無
所容其間矣立法以補弊袪弊以興利是
故有改置之名而無更革之實何患于習
故者之不吾信而大壞極敝之不可支乎
執事發策終篇而以東土之時事問玆固
punctuated:
考試官教諭劉，批〔論救弊八條，切中民情物〕〔理，鑿鑿可行，末復歸重守令得人，誠根極之論。〕

考試官教諭胡，批〔一方利弊，斟酌有條，子〕〔其識時務者與！〕

天下之患，最不可爲者，莫大乎狃於故習，而其實有不測之憂。夏時憫事者起而欲更之，則人情溺于故習之安，而不吾信；坐視而不爲之，所將必至于大壞極敝而不可支。必如何而後可？是在利之而已矣。夫聖人立法，何甞不欲爲天下利哉？利之失也，必趨於弊，雖聖人不容爲其後者計也。故欲興天下之利者，必求其弊之所自起，蓋弊袪而利行乎其中矣；欲革天下之弊者，必究其法之所從失，蓋法立而弊自無所容其間矣。立法以補弊，袪弊以興利，是故有改置之名，而無更革之實。何患于習故者之不吾信，而大壞極敝之不可支乎？執事發策終篇，而以東土之時事問，玆固
translation_en:
Examiner Liu, an Instructor, comments: 〔The eight measures proposed for remedying abuses accord closely with the people's feelings and the principles governing affairs.〕〔They are demonstrably practicable. At the end, the argument again places chief importance on securing suitable men as prefects and county magistrates: this is truly a discussion that reaches the very root.〕

Examiner Hu, an Instructor, comments: 〔The benefits and abuses of a region are weighed in an orderly fashion. You〕〔must surely be someone who understands the affairs of the time!〕

Among the troubles of the realm, none is harder to address than habituation to established practices that in fact harbor unforeseeable dangers. In summer [?], when someone concerned about affairs steps forward seeking to change them, people are so immersed in the comfort of familiar practices that they do not trust us. Yet if we sit watching and do nothing, matters will inevitably reach a state of utter collapse and extreme deterioration that cannot be sustained. What, then, must be done? It lies simply in bringing benefit to the people. When the sages established laws, did they ever fail to wish to benefit the realm? When beneficial arrangements go awry, they inevitably tend toward abuse; even the sages cannot plan for all who come after them. Thus, anyone wishing to promote the realm's benefits must seek out the origins of its abuses: once the abuses are removed, benefits will flow within the arrangements. Anyone wishing to eliminate the realm's abuses must investigate how its laws went astray: once the laws are established, abuses will themselves have no room to remain. Establish laws to remedy abuses, and remove abuses to promote benefits. In this way there is change in name, without fundamental alteration in substance. Why, then, fear that those accustomed to old ways will not trust us, or that utter collapse and extreme deterioration will become impossible to sustain?

At the conclusion of your policy questions, you ask about current affairs in the eastern region. This surely …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
與民同患之盛心而亦患之願爲執事者
告也山東古齊魯宋衛之墟太公之所培
也周公之所勸也孔子之所淑也微仲康
叔之所治也平原沃壤延袤千里持戟百
萬號得十二其富强之甲天下夫人而知
之也重禮教崇信義至漢高之興猶嘆其
爲守禮義之國而不忍屠之以兵其醇厚
之甲天下夫人而知之也
明興以來
===
太祖
成祖之保綏敎化
列聖之隨時培植加以我
皇上之加惠元元則其休養生息惇龎篤厚宜
益倍於曩時何乃逋負未輸賦役不均田
野多蕪賑荒無策軍伍缺乏驛傳罷敝民
生之困窮極矣以是而稱于天下曰富强
其將能乎寇盜乘機竊發獄訟株連不解
風俗之薄惡甚矣以是而稱于天下曰醇
punctuated:
與民同患之盛心，而亦患之願爲執事者告也。山東，古齊魯宋衛之墟，太公之所培也，周公之所勸也，孔子之所淑也，微仲、康叔之所治也。平原沃壤，延袤千里，持戟百萬，號得十二，其富强之甲天下，夫人而知之也。重禮教，崇信義，至漢高之興，猶嘆其爲守禮義之國，而不忍屠之以兵，其醇厚之甲天下，夫人而知之也。
明興以來，太祖、成祖之保綏敎化，列聖之隨時培植，加以我皇上之加惠元元，則其休養生息、惇龎篤厚，宜益倍於曩時。何乃逋負未輸，賦役不均，田野多蕪，賑荒無策，軍伍缺乏，驛傳罷敝，民生之困窮極矣！以是而稱于天下曰富强，其將能乎？寇盜乘機竊發，獄訟株連不解，風俗之薄惡甚矣！以是而稱于天下曰醇
translation_en:
…a generous concern that shares the people’s troubles; these are also troubles I wish to report to you, sir [?].
