Shandong occupies the former territories of Qi, Lu, Song, and Wei: lands nurtured by Taigong, encouraged by the Duke of Zhou, morally improved by Confucius, and governed by Weizhong and Kangshu. Its level plains and fertile soil extend a thousand li; its million halberd-bearing soldiers were reputed to constitute two tenths of the total [?]. Everyone knows that its wealth and strength ranked foremost in the realm. It valued ritual instruction and esteemed trustworthiness and righteousness. Even when Gaozu of Han rose to power, he still praised it as a land that upheld ritual propriety and righteousness, and could not bear to slaughter its people with his armies. Everyone knows that its integrity and generosity ranked foremost in the realm.
Since the rise of the Ming, Taizu and Chengzu have protected, pacified, and morally instructed its people; successive sage emperors have nurtured them as circumstances required; and our present Emperor has bestowed further kindness upon the common people. Their recovery and prosperity, their sincerity and generosity, ought therefore to have increased manyfold over former times. How, then, can arrears remain unpaid, taxes and labor services be unequally apportioned, so many fields lie waste, and famine relief lack a plan? Military ranks are depleted, and the postal relay service is exhausted. The people’s hardship and destitution have reached their utmost extreme! In such circumstances, can this land claim before the realm to be wealthy and strong? Bandits seize opportunities to rise; lawsuits implicate ever more people and remain unresolved. The shallowness and wickedness of popular customs have become extreme! In such circumstances, can this land claim before the realm to possess integrity…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
厚其將能乎山東密邇
畿輔緩急恃賴其困窮如此薄惡如此是不
可以不講也經生之言曰制田里薄稅斂
則富強自至謹庠序申敎化則禮義自興
是猶欲以粱肉之味療膏肓之疴鄉飲之
儀應軍旅之急其爲術不已踈乎夫有田
則有租聖人在上粟米之征其所不廢也
而山東取濟京邊視他省爲急善良畏法
者輸納恐後或責以包賠而姦猾邑有王
===
侯之尊里有公卿之富聽其積負莫敢誰
何甚者貪墨長民計取充槖而於公家之
稅漫不加意夫是而望逋負之輸不可得
也善督稅者其惟責廉吏以嚴姦猾之稽
乎至於積年之逋負量蠲帶征可也尚何
病于閭閻之凋敝也哉有身則有庸聖人
在上力役之征其所不廢也而山東定以
門丁視他省爲獨異齊民無蓋藏糟糠不
厭刻骨以應差遣而富豪家藏猗頓之資
punctuated:
厚，其將能乎？山東密邇畿輔，緩急恃賴，其困窮如此，薄惡如此，是不可以不講也。經生之言曰：「制田里，薄稅斂，則富強自至；謹庠序，申敎化，則禮義自興。」是猶欲以粱肉之味療膏肓之疴，鄉飲之儀應軍旅之急，其爲術不已踈乎？
夫有田則有租，聖人在上，粟米之征，其所不廢也。而山東取濟京邊，視他省爲急。善良畏法者，輸納恐後，或責以包賠；而姦猾，邑有王侯之尊，里有公卿之富，聽其積負，莫敢誰何。甚者，貪墨長民，計取充槖，而於公家之稅漫不加意。夫是而望逋負之輸，不可得也。善督稅者，其惟責廉吏以嚴姦猾之稽乎？至於積年之逋負，量蠲帶征可也，尚何病于閭閻之凋敝也哉？
有身則有庸，聖人在上，力役之征，其所不廢也。而山東定以門丁，視他省爲獨異。齊民無蓋藏，糟糠不厭，刻骨以應差遣；而富豪家藏猗頓之資
translation_en:
…and generous—could such a claim stand? Shandong lies close to the capital region and is relied upon in times of emergency. With its poverty so severe and its customs so corrupt, these matters cannot go unexamined. Students of the classics say: “Regulate the allocation of fields and homesteads and lighten taxation, and wealth and strength will come of themselves; attend carefully to the schools and reinforce moral instruction, and ritual propriety and righteousness will flourish of themselves.” This is like trying to cure a deep-seated illness with fine grain and meat, or to meet a military emergency with the ceremonies of the district drinking rite. Is this not an altogether ineffectual approach?
Where there is land, there is land tax. Even with a sage ruling above, levies of grain are not abolished. Yet the demands upon Shandong to supply the capital and the frontier are more urgent than those upon other provinces. Honest people who fear the law pay promptly, anxious not to fall behind; some are even held responsible for making good others’ shortfalls. Meanwhile, the unscrupulous enjoy the standing of princes and marquises in their counties and the wealth of dukes and ministers in their villages. They are allowed to accumulate arrears, and no one dares challenge them. Worse still, corrupt officials governing the people devise ways to fill their own purses while giving no thought to the public taxes. Under such circumstances, payment of the arrears cannot be expected. Surely those who supervise taxation well must charge upright officials with taking strict action against delays in payment by the unscrupulous? As for arrears accumulated over many years, it would be appropriate to remit a suitable portion and collect the remainder alongside current taxes. Why then should the impoverishment of the common people remain a cause for concern?
Where there are persons, there are labor obligations. Even with a sage ruling above, levies of labor service are not abolished. Yet Shandong assesses these obligations by the adult males in each household, a practice distinct from that of other provinces. Ordinary people have no stored reserves and cannot get their fill even of dregs and husks; they endure suffering to the bone to meet service assignments. Yet wealthy and powerful households possess fortunes like that of Yi Dun…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
田連阡陌之產惟准丁數歲編無幾甚者
捐貲納級優免無遺而於公家之調若罔
聞知夫是而求差徭之均不可得也善乎
役者其惟兼丁地以定編審之則乎至於
大家之騰謗以身肩之可也又何患于貧
窮之坐困也哉至田野之多蕪愚恐其原
不在流移之未復也夫民之趨利猶水之
走下也利之所在雖欲禁之尚不可得況
待驅之使就乎今莒沂郯費之郊磽确鹹
===
鹵其不治而亡者幾半至岡阜之區不暘
而乾一雨輙溢雖或墾之其地不可耕而
食也莫若聽其自然不強其所不欲移牛
種之給以資無力之民不惟見在者有固
志而流移者不將有歸心乎饑饉之間臻
愚謂其策專在於儲蓄之豫備也夫古者
三年耕而有一年之蓄九年耕而有三年
之蓄以三十年之通制國用周禮尚有救
荒之政今公私倉稟之藏懸磬塵甑其不
punctuated: 田連阡陌之產，惟准丁數，歲編無幾。甚者捐貲納級，優免無遺，而於公家之調若罔聞知。夫是而求差徭之均，不可得也。善乎役者，其惟兼丁地以定編審之則乎？至於大家之騰謗，以身肩之可也，又何患于貧窮之坐困也哉？至田野之多蕪，愚恐其原不在流移之未復也。夫民之趨利，猶水之走下也。利之所在，雖欲禁之，尚不可得，況待驅之使就乎？今莒、沂、郯、費之郊，磽确鹹鹵，其不治而亡者幾半。至岡阜之區，不暘而乾，一雨輙溢，雖或墾之，其地不可耕而食也。莫若聽其自然，不強其所不欲，移牛種之給，以資無力之民。不惟見在者有固志，而流移者不將有歸心乎？饑饉之間臻，愚謂其策專在於儲蓄之豫備也。夫古者三年耕而有一年之蓄，九年耕而有三年之蓄，以三十年之通制國用，《周禮》尚有救荒之政。今公私倉稟之藏，懸磬塵甑，其不
translation_en:
…and estates whose fields stretch across paths running north–south and east–west, yet their annual service assessments, based solely on the number of adult males, are negligible. Some go further, contributing money to purchase rank and obtaining every available preferential exemption, while behaving as though they had never heard of the government's requisitions. Under such circumstances, equitable allocation of labor service is impossible. Surely those skilled in administering labor service [?] should take both adult males and land into account in establishing the rules for registration and assessment? As for the slanders raised by great households, officials can shoulder these themselves. Why then fear that the poor will remain trapped in distress?

As for the extensive abandonment of farmland, I humbly fear that its underlying cause is not the failure of displaced people to return. People pursue advantage just as water flows downward. Where advantage lies, even attempts to restrain them cannot succeed; why should they need to be driven toward it? Now, in the countryside around Ju, Yi, Tan, and Fei, the soil is stony, barren, and saline; nearly half have left their land uncultivated and fled [?]. As for the hilly districts, they dry out even without sunshine, yet a single rainfall brings flooding. Even if reclaimed, such land cannot sustain people through cultivation. It would be better to let people follow their own inclinations, without forcing them to do what they do not wish, and redirect the allocations of oxen and seed to assist those who lack the means. Would this not both strengthen the resolve of those still resident to remain and inspire the displaced to return?

As for famines that occur from time to time, I humbly maintain that the remedy lies entirely in building up reserves beforehand. In antiquity, three years of cultivation produced one year's reserves, and nine years of cultivation produced three years' reserves. State expenditure was regulated by reckoning across thirty years; even so, the Rites of Zhou provided measures for famine relief. Today, public and private granaries are as bare as a suspended chime-stone, and cooking vessels gather dust. Those who do not …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
耕而食者有幾至勤動之民朝營而暮食
暮營而朝食設一穀不收其亡可立而待
也莫若先為區畫責守令以積穀當無事
之時而豫為有事之計不惟豐年不至於
傷農而凶年不將多所全活乎至於軍伍
也者為
國家之手足而慎固其藩維者也方其無事
坐享糧餉之利暨其有事則出性命以衛
民其立法非不善也自夫軍人無分戶之
===
禁而軍籍至不可稽軍籍不可稽數易之
後而軍丁遂不可攝春秋二班起解入衛
者徒取空籍而領班武弁降級盡矣茲欲
清之必責專城官吏考冊籍于既往清查
一定禁分戶于將來而又假衛所以防閑
之權時訓練以寓優恤之政然後軍伍可
得而實也驛傳也者為
國家之血氣而聯屬其元氣者也其解自江
南者則謂之糧僉審自傜役者則謂之土
punctuated:
耕而食者有幾？至勤動之民，朝營而暮食，暮營而朝食，設一穀不收，其亡可立而待也。莫若先為區畫，責守令以積穀，當無事之時而豫為有事之計，不惟豐年不至於傷農，而凶年不將多所全活乎？
至於軍伍也者，為國家之手足，而慎固其藩維者也。方其無事，坐享糧餉之利；暨其有事，則出性命以衛民，其立法非不善也。自夫軍人無分戶之禁，而軍籍至不可稽；軍籍不可稽，數易之後，而軍丁遂不可攝。春秋二班起解入衛者，徒取空籍，而領班武弁降級盡矣。茲欲清之，必責專城官吏考冊籍于既往，清查一定，禁分戶于將來，而又假衛所以防閑之權，時訓練以寓優恤之政，然後軍伍可得而實也。
驛傳也者，為國家之血氣，而聯屬其元氣者也。其解自江南者，則謂之糧僉；審自傜役者，則謂之土
translation_en:
… how many are there who eat without farming? As for the hardworking common people, they labor in the morning to eat that evening, and labor in the evening to eat the next morning. Should a single grain harvest fail, their destruction would follow at once. Nothing would be better than to make arrangements beforehand and charge prefects and magistrates with accumulating grain, preparing for troubled times while all is peaceful. Would this not both prevent abundant harvests from harming farmers and preserve many lives in years of dearth?
As for the military ranks, they are the state's hands and feet, securing its protective defenses. In peaceful times, soldiers enjoy provisions and pay; when trouble comes, they risk their lives to defend the people. The laws establishing this system were certainly well conceived. But since soldiers have not been prohibited from dividing their households, military registers have become impossible to verify. After repeated changes to these unverifiable registers, the men liable for military service can no longer be mustered. For the two contingents dispatched in spring and autumn to perform guard duty, only empty registers are submitted, and the military officers commanding them have all suffered demotion. To rectify this now, the officials responsible for each jurisdiction must be required to examine the earlier registers, complete a definitive investigation, and prohibit household division in future. The guards and battalions must also be granted authority to enforce these restrictions, while periodic training should incorporate measures for the soldiers' generous treatment and relief. Only then can the military ranks actually be filled.
As for the postal relay service, it is the state's blood and vital breath, connecting and sustaining its primal vitality. Those dispatched from Jiangnan are called grain-service assignees (liangqian) [?]; those selected through corvée assessment are called local …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
民共待行旅非不優也自夫倭夷爲梗江
南之馬價不輸而糧僉困糧僉不足以支
乘傳專取給於土著而土民困舳艫絡繹
假勢濟私者歲無虛日而河津告病哀痛
極矣茲欲應之必嚴催額設之馬價以濟
土民之急經理州縣之協濟以蘇夫役之
需而又使乾沒無所容其奸勢要不得攙
其利然後供億可得而繼也自古稱弭盗
者其道不同要皆隨時設法不相襲智若
===
山東之盗又不可以常理律之歲凶無賴
相率而求騁于弓馬之間頋少須臾無死
猶可說也至年既順成亦有乘機竊發者
矣事育不足不忍坐以待斃求生於死猶
可說也至富家大室亦有主謀射利者矣
指大幾股要非小失也雖守土者嘗緝捕
肆出而所遣非人或以滋擾誠有如執事
所慮者茲欲籌之惟脩保甲之法時巡邏
之令而已不幸不止又申緝捕者以波及
punctuated:
民共待行旅，非不優也。自夫倭夷爲梗，江南之馬價不輸，而糧僉困；糧僉不足以支乘傳，專取給於土著，而土民困。舳艫絡繹，假勢濟私者歲無虛日，而河津告病，哀痛極矣。茲欲應之，必嚴催額設之馬價，以濟土民之急；經理州縣之協濟，以蘇夫役之需。而又使乾沒無所容其奸，勢要不得攙其利，然後供億可得而繼也。
自古稱弭盗者，其道不同，要皆隨時設法，不相襲智。若山東之盗，又不可以常理律之。歲凶，無賴相率而求騁于弓馬之間，頋少須臾無死，猶可說也；至年既順成，亦有乘機竊發者矣。事育不足，不忍坐以待斃，求生於死，猶可說也；至富家大室，亦有主謀射利者矣。指大幾股，要非小失也。雖守土者嘗緝捕肆出，而所遣非人，或以滋擾，誠有如執事所慮者。茲欲籌之，惟脩保甲之法、時巡邏之令而已。不幸不止，又申緝捕者以波及
translation_en:
…the commoners jointly provide for travelers; these arrangements are by no means ungenerous. Since the Japanese marauders began causing trouble, however, the horse funds from Jiangnan have not been remitted, leaving those assigned to relay service through the grain levy in difficulty. When these grain-levy assignments cannot support travel by the relay system, supplies are drawn exclusively from local residents, and the local commoners suffer. Boats follow one another in an unbroken stream; throughout the year, not a day passes without someone exploiting influence for private ends. The river crossings are consequently overwhelmed: the suffering is extreme. To address this, we must rigorously press for payment of the prescribed horse funds to relieve the local people's urgent needs, and coordinate mutual assistance among the subprefectures and counties to ease the demands upon laborers. We must also leave embezzlers no opportunity for fraud and prevent powerful men from taking a share of the profits. Only then can supplies be maintained.
Since antiquity, those renowned for suppressing banditry have used different methods, but all have devised measures suited to their times rather than merely borrowing their predecessors' ingenuity. Banditry in Shandong, moreover, cannot be judged by ordinary standards. When the harvest fails, men without a livelihood band together and seek their fortunes with bows and horses, hoping only to stave off death a little longer: this can still be explained. Yet even when the harvest is good, some seize an opportunity to rise in rebellion. When people lack the means to support their parents and children, cannot bear to sit awaiting death, and seek survival amid mortal peril, this too can be explained. Yet even wealthy and substantial households mastermind such activities for profit. The fingers are nearly as large as the thighs [?]; this is certainly no minor failing. Although the officials responsible for these territories have repeatedly sent men out far and wide to apprehend bandits, their agents are unsuitable and sometimes only cause further disturbances—just as you have feared. To devise a remedy, we need only put the baojia system of mutual household responsibility in order and enforce regular patrols. If, unfortunately, the trouble does not cease, we must further admonish those charged with apprehending bandits concerning their implication of…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
平民之法焉則禦盜而爲盜者不將息乎
至若無訟之化雖孔子猶以爲難而世之
以折獄名者不相沿衛山東之訟又未必
皆屈而求伸者也愚者求以氣勝而不虞
其敗每摭拾重事以誣人卒反坐而自斃
頑者專事濟私而不求聽理恒施一網之
計以規利利厭而其入已不可復勾矣殺
人以詞其漸不可長也守土者或少乏明
決即墮計中適以相搆誠有如執事所慮
===
者茲欲息之惟嚴起滅之條重刁訐之罰
而已不幸不止又限理冤者以陳情立詞
之制焉則自誣以誣人者不少殺乎凡此
皆就事議事之法也所以袪弊而興利者
也至行法以惠民是在慎守令之選而已
是故有京兆之兒寬則大家牛車小家擔
負而不憂于逋負之不輸有全椒之劉平
則增貲就賦減年從役而不憂于傜役之
不均有南陽之杜詩則脩治陂池之政舉
punctuated:
平民之法焉，則禦盜而爲盜者不將息乎？至若無訟之化，雖孔子猶以爲難，而世之以折獄名者不相沿衛。山東之訟，又未必皆屈而求伸者也。愚者求以氣勝，而不虞其敗，每摭拾重事以誣人，卒反坐而自斃；頑者專事濟私，而不求聽理，恒施一網之計以規利，利厭而其入已不可復勾矣。殺人以詞，其漸不可長也。守土者或少乏明決，即墮計中，適以相搆，誠有如執事所慮者。茲欲息之，惟嚴起滅之條，重刁訐之罰而已。不幸不止，又限理冤者以陳情立詞之制焉，則自誣以誣人者不少殺乎？凡此皆就事議事之法也，所以袪弊而興利者也。至行法以惠民，是在慎守令之選而已。
是故有京兆之兒寬，則大家牛車，小家擔負，而不憂于逋負之不輸；有全椒之劉平，則增貲就賦，減年從役，而不憂于傜役之不均；有南陽之杜詩，則脩治陂池之政舉
translation_en:
…the law against implicating ordinary people; would those who become bandits while suppressing banditry not then cease? As for transforming the people so that litigation disappears, even Confucius considered this difficult, while those renowned in the world for deciding lawsuits do not follow and uphold one another [?]. Nor are all those bringing lawsuits in Shandong necessarily people seeking redress for wrongs. The foolish seek victory through sheer aggressiveness, without anticipating defeat. They repeatedly seize upon serious matters to accuse others falsely, only to incur the penalties for those accusations themselves and bring about their own destruction. The obstinate devote themselves solely to private ends and do not seek a hearing on the merits. They constantly employ a scheme of casting a single net [?] to obtain profit; once their appetite for profit is satisfied, those already drawn into it can no longer be retrieved [?]. Killing people through accusations is a tendency that must not be allowed to grow. If the officials responsible for a locality lack even a little discernment and decisiveness, they fall into these schemes and merely help people incriminate one another. Matters are indeed as you fear, sir. To put a stop to this, we need only enforce strictly the provisions governing the initiation and dismissal of charges and increase the penalties for malicious accusations. If, unfortunately, this does not stop it, further constrain those seeking redress through rules governing statements of circumstances and the formulation of complaints. Would those who falsely incriminate themselves in order to accuse others not then diminish somewhat? These are all methods of addressing each matter on its own terms, means of removing abuses and promoting benefits. As for implementing the law to benefit the people, this depends simply on carefully selecting prefects and magistrates.
Thus, with someone like Ni Kuan of Jingzhao, wealthy households transport their payments by ox cart and poorer households carry theirs on shoulder poles, so there is no concern that arrears will remain unpaid. With someone like Liu Ping of Quanjiao, people increase their declared wealth to pay taxes and reduce their stated ages to perform labor service, so there is no concern that labor obligations will be unevenly distributed. With someone like Du Shi of Nanyang, measures for repairing embankments and reservoirs are implemented…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
而草萊辟有青州之富瓈則多方活濟之
策行而流移賑有龔遂之治渤海則帶牛
佩犢之俗變而盜賊消有仇香之長蒲亭
則鷹鸇鸞鳳之辨明而訟獄清矣推而至
于軍伍之實驛傳之供固長民之餘事也
夫是則禮義富強之俗可追而今之山東
何媿於古昔之山東也哉嗚呼爲地擇人
是在秉鈞者慎之而已
punctuated: 而草萊辟；有青州之富瓈，則多方活濟之策行，而流移賑；有龔遂之治渤海，則帶牛佩犢之俗變，而盜賊消；有仇香之長蒲亭，則鷹鸇鸞鳳之辨明，而訟獄清矣。推而至于軍伍之實、驛傳之供，固長民之餘事也。夫是則禮義富強之俗可追，而今之山東何媿於古昔之山東也哉！嗚呼！爲地擇人，是在秉鈞者慎之而已。
translation_en: …and the uncultivated land is opened to farming. With a man like Fu Li 富瓈 [?; apparently Fu Bi 富弼] in Qingzhou, diverse measures to preserve lives and provide relief are implemented, and displaced people receive aid. With a man like Gong Sui governing Bohai, customs are transformed so that people ‘wear oxen at their belts and carry calves at their sides’—exchanging weapons for livestock—and banditry disappears. With a man like Qiu Xiang heading Puting, the distinction between hawks and falcons and luan birds and phoenixes is made clear—between predatory severity and benevolent rule—and litigation and criminal cases are cleared. Extending these achievements to filling the military ranks and provisioning the postal relay service is surely but a subsidiary task for those who govern the people. Thus, customs marked by ritual propriety and righteousness, prosperity and strength can be restored. Why, then, should today’s Shandong feel any shame before the Shandong of antiquity? Ah! Selecting the right men for each locality requires only that those who hold the reins of government exercise care.

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
嘉靖甲子秋八月天下復當
鄉試士寔御史監臨之乃七
月始以山東代者
請於是御史楊〔標〕祗
命馳往至則恭詣
泰沂東海稽首祝
===
聖主萬萬壽已乃稽綜責飭視昔
益虔慎〔田〕偕諸甄官窮日夜
之力掄閱品敘若睹職貢才
物雜陳陟武庫兵戟森列瀼
瀼乎盛也哉既竣事〔田〕宜申
言于簡末聞之天將有意於
斯人欲其久安長治則必輔
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄後序

嘉靖甲子秋八月，天下復當鄉試士，寔御史監臨之。乃七月始以山東代者請，於是御史楊〔標〕祗命馳往。至則恭詣泰沂東海，稽首祝聖主萬萬壽。已乃稽綜責飭，視昔益虔慎。〔田〕偕諸甄官，窮日夜之力，掄閱品敘，若睹職貢，才物雜陳；陟武庫，兵戟森列。瀼瀼乎盛也哉！既竣事，〔田〕宜申言于簡末。聞之，天將有意於斯人，欲其久安長治，則必輔
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

In autumn, in the eighth month of the jiazi year of the Jiajing reign [1564], it was once again time throughout the realm to examine scholars in the Provincial Examination, with censors serving as Supervising Officials. Only in the seventh month was a request made for a replacement for Shandong [?]. Accordingly, Censor Yang〔Biao〕 respectfully obeyed the command and hastened there. Upon arriving, he reverently visited the sacred sites of Tai, Yi, and the Eastern Sea, bowed his head to the ground, and prayed that the sagely sovereign might enjoy countless years of longevity. He then inspected and coordinated affairs, held those responsible to account, and issued admonitions, exercising even greater reverence and caution than before. I, 〔Tian〕, together with the examining officials, worked to the utmost day and night, scrutinizing, selecting, grading, and ranking the papers. It was like seeing the tribute offerings, with worthy talents and goods displayed in profusion, or entering an arsenal, with weapons and halberds arrayed in imposing ranks. How abundant and flourishing it all was!

Now that the work is complete, I, 〔Tian〕, ought to add some words at the end of this volume. I have heard that when Heaven intends to care for these people and desires lasting peace and enduring good government for them, it must assist…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
有道之
國使其基祚順綿奠世於康壽
臻雍熙太和極盛之會尤必
篤生
聖主歷年有永俾之馭世滋久德
澤寖深而後有以長育賢俊
保合黎庶培
===
國脉綴民心而久天下之勢堅
完固密爲不可拔易曰聖人
久於其道而天下化成此之
謂也天下之生久矣唐虞之
際聖聖相紹治之極也由玆
則周矣周之盛也文王秉純
一之德壽考作人雖中林野
punctuated:
有道之國，使其基祚順綿，奠世於康壽，臻雍熙太和極盛之會，尤必篤生聖主，歷年有永，俾之馭世滋久，德澤寖深，而後有以長育賢俊，保合黎庶，培國脉，綴民心，而久天下之勢，堅完固密，爲不可拔。《易》曰：「聖人久於其道，而天下化成。」此之謂也。
天下之生久矣。唐虞之際，聖聖相紹，治之極也。由玆則周矣。周之盛也，文王秉純一之德，壽考作人，雖中林野
translation_en:
…a state that possesses the Way, causing its dynastic foundations and blessings to endure [?], settling the age in well-being and longevity, and bringing it to the utmost flourishing of concord, prosperity, and great harmony. Above all, Heaven must bring forth a sage ruler and grant him many years, so that the longer he governs the world, the more deeply his beneficence penetrates. Only then can he nurture the worthy and talented, preserve and unite the common people, strengthen the state’s vital foundations, bind the people’s hearts together, and make the realm’s order endure—strong, intact, secure, and closely knit, so that it cannot be uprooted. The Book of Changes says: “The sage endures in his Way, and the world is transformed and brought to perfection.” This is what it means.
Human life under Heaven has endured for a long time. In the age of Tang and Yu, sage succeeded sage: this was the pinnacle of good government. After these came the Zhou. When the Zhou flourished, King Wen held fast to virtue that was pure and undivided; he lived to a great age and cultivated men of talent, even in the forests and wilds …

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
大旨爲公侯腹心承以武王
鎬京辟雍之化濬祥而嗣徽
成王繼之吉士惟所使以能
包桑鞏萇纏延固結而不可
解故煇赫㦯明歷世愈昌麗
浹俶祚垂八百載靈長之運
豈偶然哉洪惟我
===
二祖仁厚肇基統一丞夏
列聖丕承累洽重熙我
皇上天縱神聖嗣大
握符應五百年之期撫中興之運
明倫盡制
敬一敷極雍容垂衣稽古禮文
之事彬彬備具三長二□□□
punctuated: 大旨爲公侯腹心，承以武王鎬京辟雍之化，濬祥而嗣徽。成王繼之，吉士惟所使，以能包桑鞏萇，纏延固結而不可解。故煇赫㦯明，歷世愈昌，麗浹俶祚，垂八百載靈長之運，豈偶然哉？洪惟我二祖仁厚肇基，統一丞夏；列聖丕承，累洽重熙。我皇上天縱神聖，嗣大握符，應五百年之期，撫中興之運，明倫盡制，敬一敷極，雍容垂衣。稽古禮文之事，彬彬備具，三長二□□□
translation_en:
…became trusted confidants of dukes and lords [the opening 大旨 is unclear]. King Wu carried this forward through the civilizing influence of the Biyong academy at Haojing, deepening the auspicious legacy and continuing its excellence. King Cheng succeeded him, employing worthy men alone. Thus the foundations were secured like something bound to a clump of mulberry trees [?], entwined and firmly joined beyond unraveling. Hence its splendor shone brightly [?], growing more flourishing with each generation. Its founding blessings spread widely [?], extending its enduring, auspicious destiny for eight hundred years. Could this have happened by chance?

We reverently reflect that our Two Founders established the foundations through benevolence and generosity and unified the Chinese realm [丞夏, doubtful]. Successive sage sovereigns grandly carried on their work, bringing repeated peace and accumulating prosperity. Our emperor, endowed by Heaven with divine sagacity, has inherited the great sovereignty and holds the token of authority. He answers the appointed occasion that comes once in five hundred years and presides over an age of restoration. He clarifies human relationships and fully establishes their regulations; through reverent devotion to unity, he sets forth the supreme standard. With serene dignity, he lets his robes hang down, governing effortlessly. Matters of ritual and cultural observance modeled on antiquity are elegantly and fully provided for. The three strengths and two … [三長二□□□, unclear; text breaks off]

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
摩教化之所沾濡含聲鼓喙
應候奮踴矧膠序之彥乎濯
沐於
德澤者極于海隅日出太和元
氣絪縕磅礴融結而成治矧
山東密邇
皇畿
===
勳華所被視他藩獨先者乎宜
其薫蒸衍瀲洩而爲賢秀瀁
瀁乎若是其盛也山東當山
河之界而擅海岱之勝精靈
所鍾爲聖爲賢爲瑰瑋卓犖
之材代不乏人田嘗繙據上
下數千年間少皐之所都虞
punctuated:
摩，教化之所沾濡，含聲鼓喙，應候奮踴，矧膠序之彥乎！濯沐於德澤者，極于海隅日出，太和元氣絪縕磅礴，融結而成治，矧山東密邇皇畿，勳華所被，視他藩獨先者乎！宜其薫蒸衍瀲，洩而爲賢秀，瀁瀁乎若是其盛也。
山東當山河之界，而擅海岱之勝，精靈所鍾，爲聖爲賢，爲瑰瑋卓犖之材，代不乏人。田嘗繙據上下數千年間，少皐之所都，虞
translation_en:
…[?] Wherever moral instruction has spread its influence, even creatures endowed with voices and beating beaks leap up in response to the season; how much more so the outstanding men of the schools! Those bathed in the blessings of imperial virtue extend to the shores where the sun rises. The primal breath of supreme harmony mingles and spreads in vast abundance, coalescing to bring about good government. How much more must this hold for Shandong, so close to the imperial metropolitan region, which receives the glory of Yao and Shun before the other provinces! It is fitting that this pervasive, overflowing influence should issue in worthy and outstanding men, flourishing in such abundance.
Shandong lies where mountains and rivers meet and commands the scenic excellence of the sea and Mount Tai. Its concentrated spiritual essences produce sages, worthies, and men of extraordinary and outstanding talent; no age has lacked them. I, Tian, have examined textual evidence [?] spanning several thousand years: the place where Shaohao established his capital, and Yu…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
舜之所跡維時風氣鬱焉始
啓及觀明堂之址歷齊魯之
區想見周公所以制禮樂興
太平者其心英之流暢率在
於斯而賜履以表東海者非
太公耶則渭焉曰兹所謂有
其地而人足以當之也乎既
===
覽孔書望蒙龜鳧嶧諸山涉
洙泗之流扣三遷之地誦司
馬遷所稱觀廟堂車服禮器
低回不能去者斯則有其人
矣而所遇之時不偶乃若瑯
邪孫山平原蘭陵多諸侯盟
會卿士大夫聘問之故域與
punctuated: 舜之所跡，維時風氣鬱焉始啓。及觀明堂之址，歷齊魯之區，想見周公所以制禮樂、興太平者，其心英之流暢率在於斯。而賜履以表東海者，非太公耶？則渭焉曰：「兹所謂有其地而人足以當之也乎？」既覽孔書，望蒙龜鳧嶧諸山，涉洙泗之流，扣三遷之地，誦司馬遷所稱觀廟堂車服禮器、低回不能去者，斯則有其人矣，而所遇之時不偶。乃若瑯邪、孫山、平原、蘭陵，多諸侯盟會、卿士大夫聘問之故域，與
translation_en: …where Shun left his traces: at that time, the gathered vital influences first began to unfold. On viewing the site of the Hall of Light and traveling through the regions of Qi and Lu, one can imagine how the Duke of Zhou established rites and music and brought about great peace: the finest impulses of his heart flowed forth chiefly here. And was it not the Grand Duke who was granted territory extending to the East Sea? Then one says [?]: “Is this what is meant by a land whose people are worthy of it?” Having read the writings of Confucius, gazed upon the mountains Meng, Gui, Fu, and Yi, crossed the waters of the Zhu and Si, visited the places associated with the three moves of Mencius’s mother, and recited Sima Qian’s account of viewing the temple halls, carriages, robes, and ritual vessels, lingering and unable to leave, one sees that here indeed was such a man, yet the times he encountered were unfavorable. As for Langye, Sunshan [?], Pingyuan, and Lanling, they contain many former sites of covenant assemblies among the feudal lords and diplomatic visits by ministers and grandees, together with…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
夫縉紳學士授業談經陋巷
牖甕浴沂耕魯彈琴絃誦之
所陳跡具在則又未甞不嘆
乎地靈之不盡洩於人人之
或格乎時也孔子大聖人也
爲魯相僅三月孟軻氏不得
任齊之卿相甚哉時之難遘
===
也
皇上纘俊崇儒疇咨海內舉其茂
異使積行之君子不壅於上
聞於穆淳化融液而下究邇
者
敕所司揚獎廉靖汰除殘墨雖虞
周熙皞之景莫或過焉今多
punctuated:
夫縉紳學士授業談經、陋巷牖甕、浴沂耕魯、彈琴絃誦之所，陳跡具在，則又未甞不嘆乎地靈之不盡洩於人、人之或格乎時也。孔子大聖人也，爲魯相僅三月；孟軻氏不得任齊之卿相。甚哉，時之難遘也！
皇上纘俊崇儒，疇咨海內，舉其茂異，使積行之君子不壅於上聞。於穆淳化，融液而下究。邇者，敕所司揚獎廉靖，汰除殘墨，雖虞周熙皞之景，莫或過焉。今多
translation_en:
…those places where gentlemen and scholars taught and discussed the classics, lived in humble lanes with broken jars for windows, bathed in the Yi River and tilled the fields of Lu, played the qin and recited to strings: the traces of the past are all still there. One cannot but lament that the spiritual potency of the land does not find full expression in its people, and that people are sometimes thwarted by their times. Confucius was a great sage, yet served as chief minister of Lu for only three months; Meng Ke could not obtain appointment as a minister or chief minister of Qi. How difficult it is to encounter a favorable age!
Our emperor carries forward the illustrious legacy [?] and honors Confucian learning. He seeks counsel throughout the realm and raises up its outstanding men, ensuring that gentlemen of cultivated conduct are not prevented from becoming known to the throne. Glorious is his pure transforming influence, spreading and penetrating down to all below. Recently, he commanded the responsible officials to commend and encourage the incorruptible and the composed, and to dismiss the cruel and corrupt. Even the radiant harmony of the ages of Yu and Zhou could not surpass this. Now the many…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
士裒然出以文錄於有司矣
孔孟之所不可得者旣躬遘
其盛行將籍
天府奏
大廷之對而服官于中外則何以
哉居則曰吾學孔孟之所學
志周呂之所志也夫功業道
德烏可岐而二之處則爲孔
孟出則爲周呂獨非盡地之
人與被遘
熙時而不思奮山川炳靈而無
以副之生聖賢之鄉而猶未
免爲鄉人斯三者耻也𤰞願
多士以孔孟之道德出之爲
punctuated: 士裒然出，以文錄於有司矣。孔孟之所不可得者，旣躬遘其盛，行將籍天府，奏大廷之對，而服官于中外，則何以哉？居則曰：「吾學孔孟之所學，志周呂之所志也。」夫功業道德，烏可岐而二之？處則爲孔孟，出則爲周呂，獨非盡地之人與？被遘熙時而不思奮，山川炳靈而無以副之，生聖賢之鄉而猶未免爲鄉人，斯三者耻也。𤰞願多士以孔孟之道德，出之爲
translation_en:
…the scholars have come forth in great numbers and have been selected by the responsible officials on the strength of their writings. They have personally encountered flourishing circumstances such as even Kongzi and Mengzi could not obtain. Soon their names will be entered in the imperial registers; they will present their answers in the great court and take up offices in the capital and the provinces. By what means, then, will they serve? In private life they say: “We study what Kongzi and Mengzi studied and aspire to what the Duke of Zhou and Lü Shang aspired to.” But how can achievements in service and moral virtue be separated into two? To be like Kongzi and Mengzi in retirement and like the Duke of Zhou and Lü Shang in office—is this not to fulfill one’s place as a human being [?]?

To encounter an age of flourishing peace [?] yet have no thought of exerting oneself; to have no means of matching the manifest spiritual potency of these mountains and rivers; to be born in the homeland of sages and worthies yet remain merely an ordinary villager: these three things are shameful. I humbly hope that you scholars will bring forth the moral virtue of Kongzi and Mengzi to make it into…

title: 嘉靖四十三年山東鄉試錄
text:
周呂之功業光輔
聖治引翊
昌明綦隆之運益絕以固綿
億萬載
國祚於無疆則是役也□與諸
執事咸獲藉手以報
聖主誠甚慶幸也維爾多士念之
哉維爾多士念之哉
浙江紹興府上虞縣儒學教
諭劉□謹序
punctuated:
周呂之功業，光輔聖治，引翊昌明綦隆之運，益絕以固，綿億萬載國祚於無疆，則是役也，□與諸執事咸獲藉手以報聖主，誠甚慶幸也。維爾多士念之哉！維爾多士念之哉！
浙江紹興府上虞縣儒學教諭劉□謹序。
translation_en:
…the achievements of Zhou and Lü, gloriously assisting the sagely government and sustaining this era of flourishing enlightenment and supreme prosperity, further strengthening and securing it [?], and perpetuating the dynasty’s fortunes without limit for countless ages. Then, through this undertaking, [illegible] and all the officials involved will have gained the means to repay our sagely sovereign—a truly great cause for rejoicing. You assembled scholars, reflect upon this! You assembled scholars, reflect upon this!
Preface respectfully composed by Liu □, Instructor in the Confucian School of Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang.
